fieldData.meta-description: Brisbane cookie bakehouse with a vegan choc chip cookie option
fieldData.description:
Brooki Bakehouse is a popular Brisbane bakery known for its big, chunky cookies, brownies and cupcakes. Most of the menu isn't vegan, but they make a vegan version of their classic choc chip cookie.

‍

I really like the texture of the vegan choc chip cookie. It's packed with chocolate chunks and tastes kind of buttery, which is impressive for a vegan cookie. The downsides are that the price is on the higher side for a single cookie, and the vegan option isn't always available. If you're making a special trip, it's worth checking with the store first.
fieldData.name: Brooki

fieldData.meta-description: Tofu gelato shop in the CBD with clearly marked vegan flavours like black sesame & coconut pandan
fieldData.description:
Sōfu is a tofu gelato shop on Edward Street in the city, and the first of its kind in Brisbane. The vegan flavours are clearly marked. When I visited, they were original, black sesame and coconut pandan. The gelato is rich and creamy.

‍

My only wish is that all the flavours were vegan, which should be quite doable for a tofu gelato shop.
fieldData.name: Sofu Gelato

fieldData.meta-description: Craft brewery in Murarrie, plus a Valley bar, with vegan pizzas, burgers, wings & milkshakes
fieldData.description:
BrewDog has two venues in Brisbane: DogTap, its brewery in Murarrie, and a bar in Fortitude Valley. I've been to both, and on my last visit I went to DogTap, which is very spacious. Both have great vegan options, including a few pizzas, a parmy, cauliflower wings, burgers and even vegan milkshakes.

‍

I went for their 2-for-1 pizza deal and tried the mushroom pizza and the eggplant parmy pizza, which worked out to about $13–14 each. They're decent woodfired pizzas. The base is slightly dense, but they were better than I expected from a brewery, and I'm happy they use vegan cheese. I also really loved the vegan milkshake; I got the Oreo flavour.
fieldData.name: BrewDog / DogTap

fieldData.meta-description: Modern Southeast Asian restaurant in Tarragindi with plenty of vegan options, priced below the meat
fieldData.description:
Oh Monk is a modern Southeast Asian restaurant in leafy Tarragindi with quite a lot of vegan options. I like that the vegan dishes are cheaper than the meat versions. For example, a tofu stir-fry is $21, while the meat stir-fries are $24–28.

‍

I tried two of the lunch specials: the green curry tofu rice bowl ($15) and the crispy cauliflower Japanese curry rice bowl ($17). Both were good value and tasted okay.
fieldData.name: Oh Monk

fieldData.address-text: The Garden Pavilion West Village TG.2, Level 2/111 Boundary St, West End QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: High-end Japanese restaurant in West Village with a vegetarian lunch set that can be made vegan
fieldData.description:
Ippin is a high-end Japanese restaurant upstairs in West Village. A full dinner here is a splurge, but the express lunch set is a great way to try it. One of the set options is the "Vegetarian Set", which comes with salad, sushi, tempura, miso eggplant, agedashi tofu and more. It tasted pretty good, and it's a lovely spot for a special lunch.

‍

Tip: The Vegetarian Set isn't vegan by default, so make sure you tell the staff you're vegan when ordering. For dinner, Ippin also has a multi-course vegetarian set menu that must be pre-ordered by email at least a day ahead; mention that you're vegan when you book.
fieldData.name: IPPIN Japanese Dining

fieldData.meta-description: Funky Indonesian restaurant & bar in the Valley with a vegan section and vegan banquet
fieldData.description:
Warisan is a funky Indonesian restaurant and bar on a side street in the Valley, with a vegan section on the menu that has quite a few options. I tried a few dishes, and my favourites were the tempeh chips and the mie goreng tek-tek. The cap chay (stir-fried vegetables), however, came in an overly salty sauce.

‍

Tip: Order the mie goreng tek-tek from the vegan section, as the regular version on the main menu comes with egg. If you're in a group, there's also a vegan banquet (minimum two people).
fieldData.name: Warisan

fieldData.meta-description: Indian restaurant opposite Musgrave Park with a dedicated vegan section of rich, high-quality currie
fieldData.description:
Kinara is an Indian restaurant in South Brisbane, right across from Musgrave Park, with a dedicated vegan section on the menu. The curries here are very good quality, and I especially love the pumpkin and the spinach curries. The only shame is that none of the naan is vegan, so pair your curry with rice instead.

‍

If you're nearby, its sister restaurant Bagicha on Melbourne Street also has a vegan section, with a British-Indian 'curry house' twist.
fieldData.name: Kinara

fieldData.meta-description: Organic health food store with a cafe section offering vegan salads, burgers & brownies
fieldData.description:
Fundies is a long-running health food and organic grocery store on Byron's main street. It's a good place to stock up on vegan snacks, plant milks and organic produce for your stay.

‍

It also has a separate garden cafe and fresh food section with vegan options like salads, burgers, brownies and more. I didn't try anything from the cafe on this trip, but it's handy if you want to grab something quick or put together a beach picnic.
fieldData.name: Fundies Organics

fieldData.address-text: Shop 5/109 Jonson St, Byron Bay NSW 2481
fieldData.meta-description: Asian grocery & gift shop with a hot food cupboard of vegan buns, spring rolls & gyoza
fieldData.description:
Red Ginger has been a Byron Bay favourite since 2002. It's part Asian grocery store, part dumpling house and part gift shop. It's a beautiful store to wander through, with handmade gifts, ceramics and teaware alongside shelves of Asian groceries.

‍

The front of the shop has a hot food cupboard with quite a few vegan options. The red bean bun and soy skin spring roll were tasty. The skin on the gyoza was a bit dry, but that's to be expected when it had been sitting in the cupboard for a while.

‍

Tip: Red Ginger also sells roast duck, pork and other meat dishes, so check the labels or ask the staff which items in the hot food cupboard are vegan. There's a second store in Bangalow (38 Byron St), a 15-minute drive inland, if you're visiting the village.
fieldData.name: Red Ginger

fieldData.meta-description: Popular organic brunch cafe with acai bowls, specialty coffee & good vegan options
fieldData.description:
Combi is one of Byron Bay's best-known brunch cafes, with an organic menu of açaí bowls, smoothies, toasts and specialty coffee. There are good vegan options across the menu, and it opens at 7am every day, so it's an easy breakfast stop before the beach.

‍

I tried my friend's loaded banana bread, which was a highlight. It was toasted with crispy edges while still soft in the middle, and loaded with vegan cream and fruit. The mocha I had, however, was a bit watery.
fieldData.name: Combi

fieldData.meta-description: Sicilian-inspired gelateria near Main Beach with plenty of clearly marked vegan flavours
fieldData.description:
A short stroll from Main Beach, Frankies is a Sicilian-inspired gelateria that churns all its gelato on site with local ingredients and no added colours or preservatives. Around 40% of the flavours are vegan, so there's always a good selection to choose from.

‍

The gelato here is creamy and delicious. I tried the matcha macadamia flavour, which had a great balance of nutty macadamia and strong matcha.

‍

Tip: Vegan flavours are marked "VGN" on the menu. You can also have your gelato in a Sicilian-style brioche bun, but brioche usually contains egg and butter, so check with the staff before ordering it. Frankies stays open late and is just a few doors from No Bones, so it's an easy second dessert stop after dinner.
fieldData.name: Frankies Gelato

fieldData.meta-description: Not-for-profit vegan cafe with a changing counter of hot & cold lunch dishes
fieldData.description:
Manna Haven is a not-for-profit vegan cafe run by the Byron Bay Seventh-day Adventist Church, and it has been feeding locals for over 20 years. It's a lunch spot with a counter of hot and cold dishes that changes regularly, so you can mix and match mains, salads and desserts. It's only open for weekday lunch, so plan around it. Eat in the indoor area or the garden, or grab your food to go.

‍

I had lunch here and tried the lasagna and the frittata. The frittata (more like a quiche) was nice and loaded with pumpkin, and the staff offered to heat it up for me. The lasagna tasted good but was a bit too salty for my taste. There's no coffee here, but there are smoothies, a house chai made on rooibos, hot chocolate and herbal teas (the banana smoothie is listed with honey, so ask for it without).
fieldData.name: Manna Haven

fieldData.meta-description: All-vegan restaurant and bar near Main Beach with share plates, cocktails & standout desserts
fieldData.description:
Just 100m from Main Beach, No Bones is Byron Bay's go-to spot for an all-vegan dinner with cocktails. The food is good quality overall, with a slightly fancy feel and smaller portions, so it's a great pick for a date night or a special occasion.

‍

In my opinion, the sweet side of the menu is even stronger than the savoury. The tiramisu is the standout, and I think it's one of the best tiramisus I've ever had. Don't leave without ordering it.

‍

On the savoury side, the carbonara has a good flavour overall, though I was expecting the 'vegan egg yolk' on top to be runny. The sticky tofu comes with a sauce that was a bit too bitter for my taste. The service, however, was amazing from start to finish.

‍

Tip: No Bones runs $20 Carbonara Mondays (all night, currently scheduled until 30 November 2026) and live jazz on the first Friday of every month. It's dinner only, so book ahead for weekends.
fieldData.name: No Bones

fieldData.meta-description: Specialty matcha cafe serving vegan-friendly pastries from Sweet and Green
fieldData.description:
Oh My Brew is a small coffee shop in South Brisbane that shares its location with the Sweet and Green bakery. This unique setup allows customers to get the matcha drinks and coffee from Oh My Brew, alongside a nice selection of fresh pastries and baked goods from Sweet and Green. They have a few outdoor seats available, making it a nice little spot to enjoy a coffee and a treat.

‍

The main draw for foodies is the ready access to vegan pastries, and baked goods, many of which are vegan-friendly. You can find everything from delightful croissants to brioche and focaccia. But the vegan options are not marked explicitly, so make sure to ask the staff to confirm which options are vegan before ordering.

‍

Oh My Brew specialises at drinks, with a special focus on matcha drinks. The ube matcha latte I tried was nice and strong, with an earthy and tasty profile. While some drinks like the Biscoff latte can be subtle in flavour, the staff is happy to customize your drink if you ask for a stronger flavour.
fieldData.name: Oh My Brew

fieldData.meta-description: Fresh and healthy bowls featuring Fable's popular shiitake mushroom meat
fieldData.description:
Fishbowl is well-known for its fresh, vibrant, and healthy bowls, and they offer some solid options for vegans by using Fable's tasty shiitake mushroom meat.

‍

In the menu, the mushroom street food box and Mush Love bowl are vegan by default and they use Fable's mushroom meat. The mushroom box is a great budget option with mushroom meat, sesame dressing, umami cashew crunch, house slaw, and a base of sushi rice. And the Mush Love Bowl is a larger meal featuring Fable meat alongside a variety of vegetables tossed in a lemon olive oil and soy sauce dressing, topped with crunchy wasabi peas.

‍

For anyone wanting an even heartier meal, you also have the option to add an extra serving of the Fable mushroom meat to any bowl.
fieldData.name: Fishbowl

fieldData.meta-description: An all-vegan bakehouse in Surfers Paradise with must-try cookies & croissants
fieldData.description:
Brought to you by the team behind the popular vegan cafe, Blendlove, this vegan bakehouse is a welcome addition to the Surfer's Paradise area. Its convenient location, just a few minutes' walk from both the Cypress Avenue tram stop and the beach, makes it a great, accessible spot for vegan foodies.

‍

The bakery cafe impresses with a wide array of freshly baked goods, with almost everything made in-house. You can expect to find soft fragrant cookies, decadent brownies, and fresh sourdough. For the perfect flaky pastry, they have also sourced delicious croissants all the way from Sydney's vegan bakery, Oh My Days.

‍

Among the standout items, the cookie dough croissant is an absolute must-try. It has the perfect combination of a crispy, flaky croissant with a rich cookie dough filling. The housemade cookies are another highlight with their soft and chewy texture that I love personally.
fieldData.name: Uni’s Bakehouse

fieldData.address-text: Shop 2/52 Merivale St, South Brisbane QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: New ramen lab by Ramen Danbo serving veganised Tonkotsu ramen bowls
fieldData.description:
Danbo Labo is a new concept restaurant in South Brisbane from the creators of Ramen Danbo. Located right next to the original shop, this "laboratory" is a restaurant with an evolving menu. And for its opening, they offer a vegan menu with ramen, gyoza and more.

‍

Drawing inspiration from Fukuoka, the birthplace of Tonkotsu ramen, the opening menu is concise. It features rich and creamy bowls like the vegan tonkotsu, vegan miso tonkotsu, and vegan negi-goma (spring onion & sesame) ramen. Each bowl is generously portioned with five slices of atsuage tofu and can be customized to your preferred spice level. The Hakata-style vegan gyoza is also a solid and delicious side dish to complement your meal.

‍

It is important to keep in mind that while the initial food menu is entirely vegan, they may not stay vegan in the future. And in the opening menu, not all drinks are vegan, namely the Calpis drink.
fieldData.name: Danbo Labo

fieldData.meta-description: Enjoy vegan pancakes 24/7 inside a medieval-themed old church
fieldData.description:
Pancake Manor offers a unique dining atmospheres in the Brisbane CBD. Housed within a beautiful old church, stepping inside feels like being transported to a medieval hall, complete with armoured knights guarding the entrance.

‍

The menu includes several vegan choices, including a veganised version of their ‘buttermilk’ pancakes. While the pancakes themselves have a decent, nostalgic flavour, their texture can be a bit crumbly. Even though vegan pancakes are available, they don't currently offer vegan substitutes for butter or cream, and you'll be charged the same price for getting less. Other vegan options available include the black forest cherry, blueberry, and lemon & sugar pancakes.

‍

Perhaps its most famous feature is that it's open 24/7, making it the go-to destination if you find yourself craving vegan pancakes at 3am.
fieldData.name: The Pancake Manor

fieldData.meta-description: Vegetarian Vietnamese spot in Inala with hearty, affordable vegan options
fieldData.description:
Tinh Lac Vietnamese Vegetarian is a hidden little gem tucked away in an alleyway at the back of Inala Plaza. This small, local eatery offers an authentic and intimate atmosphere with just four tables, making it a quiet spot for those in the know. It stands out as a welcome vegan-friendly destination in an area with limited plant-based choices.

‍

The menu features traditional Vietnamese dishes at reasonable prices, with all but one dish that are either vegan or can be made vegan. I've tried the Cơm Tấm Bì, or Vietnamese broken rice. This interesting and flavourful dish combines crispy ‘pork’ skin, chewy vegan meat, pickles, and fresh vegetables, all brought together by a sweet and tangy vegan ‘fish’ sauce.

‍

While the food is a highlight, it's a good idea to be extra clear when ordering, as some staff members may have limited English, which can lead to mix-ups. When I order the dish, they initially forgot to make my dish vegan. However, they were very quick to fix it once I double checked with them. So just make sure to be a bit careful when you order.
fieldData.name: Tinh Lac Vietnamese Vegetarian Restaurant

fieldData.name-in-original-language: わらび餅専門店 門藤
fieldData.meta-description: Warabimochi specialty shop on the way to Himeji Castle
fieldData.description:
As I was walking towards Himeji Castle, I stumbled upon this warabimochi specialty shop. Warabimochi (蕨餅) is a jelly-like mochi coated with soybean flour (kinako) and sometimes drizzled with brown sugar syrup. It’s traditionally vegan.

‍

The 3-piece warabimochi box makes a great snack in between meals. It comes with 3 soft, chewy pieces coated with 3 different types of soybean powders. Keep in mind that the drinks and ice cream are not vegan.
fieldData.name: Kadofuji Warabimochi

fieldData.meta-description: Cozy vegan cafe by Himeji Castle known for its ramen & katsu sets.
fieldData.description:
(Sai Cafe is permanently closed. A new cafe called Cafe COVO reopened in the same place but reportedly they have no vegan options.)

‍

Sai Cafe in Himeji is an amazing vegan restaurant with a menu that is supervised by the head chef of the popular Saido restaurant in Tokyo. Although this cafe may not be the easiest to get to, it is well-worth a little detour as the food quality is top-notch. You can find beautifully-presented dishes including ramen, katsu curry rice, tempura rice bowl and more. English menu is available, but it's not as updated as the Japanese menu, so I'd recommend translating from the Japanese menu to see all the dishes.

‍

The atmosphere is calm and relaxing, and the staff is friendly. The closest train station is Nozato, which is about a 20-minute walk away.
fieldData.name: Sai Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: Charming plant-based cafe serving a set vegan lunch menu & sweets.
fieldData.description:
Il riccio is a charming, vegan cafe with a relaxing atmosphere and friendly service. It's a great choice if you are heading to Himeji Castle as it's located in between the Castle and Himeji Station. Keep in mind that the shop section may sell some non-vegan products, so it's best to check the ingredients and double-confirm with staff.

‍

They offer 2 main lunch sets until 3:30, the monthly changing set meal and the baked Japanese taro soy milk gratin. I chose the latter which was served with bread and salad. The bake is creamy with soft Japanese yam and soy meat bolognese sauce inside, and it’s delicious when spread on bread. For desserts, they use organic flour from Japan and avoid using white sugar. You’ll find options like matcha flan, gateau chocolate cake and gelato .
fieldData.name: il riccio

fieldData.name-in-original-language: チャイナダイニング ⾶天
fieldData.meta-description: Upstairs Chinese restaurant with a dedicated vegan menu near Kintetsu Nara station
fieldData.description: China Dining Hiten is a Chinese restaurant that serves meat but offers a separate menu with vegan options, making it a convenient choice for mixed-diet groups. Kepe in mind that the restaurant is on the 2nd floor and you may have to ask for the vegan menu. Popular choices include the mapo tofu and soy cashew stir-fry.
fieldData.name: China Dining Hiten

fieldData.meta-description: Famous shop with live pounding shows for its fresh, warm vegan mochi
fieldData.description:
Near the entrance of Nara Park, this traditional dessert shop sells a green mugwort ‘yomogi’ mochi with sweet red bean filling. The surface is dusted with yellow soybean powder. The mochi is soft and chewy, and it’s filled with a generous amount of red bean paste.

‍

As the mochi is freshly made, if you are lucky, you can witness the famous mochi making show. Just keep in mind that because of that, this place has become extremely popular and there would likely be a queue when you buy the mochi.
fieldData.name: Nakatanidou

fieldData.meta-description: Ramen shop by Nara Park with vegan ramen options
fieldData.description: This ramen shop is a convenient option for vegans, located directly across from Nara Park and Nara National Museum. Unlike their sister shop in Osaka which is all-vegan, this branch in Nara serves meat, but still offer clearly marked vegan options like vegan miso ramen and vegan tonkotsu ramen.
fieldData.name: Vegan Friendly Ramen by Playpen Friends

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒630-8357 Nara, Surugamachi, 25-1 Felis 駅前 1階
fieldData.meta-description: Cozy spot for delicious, gluten-free vegan Japanese set lunches
fieldData.description:
A vegetarian cafe 10-minute walk from JR Nara Station, offering daily lunch plates with 4 small dishes, soup and rice. The small dishes often include salad, steamed vegetables, and fried tofu. They also serve ramen or udon sets. Lunch sets are 2,000 yen.

‍

Some dishes may have a dairy and dairy-free option. Opens for lunch, but the dinner kaiseki cuisine requires reservations.

‍
fieldData.name: Kinatei

fieldData.meta-description: All-vegan cafe serving delicious Japanese plates near JR Nara station
fieldData.description:
Tucked away in the back streets near JR Nara station, Onwa is an all-vegan cafe serving incredibly photogenic and delicious plates, The highlight here is the "Vegan Delight" plate which features all the small dishes they make here, including soy protein taco, tofu patty, fried soy meat, pickles, radish cake and more. As the dishes are freshly made, be prepared for a bit of a wait.

‍

Near the entrance, you'll also find a cabinet full of vegan treats and desserts like blueberry tart and vegan cheesecake. The staff here is friendly and English menu is available.
fieldData.name: Onwa

fieldData.name-in-original-language: モダナークファームカフェ
fieldData.address-text: 3 Chome-11-15 Kitanagasadori, Chuo Ward, Kobe, Hyogo 650-0012, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Casual vegetarian cafe with many vegan options & a resident cat
fieldData.description: Modernark Pharm is a charming cafe with a vintage vibe that offers great vegan options. All the dishes are either vegan by default or can be made vegan. You can find meals like the vegetarian plate or the curry plate, both of which may need to customise for vegans. Keep in mind that this cafe only accepts cash or Paypay.
fieldData.name: Modernark Pharm Cafe

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ベジバーガー元町バロム
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒650-0021 Hyogo, Kobe, Chuo Ward, Sannomiyacho, 3 Chome−5−5 2F
fieldData.meta-description: Takeaway vegan spot with budget-friendly and delicious burgers
fieldData.description:
Located in the heart of Kobe near Chinatown and Sannomiya station, Veggie Junkies Burger is an all-vegan, takeaway-only spot. This place is run by a cute couple and offers a limited setting area for customers to wait for their orders, but there’s no dine-in option. I’d recommend going to a nearby park, or to the seaside area where Kobe Port Tower is to enjoy the burger.

‍

After going upstairs, you can order through a ticket machine, hand the ticket to the staff, and they will prepare your burger. They offer a small menu of 3 burgers: teriyaki mushroom, curry bean and tomato, and desserts like soy milk pudding or agar agar jelly.
fieldData.name: Veggie Junkies Burger

fieldData.address-text: 2 Chome-10-18 Kitanocho, Chuo Ward, Kobe, Hyogo 650-0002, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Organic vegan cafe in a traditional house serving seasonal set meals
fieldData.description: Located in a small alleyway in Kitano Ijinkan-Gai, Vegan Cafe Kiu is a homey, cozy vegan place offering delicious food with friendly staff. They specialise in a one-plate set meal that changes regularly, typically offering a choice between a curry or a “Kiu Gohan” set, both featuring seasonal vegetables. I tried the latter and all the elements on the plates are well-made and delicious. While the main meals are excellent, the desserts are a true highlight—the warm, fluffy carrot cake and the beautifully presented cheesecake come highly recommended. The cafe is a bit of a walk up a hill, which some may find tricky, but most agree it is well worth the trip.
fieldData.name: Vegan Cafe Kiu

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ヴィーガンカフェ タロ
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒650-0012 Hyogo, Kobe, Chuo Ward, Kitanagasadori, 4 Chome−7−12 オーシャンズコート 1F
fieldData.meta-description: Weekend-only vegan cafe with colourful nutritious plates and vegan cakes
fieldData.description: Thallo is an all-vegan cafe with a comfy interior and a passion for animal rights, run by a friendly owner who is also involved in cat rescue. The menu changes regularly, but you can expect a colourful plate using seasonal produce and soy products. They may also have desserts like chocolate cakes. Keep in mind that they only open on the weekends.
fieldData.name: Vegan Cafe Thallo

fieldData.meta-description: Japanese spot with a separate English menu for vegan ramen & sushi
fieldData.description: Onari Yokocho is a Japanese omni restaurant that offers a good selection of clearly marked vegan dishes on a separate English menu. The vegan options include a tonkotsu-style ramen, sushi and Japanese curry. The prices are relatively high for the portion, but with its convenient location (just a few minutes from Kamakura station) and the clear vegan options, it's still a solid choice.
fieldData.name: Onari Yokocho Kamakura

fieldData.name-in-original-language: カズローデリカマクラ
fieldData.meta-description: Cozy vegan deli with a Japanese & Middle Eastern fusion menu
fieldData.description: This cozy, vegan restaurant offers a delicious fusion of Japanese and Middle Eastern dishes. The cafe has a relaxing vibe decorated with wood and dried flowers. The cafe often is run by just the owner, both taking your order and cooking up food. The standout menu item is the excellent falafel, which you can enjoy in a pita or as part of a larger plate. An English menu with photos is available.
fieldData.name: Kazro Deli Kamakura

fieldData.meta-description: Popular all-vegan burger restaurant near the beach
fieldData.description: Starting as a food truck, Luna Burger is now a popular brick-and-mortar restaurant in Kamakura located right next to Hase Station. They serve a great selection of all-vegan burgers, like the Kamakura BBQ burger I tried. Other than burgers, you'll find a unique assortment of soy whipped cream-filled buns, with one that’s fried and needs to be eaten within 60 seconds before the cream melts.
fieldData.name: Luna Burger

fieldData.meta-description: Reservation-only vegan bistro for a classy multi-course meal
fieldData.description: Vegetus is a high-end vegan bistro offering an intimate, high-end dining experience perfect for a special occasion. Seating is limited, and reservations are required at least two business days in advance. The owner, who is also the chef, prepares an exquisite fixed multi-course menu using local vegetables, with options for the main dish and pasta. The food quality is high but also with a high price tag. The experience is intentionally slow-paced, with a full meal lasting up to three hours.
fieldData.name: Vegetus Kamakura

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan restaurant in a vintage setting serving curries & buddha bowls
fieldData.description: Just a short walk from Hase station, Cotonoha is an all-vegan restaurant set in a vintage Japanese house with a cute patio. The food here focuses on fresh, healthy ingredients. The menu is concise and typically features their buddha bowl plate and curry plate, which are beautifully presented and delicious. Although the friendly owners may not speak great English, you'll find an English menu.
fieldData.name: Cotonoha

fieldData.name-in-original-language: アーリーバードコーヒー
fieldData.meta-description: Creative vegan cafe known for sweet & savoury gluten-free pancakes
fieldData.description: Early Bird Coffee is a sweet and creative all-vegan cafe run by a kind, English-speaking couple. The menu offers a surprising range of options, with a special focus on pancakes that come in both sweet and savoury varieties, such as the unique falafel pancakes. In addition to pancakes, you can find lunch plates and baked goods. Be sure to check their Instagram for pop-up events and irregular hours, and keep in mind that they are cash only. To get there, it's a 15-minute walk from Kotoku-in.
fieldData.name: Early Bird Coffee

fieldData.meta-description: Peaceful vegan Taiwanese-Japanese fusion restaurant in a traditional Japanese house
fieldData.description: Isso is a beautiful and intimate restaurant offering a fusion of vegan Taiwanese and Japanese traditional cuisine. With a peaceful, zen-like atmosphere, it’s a place that makes you slow down and enjoy the moment. Remember to take your shoes off when you enter. The menu is fully vegan, centred around Taiwanese-Japanese fusion dishes. Try their Isso plate to sample a variety of beautifully presented dishes.
fieldData.name: Isso Chaan

fieldData.name-in-original-language: カフェ スタンド ブロッサム
fieldData.meta-description: Lovely vegan gem near Kotoku-in serving Japanese sweets & amazake drinks
fieldData.description:
On your way from Kase station to see the big buddha at Kotoku-in, you'll find Cafe Stand Blossom. This little all-vegan cafe is such a gem with delicious veganised Japanese desserts, like the chocolate ganache monaka and red bean dorayaki. You'll also find muffin, ice cream sundae and banana cake.

‍

Don't miss their 'amazake' drinks, which is a non-alcoholic drink made from fermented rice. Its natural sweetness goes very well with matcha.
fieldData.name: Cafe Stand Blossom Kamakura

fieldData.meta-description: Cozy all-vegan bakery & cafe with homemade bread & sandwich sets
fieldData.description: 24sekki is a small, cozy, all-vegan bakery and cafe which is a 10 minute bus away from Kamakura station. The quiet, hideout-like atmosphere makes it a great spot for a relaxing meal. They offer simple lunch sets, with options like the vegan meat sandwich and other house-made bread. Cinnamon rolls are another popular choice if you are looking for something sweet. Keep in mind that the hours are irregular and limited, so be sure to check their website or Instagram before visiting.
fieldData.name: Kamakura 24sekki

fieldData.name-in-original-language: 野菜寿司処 ちらしや
fieldData.meta-description: An all-vegan restaurant near Kita-Kamakura station serving beautifully presented & delicious sushi
fieldData.description:
Chirashiya is a small, all-vegan restaurant that specialises in beautifully crafted vegan sushi sets. Each sushi is carefully prepared and visually stunning. I tried their 12-piece sushi set which showcases a range of fresh Japanese produce like pumpkin coconut oil sushi and the yam tofu sushi. Don't expect the sushi to taste like seafood though; what you can expect is a sushi plate that highlights the tasty veggies and soy products of Japan. The set also comes with an appetiser and miso soup.

‍

The place is cozy and relaxing, and the owners and staff are very friendly. Because of its popularity and limited space, it’s a good idea to make a reservation. Be sure to arrive well before the closing time, as they can sell out of their popular sushi sets early in the afternoon.
fieldData.name: Chirashiya

fieldData.meta-description: Middle Eastern and Mediterranean restaurant in Paddington with an impressive seasonal vegan menu
fieldData.description:
Located in Paddington, Nain serves up impressive Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisine with a separate vegan menu. The chefs clearly put a lot of thought into creating dishes with well-executed flavours and textures, and the menu changes seasonally.

‍
Standout vegan dishes might include creative share plates like "Muhamarra" with an interesting flavour mix of black tahini and cashew cheese, or hearty mains such as a Fable mushroom lasagna that goes great with the rich cashew parmesan and sundried tomato. While the food quality is consistently high, keep in mind that the prices are also relatively high, and service can sometimes be on the slower side, with waits between courses.

‍
fieldData.name: NAÏM

fieldData.meta-description: A Vietnamese food and juice shop with a separate vegan menu serving banh mi, rice paper rolls & more
fieldData.description: Fat Carrot is a Vietnamese cafe located in the heart of West End on Boundary Street, offering a great selection for vegans with its separate vegan menu. You'll find classics like pho and rice paper rolls, but their vegan banh mi range is my favourite here, featuring options like satay chicken, lemongrass beef, and fish cake. These are typically packed with shredded carrots and other veggies, with vegan mayo. It's a good idea to specify "vegan" when ordering your banh mi, as not all options are vegan by default. The cafe offers both indoor and outdoor seating.
fieldData.name: The Fat Carrot

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒604-8172 Kyoto, Nakagyo Ward, Banocho, 586-2 新風館 1F
fieldData.meta-description: A book shop + cafe concept serving clearly marked vegan food and snacks; Located in Shinpuukan
fieldData.description:
Book and Vege OyOy is a book shop + cafe concept located inside the Shinpuukan shopping centre, which is just next to exit 5 of Karasuma Oike Station.

‍

The food uses fresh, organic seasonal vegetables sourced from small-scale, sustainable farms. On Friday, Saturday and Sunday, you can try the local produce out in the 'Oyoy Vegan Plate'. They also have snacks and desserts like the persimmon tofu pudding I tried. You can also find oat milk latte here which is not common in Japan.

‍

When you are waiting for your order, you can browse their shop for books and groceries, but note that you’re not allowed to take the books to the dining area to read without buying them.
fieldData.name: Book and Vege OyOy

fieldData.meta-description: All-vegan Taiwanese-focused eatery with eel rice, hot pot and herbal dishes
fieldData.description:
Cafe Ren is an all-vegan restaurant specialising in Taiwanese cuisine, with a focus on herbal dishes, dim sum and hot pot, all prepared without onion or garlic. I love the vegan eel rice bowl here, which they created a spot-on eel texture using okara (tofu pulp) and seaweed. The set also comes with three small side dishes and a soup.

‍

They have two branches in Kyoto - one near Omiya station and one in the Horikawa area.
fieldData.name: Cafe Ren

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒604-0842 Kyoto, Nakagyo Ward, Kurumayacho, 通押小路上る109-1
fieldData.meta-description: Small bakery with a range of vegan donuts, including tofu cream filled doughnuts
fieldData.description:
A doughnut specialty bakery with clearly marked vegan options including original, mocha and red bean. You can also find doughnuts filled with tofu whipped cream.

‍

The doughnuts have a fluffy, bread-y texture. The mocha doughnut I tried had subtle flavours. However, the soy latte I got was pretty average. They have a few seats inside for dining in.

‍
fieldData.name: Doughnut Cafe nicotto & mam

fieldData.meta-description: A mostly vegan cafe specialising in sesame-based dishes like tantan ramen and white sesame curry
fieldData.description:
Gomacro is a true gem for vegans who love sesame (like me!). This cozy, relaxing cafe celebrates everything sesame and offers a selection of delicious dishes. Everything is vegan except the use of honey in the eggplant for bibimbap.

‍

You’ll find dishes like tantan ramen and curry rice that highlight the flavours of sesame. The white curry rice set I tried is delicious and comes with a hearty salad. The curry is rich and fragrant, with a generous amount of curry sauce. Even the drinks and desserts include sesame, like the soy milk black sesame pudding, sesame ice cream affogato and sesame chai.

‍

On each table is a basket of sesame condiments, including tahini-like sesame sauce, sesame oil, and sesame salt, allowing you to make your dish even stronger in sesame flavours.

‍

Don’t miss their shop area after your meal to find some sesame goodies, like sesame oil and sesame furikake (a rice topping that often contains fish).

‍
fieldData.name: Gomacro Salon

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ぎをん⾖乳ら〜めん うのゆきこ
fieldData.meta-description: Fully vegan soy milk ramen in the popular Gion area
fieldData.description:
Located conveniently in the Gion area (walking distance from Yasaka Shrine), this fully vegan ramen restaurant specialises in two types of ramen made with a creamy soy milk base - Soy milk ramen and soy milk tantan ramen.

‍

The ramen broth is creamy, rich and flavourful. That being said, it's slightly on the sour side for my taste. The tantan ramen I ordered comes with chewy, glass-noodle like ramen and topped with vegan mince and soy cream.

‍

Other than ramen, you can also find soy meat rice bowl, gyoza, croquettes and more. They also offer some vegan desserts including creme brulee and ice cream. You'll also find a vending machine out front selling vegan cakes.
fieldData.name: Gion Soy Milk Ramen Uno Yokiko

fieldData.meta-description: Local udon shop in Gion area with clearly marked vegan options including tempura udon
fieldData.description:
While Menkui Kinya serves meat, it’s a popular local spot near the Gion-Shijo station for those seeking vegan-friendly udon and tempura. They have clearly marked vegan options on the menu and even provide labeled vegan soy sauce and tempura sauce.

‍

They offer freshly-made udon noodles with 2 vegan tempura options - 6-vegetable tempura and green onion tempura. The 6-vegetable one I tried is light, crispy and delicious. The prices are also reasonable compared to other vegan-friendly places in Kyoto.

‍

The restaurant is quite small which means there's likely a wait for a table. If the wait is too long, consider Gion Soy Milk Ramen which is just around the corner.
fieldData.name: Menkui Kinya

fieldData.name-in-original-language: プレマルシェ·オルタナティブ·ダイナー
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan-friendly diner offering burgers and pizzas; walking distance from Nijō Castle
fieldData.description:
Part of the Premarche group, this "alternative diner" and pizzeria serves meat but all the dishes are vegan by default (marked with a V) with options to change to meat. Burgers like fish burger or Korean BBQ burger are great options for first-time visitors. However, the Japanese mushroom pizza I tried is not my favourite with a relatively average pizza base and a lack of sauce, though the toppings are interesting with a mix of Japanese mushrooms, seaweed and soy sauce.

‍

The same company also runs the ‘Premarche’ gelato shop just a block away, which makes a wide range of vegan gelato that are rich and delicious. I'd highly recommend trying it out if you have a chance. If you dine in the restaurant, you may get a 100-yen discount coupon to use in the gelato shop.

‍

This restaurant is located just about a 10-minute walk from Nijō Castle, making it a decent option for a meal.
fieldData.name: Premarche Alternative Diner

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒604-8022 Kyoto, Nakagyo Ward, Minamikurumayacho, 287 木屋町会館 １階
fieldData.meta-description: Intimate vegan izakaya offering traditional Japanese sets & chazuke
fieldData.description:
For an authentic and traditional vegan Japanese dining experience, Nijiya is a standout. This small izakaya specialises in chazuke (rice with tea/dashi) and offers beautifully presented tasting menus or sets that showcase dishes like stewed shiitake mushrooms and grilled origiri. I recommend getting a full set to try a bit of everything. The intimate setting, with only about seven seats, makes for a special meal.

‍

Because of its location near Kawaramachi area, it's a highly popular restaurant with limited space. Be prepared for a wait and potentially a dine-in time limit.
fieldData.name: Vegan Izakaya Nijiya

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ムスビ スウィーツ ファクトリー
fieldData.address-text: 51 Arashiyama Nakaoshitacho, Nishikyo Ward, Kyoto, 616-0004, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan & gluten-free cake shop in Arashiyama area
fieldData.description: Musubi Sweets Factory is a fully vegan and gluten-free cake shop located clear to the Hankyu Arashiyama station. The cafe is relaxing and cozy, offering a range of cakes, tarts and even ice cream cookie sandwich. For a classic Japanese dessert, I'd recommend the matcha tofu cake which has a soft, creamy texture. However, the coffee I had was not great as it was very weak.
fieldData.name: Musubi Sweets Factory

fieldData.address-text: 8 Chome-414-4 宮川 Higashiyama Ward, Kyoto, 605-0801, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan zero-waste store with a cafe serving vegan Korean dishes like gimbap and BBQ bowl
fieldData.description: Tu Casa is a charming Korean vegan cafe with a strong commitment to sustainability, featuring a zero-waste store on site. They serve classic delicious Korean dishes including bibimbap, gimbap, and BBQ bowl with grilled soy meat. Don't miss their baked goods; the lemon cake is a particular favourite. The vibe is cute, calm, and friendly, run by lovely owners. With limited seatings, I'd recommend arriving early if you're looking to dine in.
fieldData.name: Tu Casa

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒604-8041 Kyoto, Nakagyo Ward, Uraderacho, 607‐19 ヴァントワビル3階 4階
fieldData.meta-description: A small, artsy omni restaurant near Teramachi-Dori shopping street
fieldData.description:
Close to the Teramachi-Dori shopping street, Pelgag is a small restaurant with a veg menu with vegan options marked. They offer rotating vegan options like curry rice, fried rice and sautéed vegetable dishes. As there are only around 10 seats, and the cafe is often run by just one person, there could be a wait for food.

‍
fieldData.name: Pelgag

fieldData.address-text: 1 Chome-5-5 Namba, Chuo Ward, Osaka, 542-0076, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: A small cake shop near Dotonbori offering beautifully crafted, fully vegan cakes and tarts
fieldData.description: Naki Vegan Sweets is a small, fully vegan bakery located in the Namba/Dotonbori area of Osaka. They specialise in beautifully made cakes, tarts, and cookies, with a rotating selection. The products are high quality and visually stunning. The shop itself is quite small and more of a grab-and-go spot, though there are some wall-facing seats.
fieldData.name: Naki Vegan Sweets

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒542-0071 Osaka, Chuo Ward, Dotonbori, 1 Chome−7−21 中座くいだおれビル 1階
fieldData.meta-description: This Dotonbori vegan cafe serves Osaka street food like takoyaki and okonomiyaki
fieldData.description: Pivot BASE is a fully vegan cafe and bar conveniently located in the busy Dotonbori area. Their concept is to offer vegan versions of iconic Osaka specialty street foods, such as takoyaki (octopus balls), okonomiyaki (savoury pancakes) and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers). The menu also includes dishes like yakisoba, ramen, vegan cutlet rice bowls (katsudon), and fried gyoza. English menu is available and you can communicate with the staff in English.
fieldData.name: Pivot BASE Cafe & Bar

fieldData.meta-description: Acai bowl and smoothie cafe in Greenslopes where you can also find vegan burgers
fieldData.description:
Charlie's Raw Squeeze in Greenslopes/Stones Corner is a go-to for healthy smoothie bowls and juices. What's great about this particular location is that it also houses their own vegan burger shop, MooFree Burgers, so you can get both at one location. I find their acai bowls and smoothie options to be fresh and hearty, and I particularly love their peanut butter acai bowl.

‍

They also offer weekday deals when you mention their social media or website. For example, by one get one free juice on Tuesdays and $5 falafel burger with any juice purchase on Fridays.
fieldData.name: Charlies Raw Squeeze + MooFree Burgers

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan-friendly cafe in New Farm with acai bowls, gnocchi and other options
fieldData.description:
Mylkko in New Farm has a vegan purple ube hotcake on their menu, and as an ube fan, I went to try it. This vegan and gluten-free dessert comes with ube ice cream, ube custard, crumble, and edible gold flakes on a hotcake that is soft and a bit chewy. While the ube flavours were there, I found the portion to be quite small for the price.

‍

Beyond the ube hotcake, Mylkko offers other vegan choices. For savoury food, they have gnocchi and salad bowls. It's also good to know that all their açai bowls are vegan, including interesting ones like the "Snickers Bowl" with cacao, peanut butter, and salted caramel, or the "Golden Gaytime" inspired bowl with cookie dough, chocolate sauce, and chocolate granola.
fieldData.name: Mylk & Ko

fieldData.meta-description: A LGBTQ+ friendly bar with good vegan food options
fieldData.description: The Wickham, a vibrant LGBTQ+ friendly venue, surprised me with its great vegan food offerings. They have vegan-friendly stone-baked pizza, burger, schnitzel, garlic bread and more. I tried their Tartufo pizza, which features truffle paste, mushrooms, vegan cheese, and topped with crispy fried enoki mushrooms. The base is well-made and chewy, and at the weekday lunch special price of $15 (usually $29), it was an absolute steal – just remember to specify 'vegan' when ordering.
fieldData.name: The Wickham

fieldData.name-in-original-language: アサカラ グッドストア
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒540-0006 Osaka, Chuo Ward, Hoenzaka, 1 Chome−4−6 1F102 法円坂ハイツ
fieldData.meta-description: Popular cafe with clearly marked vegan options located near Osaka Castle
fieldData.description:
While not a fully vegan cafe, Asakara Good Store has clearly marked vegan options. You can expect to find choices like a vegan miso tuna melt sandwich or a full Aussie-style vegan breakfast. For those with a sweet tooth (like me!), the vegan strawberry cream sandwich is a great sweet breakfast option, featuring vegan whipped cream and fresh strawberries in soft bread.

‍

It's located about 15-20 minute walk from Osaka Castle, so it's a good dining option if that's in your itinerary. Do keep in mind that this cafe is quite popular, so you might have to wait before getting a dine-in spot.
fieldData.name: Asakara Good Store

fieldData.address-text: 3 Chome-4-5 Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa Ward, Osaka, 556-0002, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan cafe serving veganised Japanese street food located near Tsūtenkaku tower
fieldData.description:
Shinsekai Paprika Shokudo is just a short walk away from the famous Tsūtenkaku tower. This vegan cafe serves classic Japanese street food including kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) and takoyaki (octopus balls). I tried the assorted plate of kushikatsu which includes a delicious variety of skewers of Beyond Meat, vegan cheese, shiitake mushrooms, lotus root, and sweet potato.

‍

The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating, and the staff is friendly. If you're lucky, you may also see the two cats that are frequent visitors to this cafe. With its high quality food, friendly staff and proximity to the famous sightseeing spot, Shinsekai Paprika Shokudo is an amazing option if you are in the area.
fieldData.name: Shinsekai Paprika Shokudo Vegan

fieldData.name-in-original-language: メーシー ビーガン ファクトリー
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒542-0066 Osaka, Chuo Ward, Kawarayamachi, 2 Chome−4−15 西側（瓦屋町グランド正面 1階
fieldData.meta-description: All vegan cafe serving realistic egg sandwich and other delicious comfort food
fieldData.description:
Mercy Vegan Factory is one of my favourite places in Osaka because of the amazing food and comfy , neighbourhood vibe. I love their vegan egg sandwich – the vegan egg salad part is realistic and delicious, and it's served on soft sandwich bread. This tasty egg sandwich is also available for takeaway if you're in a rush.

‍

You'll also find comfort food like karaage chicken, Korean gimbap and curry rice in their lunch and dinner menus. In the cabinet, they carry a good range of vegan desserts and patisserie using seasonal fruits. All the food I've tried here is delicious and well-made.

‍

The closest station to Mercy Vegan Factory is Tanimachi 9-chome Station, but it's walkable from Dotonbori or Namba Station.
fieldData.name: Mercy Vegan Factory

fieldData.address-text: 6 Chome-17-5 Tanimachi, Chuo Ward, Osaka, 542-0012, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Fully vegan cat cafe fostering rescue cats; Meals only available Saturday - Monday
fieldData.description:
Tucked away in an unassuming alleyway, Shelter Cat & Vegan Cafe NEU is a unique cat cafe where all the cats are rescues and the food is all vegan.

‍

After you take off your shoes and wash your hands, you’ll step in and be greeted by cute rescue cats. There are two cat rooms: The first floor cat room is home to the more social and experienced cats who enjoy human interactions. Upstairs (careful of the steep staircase!), you'll find a space dedicated to newer cats who are a bit more timid and still adjusting to human company. While petting is discouraged in the upstairs area, you can still play with them with toys.

‍

What makes this place even better is that they have a small eating area upstairs serving an all vegan menu. Despite not being a full-scale cafe, the food is surprisingly tasty. The eating area is right next to the upstairs cat room so you can eat while watching cute cats. But if you plan to eat here, arrive early because there are only 2 tables. Also keep in mind that they only serve food on Saturday, Sunday and Monday; On other days, only drinks are available.

‍

The menu is relatively small with options like fried soy meat lunch plate, bolognese and soy burger steak plate. You can finish your meal with a brown syrup ice cream or a matcha latte with cat-shaped foam.

‍

The entry price for the cat room is 1,500 yen for one hour. And if you choose to have food in addition, you can get a 300 yen discount for food.
fieldData.name: Shelter Cat & Vegan Cafe NEU

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒530-0037 Osaka, Kita Ward, Matsugaecho, 6−1 グロウビル 1F
fieldData.meta-description: Wholesome vegan cafe serving buddha bowl, bibimbap and more. Located near Tenmangu Shrine
fieldData.description:
Bee9 Vegan Cafe is a relatively unknown gem in Osaka serving up delicious vegan food. This cozy cafe has a cozy, inviting ambiance and is conveniently located near the famous Tenmangu Shrine. Though the menu is concise, it offers excellent main dishes like buddha bowls, bibimbap, and tantan ramen.

‍

I tried and loved the kimbap/gimbap plate, featuring colourful kimbap stuffed with hearty veggies and flavourful fried soy meat. For dessert, you'll find hard-to-find items in Japan like acai parfait, alongside pound cakes and cupcakes.

‍

The cafe is relaxing and peaceful, and the staff is friendly. English menu is available.
fieldData.name: Bee9 Vegan Cafe

fieldData.address-text: Tennoji Park Villa, 105号, 1 Chome-1-10 Sanno, Nishinari Ward, Osaka, 557-0001, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Fully vegan Taiwanese spot that's budget-friendly and delicious
fieldData.description:
(TW VEGAN NIGHT MARKET is previously known as Saijiki)

‍

Saijiki is a vegan Taiwanese restaurant offering authentic cuisine at great prices. As a restaurant that doesn’t use the "five pungent roots" like onions and garlic, their food is still tasty and flavourful. You can find classic Taiwanese dishes like mapo tofu, deep-fried "big chicken" cutlet, bamboo basket-steamed dumplings, and more.

‍

For a satisfying and budget-friendly meal, come for lunch and get one of their lunch sets. The Taiwanese mince rice set comes with dumplings, veggies and soup in addition to the main. They use a ticket machine ordering process - simply purchase your meal ticket from the vending machine near the entrance, then hand it over to the friendly staff who will promptly prepare your food.
fieldData.name: TW VEGAN NIGHT MARKET

fieldData.address-text: 5 Chome-11-6 Nipponbashi, Naniwa Ward, Osaka, 550-0005, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan food stand serving a variety of fluffy baos & donuts
fieldData.description:
LUU's BAO is a specialty shop serving delicious vegan baos. Located next to a busy road, the setting may not be the most serene, but the great food quality more than makes up for it.

‍

The bao I tried - Kakiage tempura with wasabi tartare sauce - was fresh and delicious with perfectly soft buns and crispy veggie tempura. The sauce is creamy, though the wasabi flavour could be stronger. The prices are reasonable for the large size of the baos. If you want something sweet afterwards, try one of their freshly fried doughnuts.
fieldData.name: LUU's Bao

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ヴィーガンラーメン ウズ トウキョウ
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒135-0061 Tokyo, Koto City, Toyosu, 6 Chome−1−16 teamLab Planets TOKYO
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan ramen inside TeamLab Planets; museum ticket required.
fieldData.description: Vegan Ramen UZU Tokyo offers a unique dining experience, located exclusively inside the TeamLab Planets digital art museum – meaning you must have a museum ticket to access it. They serve fully vegan ramen, specialty teas, muffins, and ice cream (flavours like matcha, yuzu, strawberry). It's a convenient option for a meal or snack during your museum visit, with outdoor seating available. However, reviews are strongly mixed. Some visitors rave about the delicious ramen and ice cream, calling it one of the best things they've eaten. Others find the ramen basic and lacking toppings, criticize the ice cream quality, and express frustration about the restricted access and potential wait times. If eating before your exhibit, book your museum ticket for at least an hour earlier.
fieldData.name: Vegan Ramen UZU Tokyo

fieldData.address-text: 2 Chome-15-10 Jiyugaoka, Meguro City, Tokyo 152-0035, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Top-tier vegan Japanese; innovative food, requires reservation.
fieldData.description: Saido in Jiyugaoka offers an outstanding fine dining experience focused entirely on innovative vegan Japanese cuisine. This reservation-only restaurant is celebrated for its creative use of vegetables and mushrooms, crafting dishes like vegan eel, katsu, noodles, and curry, alongside exquisite bento sets. The presentation is artistic and playful, adding to the fun. Diners consistently rave about the incredible flavours, meticulous attention to detail, and top-notch, intimate service where staff patiently explain each course. Vegan sake and wine are also available. While pricey, Saido is widely regarded as one of the best vegan dining experiences in Tokyo, impressing vegans and non-vegans alike. Reservations are essential (no walk-ins) and must be made via their website. Closed Wednesdays.
fieldData.name: Saido

fieldData.name-in-original-language: オブゴ ベイカー
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan cookie cafe in Laforet; mixed reviews on cookie texture.
fieldData.description: Located on the 2nd floor of Laforet Harajuku, OVGO B.A.K.E.R. is a fully vegan cookie shop and cafe with a cute atmosphere. They offer a wide variety of American-style cookies, alongside scones, ice cream, cookie sundaes, and coffee/tea. It provides a convenient vegan dessert option within the busy mall. However, reviews are quite mixed. While some enjoy the scones or appreciate the vegan availability, many visitors report the cookies being extremely hard and difficult to eat, and the coffee quality has been criticized. Some also find it pricey for what's offered. It might be worth a stop if you're nearby and need a quick vegan treat, but manage expectations, especially regarding the cookie texture. Credit card only.
fieldData.name: ovgo Baker

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ヴィーガンカフェピーキューズ
fieldData.address-text: 1 Chome-1-2 Ryusen, Taito City, Tokyo 110-0012, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Creative vegan cafe; seasonal menus, dog-friendly, peaceful vibe.
fieldData.description: Vegan Cafe PQ's is a gem offering a welcoming, chill vibe and highly creative, beautifully presented 100% vegan food. They use quality organic and fair-trade ingredients for their daily changing lunch sets and impressive seasonal menus (like Sakura-themed dishes). Standouts include hamburger steak, sweet and savory pancakes, and delicious baked goods. The cafe is spacious, peaceful, and notably dog-friendly (they even have a dog menu!). Located slightly out of the way but considered well worth the trip, it's perfect for a relaxing meal. Note: Ordering is via QR code, and they have specific opening days/times (closed Tue/Wed, Wed is baked goods/drinks only).
fieldData.name: Vegan Cafe PQ's

fieldData.meta-description: Ramen shop (serves meat) w/ one tasty vegan ramen option; busy.
fieldData.description: Located in the bustling Akihabara area, Kyushu Jangara Ramen is a traditional ramen shop that serves meat but offers a vegan ramen option. While they previously had two choices, recent reports (as of March 2025, needs confirmation) suggest only one vegan ramen bowl is currently available, featuring vegetables and tofu (you can add vegan char siu). Despite the limited choice, reviewers find the vegan ramen delicious and authentic. The atmosphere is trendy but seating is very limited, leading to likely queues and a quick eat-and-go experience. It's a worthwhile option if you need vegan ramen in Akihabara, but manage expectations regarding choice and wait times.
fieldData.name: Kyushu Jangara

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ヴィーガンギョーザ ユー
fieldData.address-text: 3 Chome-11-17 Negishi, Taito City, Tokyo 110-0003, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan gyoza specialist; flavourful dumplings, no sauce needed.
fieldData.description: This unique spot is a fully vegan gyoza house and coffee shop, serving up pan-fried or steamed dumplings bursting with distinct flavours – so flavourful, reviewers say no sauce is needed! Each gyoza in their mixed platters tastes different, with fillings like shiitake, miso ginger, and kimchi being favourites. The gyoza wrappers are noted as being slightly thicker than typical. They also offer great coffee, beers, and fun vegan cream sodas. It's a charming but popular place, so expect a potential wait, especially on weekends. Located in a quiet neighborhood, it's worth the trip for dedicated gyoza fans. Closed Mon/Tue.
fieldData.name: Vegan Gyoza Yu

fieldData.address-text: 2 Chome-18-8 Azabujuban, Minato City, Tokyo 106-0045, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Amazing vegan bakery; huge range (croissants, melon pan), sells out!
fieldData.description: Te Cor Gentil is a highly recommended fully vegan bakery offering an amazing and extensive selection of both sweet and savory baked goods. You can find everything from croissants, various bread loaves, and pizza slices to Japanese favourites like melon pan and anpan, alongside donuts, cream choux, and sandwiches. Everything is praised for being delicious and great value. It's a small spot with limited outdoor seating (locals suggest enjoying purchases in the nearby park), so plan for takeaway. Be sure to arrive early, as popular items sell out quickly. Check their Instagram for irregular closing days.
fieldData.name: Te Cor Gentil

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒105-0001 Tokyo, Minato City, Toranomon, 5 Chome−8−1 麻布台ヒルズ ガーデンプラザA 2F
fieldData.meta-description: Classy vegan restaurant with beautifully presented food, located near Azabudai Hills
fieldData.description:
8ablish is a high-end vegan restaurant located near Azabudai Hills. The food here is beautifully presented and delicious, despite the relatively high price. Both dishes I tried are both solid - The baked soy bolognese penne gratin has a creamy sauce with a variety of colourful veggies and pasta. It's tasty but slightly under-seasoned. On the other hand, the Gateau au chocolate is beautifully shaped like a cacao bean, with strong decadent chocolate flavours.

‍

While indoor seating is limited, there are plenty of outdoor seating available with a quiet, pleasant ambiance. They also have a selection of baked goods that you can buy and take home.
fieldData.name: 8ablish

fieldData.address-text: 1 Chome-1-10 Yokokawa, Sumida City, Tokyo 130-0003, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Mostly vegan park cafe; organic veg, small affordable plates.
fieldData.description: Situated within Yokokawa Park, Sasaya Cafe offers a mostly vegan menu (honey products are sold in the shop, so double-check ingredients if concerned) in a relaxed setting. They serve tasty dishes featuring organic vegetables, like tempeh cutlets, curry, sandwiches, and daily specials, alongside drinks. It's known for being affordable and having friendly staff. However, be aware that meal portions are often described as small, more like snack-sized. The park location means it can sometimes be noisy with children, but it also offers a dog-friendly terrace. It's a pleasant, budget-friendly spot for a light bite or coffee break.
fieldData.name: Sasaya Cafe

fieldData.name-in-original-language: 浅草 鳩家 ヴィーガンフルーツサンド
fieldData.address-text: 2 Chome-3-3 Asakusa, Taito City, Tokyo 111-0032, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan fruit sandwiches takeaway place located near Senso-ji in Asakusa
fieldData.description:
Located conveniently near the popular Senso-ji Temple, Hatoya is a dedicated vegan shop specialising in Japanese fruit sandwiches (fruit sando). They use vegan whipped cream and bread, filling them with a variety of seasonal fruits like strawberries, pineapple and mandarin.

‍

The red bean paste and strawberry sandwich one I tried was delicious with light and creamy whipped cream, and sweet strawberries. They have a few seats located at the store for you to eat the sandwich there, but it's more of a takeaway place. Nonetheless, Hatoya is a great option to try out the trendy fruit sandwich at a convenient location.
fieldData.name: Hatoya’s Vegan Fruit Sandwiches

fieldData.address-text: 2 Chome-7-6 Nishiasakusa, Taito City, Tokyo 111-0035, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Cute vegan cafe near Kappabashi; cakes, coffee, light meals, GF.
fieldData.description: Shochiku-en is a cute, fully vegan cafe conveniently located right by Kappabashi street. It offers a nice selection of treats and light meals, including coffee with plant milk options, cakes (like their signature rainbow cake), muffins, nut tarts, steamed buns, small burgers, and pizza, with some gluten-free options available. While space is limited, it's a good spot for a coffee break or a light bite. Reviews highlight the delicious baked goods (mousse cake, rose cookies, muffins, tarts) and good coffee, though one diner found a burger slightly oily. It's a worthwhile stop for vegans exploring the Kappabashi area.
fieldData.name: Shochikuen Cafe

fieldData.name-in-original-language: まるごとVeganダイニング浅草
fieldData.address-text: 1 Chome-3-13 Hanakawado, Taito City, Tokyo 111-0033, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Cozy vegan cafe in Asakusa offering tempura, curry rice, waffles and more
fieldData.description:
Located next to the Sumida River, Marugoto Vegan Dining Asakusa (formerly The Farm Cafe) is a cozy vegan cafe that's walking distance from Senso-Ji Temple.

‍

They offer a variety of delicious options, including tempura, fried tempeh, curry, salads, and waffles. Go for the lunch plate, which features a mix of curry, tempura, and salad, if you want to try a bit of everything. I chose the tempura curry rice which includes a variety of veggies with a tasty curry sauce. Staff are warm and welcoming, and their handwritten menu has English translation.
fieldData.name: Marugoto Vegan Dining Asakusa

fieldData.address-text: 3 Chome-10-14 Kita-Aoyama, Minato City, Tokyo 107-0061, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: High quality vegan & GF fruit tart cafe in Omotesando and Yoyogi
fieldData.description:
So Tarte is a cute, cozy, fully vegan and gluten-free cafe in Omotesando and Yoyogi-Uehara. They specialise in beautifully decorated fruit tarts using seasonal produce. the seasonal white strawberry tart I tried remains one of my favourite desserts in Tokyo. The base was crunchy around the edges while chewy and buttery in the middle. The soy cream is fluffy, and the white strawberry is fragrant and subtly sweet.

‍

Other than their signature tarts, they may also offer other seasonal desserts like fruit parfait, as well as drinks like oat latte. The price is relatively high but I think the high quality tarts justify the price. Keep in mind that you're required to order a drink if you want to dine in.

‍

So Tarte has a sister cafe called Fruits & Season that's known for its vegan whipped cream fruit sandwiches, which is also located in Tokyo.
fieldData.name: So Tarte

fieldData.name-in-original-language: オスカー アメリカン チャイニーズ
fieldData.address-text: 2 Chome-36-15 Daita, Setagaya City, Tokyo 155-0033, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan eatery serving American-Chinese style food near Shimo-Kitazawa
fieldData.description:
Oscar brings the American-Chinese style takeaway experience to the vegan scene. Located just a 5-minute walk from Shimo-Kitazawa Station South exit, this fully vegan restaurant serves up classic dishes like General Tso's 'chicken', ornage chicken and mapo tofu. They offer set meals where you can pick a number of mains along with a rice or noodle dish and a drink. I chose a half-&-half and fried rice and fried noodles.

‍

The food is flavourful, well-seasoned, and offers good value with large portions for the price. The atmosphere is clean and bright, and staff are friendly and helpful. My only small complaint is that some dishes are not hot when served, but the staff is happy to heat them up for you if you need.
fieldData.name: Oscar America Chinese

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒153-0061 Tokyo, Meguro City, Nakameguro, 3 Chome−2−19 ラミアール中目黒
fieldData.meta-description: Tiny vegan spot; known for amazing falafel & vegan soft serve.
fieldData.description: Ballon is a tiny, fully vegan eatery near Nakameguro station, focused primarily on falafel and soft-serve ice cream. Their falafel, served in sandwiches or bowls, receives high praise for its exceptional flavour. They also offer tasty soups (like tomato) and salads. It's a great spot for a quick, delicious Israeli-inspired meal or a vegan soft serve treat. The main thing to keep in mind is the extremely limited seating – only about four small tables. While service is fast, portion sizes for meals are described as medium, so factor that in if you're very hungry. Check closing times as they vary slightly.
fieldData.name: Ballon

fieldData.name-in-original-language: プレマルシェ·ジェラテリア＆オルタナティブ·ジャンク
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒153-0051 Tokyo, Meguro City, Kamimeguro, 2 Chome−9−36 目黒銀座ビル1F
fieldData.meta-description: Gelato shop w/ huge variety of amazing vegan flavors; pricey
fieldData.description: For vegan gelato lovers, Premarché Gelateria near Nakameguro station is a must-visit. While not fully vegan, they boast a huge and impressive variety of high-quality vegan gelato flavors, including creative Japanese-inspired options (like shiso or fermented cheesecake) alongside rich classics like premium chocolate. Vegan cones are available. Staff are helpful, and you can often sample flavors if you ask. The gelato is considered among the best vegan versions in Tokyo by many. Just be prepared for the premium price tag. They also offer coffee (with soy milk option) and tea. Note the pay-first, get-ticket system for ordering.
fieldData.name: Premarché Gelateria & Alternative Junk

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0011 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Higashi, 3 Chome−25−3, Lions Plaza Ebisu, 1F
fieldData.meta-description: Cozy vegan health cafe near Ebisu; great pancakes & soy meat.
fieldData.description: Ko-So Cafe is a cute, fully vegan health food spot near Ebisu station with a cozy, albeit narrow, interior. The menu includes curries, pastas, risottos, salads, and standout dishes like flavourful pancakes and juicy, well-seasoned soy meat preparations. Desserts like tiramisu cake are also available. Staff are friendly and attentive. While the food is praised for being fresh and tasty, some diners find the portions a bit small for the price point, which can be slightly high. It's a lovely place for a healthy meal or coffee, especially if you're in the Ebisu area. Note: they are closed on Wednesdays.
fieldData.name: Ko-So Cafe

fieldData.name-in-original-language: アラスカ ツヴァイ
fieldData.address-text: 2 Chome-5-7 Higashiyama, Meguro City, Tokyo 153-0043, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Cozy vegan cafe; known for tofu katsu sandwich & set meals.
fieldData.description: Alaska Zwei is a cozy, fully vegan cafe with a great atmosphere and friendly staff, open from breakfast time. They offer satisfying set meals (like brown rice or curry plates), rice bowls, and filled bagels – the tofu katsu sandwich on focaccia is particularly popular and highly recommended. You can also find a selection of respectable pastries, cakes, and coffee. It's considered a favorite vegan spot in Tokyo by some reviewers due to the quality food and welcoming vibe. Keep in mind they close relatively early (6 pm), so it's not an option for dinner, and one visitor noted needing to purchase a drink.
fieldData.name: Alaska Zwei

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0034 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Daikanyamacho, 12−16 シンフォニー代官山 103
fieldData.meta-description: Fine vegan patisserie; exquisite cakes & amazing gelato; pricey.
fieldData.description: Premium SOW is a fully vegan fine bakery and patisserie specializing in exquisite French-style cakes, gelato, parfaits, cookies, and chocolates. The gelato, particularly flavors like tiramisu and pistachio, receives high praise for its rich taste, as do the various tarts. While the offerings are beautifully crafted and delicious, be prepared for high prices and potentially small portions, making it more suitable for special occasions or gifts. The space itself is very small, possibly standing-room only. Note that many items contain coconut, though some coconut-free options exist. Also, gelato "doubles" feature a smaller second scoop, and some flavors cost extra.
fieldData.name: Premium Sow

fieldData.meta-description: Health-focused cafe w/ vegan bowls/burgers in Midtown Hibiya.
fieldData.description: Located in the upscale Midtown Hibiya complex, Mr. Farmer is a health-oriented cafe serving American-style dishes with meat, but offering clearly marked vegan and gluten-free options. You can find satisfying vegan choices like Buddha bowls (the tofu comes recommended), wraps, burgers served with potato, and their popular locomoco bowl. They also offer smoothies, juices, and complimentary flavoured water. The interior is nice, service is fast, and ordering via QR code (in English) is convenient. While it's a good option for mixed groups in a fancy area, be aware that many find it quite pricey, and portion sizes might seem modest to some.
fieldData.name: Mr Farmer

fieldData.name-in-original-language: アインソフ　ジャーニー
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒160-0022 Tokyo, Shinjuku City, Shinjuku, 3 Chome−8−9 B1,1F,2F 新宿Ｑビル
fieldData.meta-description: Popular vegan spot for Japanese fusion dishes, including amazing fluffy pancakes.
fieldData.description:
The Shinjuku branch of the popular vegan restaurant chain - Ain Soph Journey - is conveniently located between Shinjuku Station and Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden. As the place is not particularly large and is a popular among tourists, you’re likely to have to wait if you're looking to fine during lunch and dinner hours; booking ahead might be a good idea.

‍

The food here is delicious and of high quality. They specialise in Japanese fusion dishes, though prices are on the more expensive side. If you have a sweet tooth, definitely try their signature 'heavenly' pancakes, which are soft, fluffy, and pretty "heavenly". They regularly have seasonal pancake flavours like strawberry pancakes in Spring, and chestnut ones in Autumn. Other than the pancake, they also serve some tasty, healthy savoury options, including teriyaki chick'n rice bowl, curry rice, pasta and more.
fieldData.name: Ain Soph Journey Tokyo

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ザ ヴィーガンマシュマロ
fieldData.address-text: 洋菓子エリア 銀座三越 地下2, 4 Chome-6-16 Ginza, Chuo City, Tokyo 104-0061, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Stunning vegan cakes & pastries in Ginza Mitsukoshi B2F; pricey.
fieldData.description: Situated in the B2F food hall of Ginza Mitsukoshi, The Vegan Marshmallooow is a fully vegan bakery renowned for its stunningly beautiful and delicious cakes, cookies, and pastries. They boast one of Japan's largest vegan bakery selections, including gluten-free options and popular items like their 'anime-perfect' strawberry cream cake. Everything is crafted with refined textures and flavours. While items are pricey (often over ¥1000), many find the quality justifies the cost. Service is friendly. Keep in mind it's a counter within a busy food hall, and there's no immediate seating – you can take your treats up to the 9th-floor terrace.
fieldData.name: the vegan marshmallooow

fieldData.meta-description: Convenient ramen in Tokyo Station w/ vegan options via machine.
fieldData.description: Conveniently located in Tokyo Station's busy Ramen Street (downstairs, before the ticket gates), Soranoiro Nippon serves meat but offers clearly marked vegan ramen options. Ordering is via an efficient ticket machine (menu mostly Japanese, but vegan options labeled in English). A vegan dandan ramen is available. However, reviews on the ramen itself are mixed; some find it a decent, quick option, while others report changes in recipe leading to a less impressive, potentially oily or overly spicy bowl with fewer toppings. Portions are generous. It's a viable spot if you need a quick vegan ramen fix right in the station, especially for mixed groups, but manage expectations regarding taste.
fieldData.name: Soranoiro

fieldData.address-text: 4 Chome-12-1 Ginza, Chuo City, Tokyo 104-0061, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Fine dining vegan Japanese fusion in Ginza; pricey, book ahead.
fieldData.description: Located in the upscale Ginza district, AIN SOPH.Ginza offers a fine dining, fully vegan experience across multiple floors. The ground floor features a patisserie and juice/smoothie cafe, while the upper floors house the restaurant serving beautifully presented Japanese fusion lunches, tea-time desserts, and dinners. Reservations are strongly recommended, often needed well in advance, and might be required to access the full menu, including options like elaborate bento boxes or pre-ordered sushi. While the food (including their famous pancakes) and service are excellent, be prepared for a significantly higher price point compared to other vegan spots or even other Ain Soph locations. It's best for a special occasion planned ahead.
fieldData.name: Ain Soph Ginza

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒170-0013 Tokyo, Toshima City, Higashiikebukuro, 3 Chome−5−7 ユニオンビルディング 101
fieldData.meta-description: Calm vegan Japanese fusion near Sunshine City; kids menu avail.
fieldData.description: Tucked away near Ikebukuro's Sunshine City, AIN SOPH.Soar provides a tranquil, fully vegan dining experience. This branch offers the brand's signature plant-based Japanese fusion meals, seasonal desserts, and friendly service in a cool, calm setting. Menu items like burgers and green curry have been enjoyed by visitors. While the desserts are tempting, be aware they, and the menu overall, can lean towards the expensive side. They offer a kids menu, making it family-friendly. It's a lovely escape from the city bustle, but it's wise to confirm their current opening hours before heading over, and note they are closed on Tuesdays.
fieldData.name: Ain Soph Soar

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ヘルシートウキョウ CBDショップ&カフェ
fieldData.address-text: B1, 3 Chome-30-13 Shinjuku, Shinjuku City, Tokyo 160-0022, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Small vegan cafe with quick-eat meals, desserts & products, with a focus on CBD oils.
fieldData.description:
This Shinjuku branch of HealthyTOKYO is a fully vegan cafe with a unique focus on CBD. Located conveniently on the B1 floor of Shinjuku Marui (Connected to Shinjuku-Sanchome Station A1 exit), it offers a range of plant-based meals like sandwiches, lasagna and quiche. For something sweet, expect to find cheesecake and chocolate cake.

‍

This Shinjuku branch is a good option if you're looking for breakfast as it opens earlier than other vegan options in the area. They also have branches in Harajuku, Daikanyama, and Haneda Airport.
fieldData.name: HealthyTOKYO CBD Shop & Cafe

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0042 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Udagawacho, 16−14 パティオⅠ １F
fieldData.meta-description: Organic-focused cafe near Shibuya with clearly marked vegan options
fieldData.description: Located near Shibuya Crossing, Bio Cafe combines a French bakery with a relaxed, organic-focused cafe. While it serves meat, there are clearly marked vegan options available on the English menu. You can find dishes like soy cheese carbonara and tofu steak mochi brown rice. The portion could be a bit small for the relatively high prices.
fieldData.name: Bio Cafe

fieldData.name-in-original-language: フタバフルーツパーラー
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒160-0022 Tokyo, Shinjuku City, Shinjuku, 3 Chome−30−13 マルイ本館 5F
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan-friendly dessert cafe located in Shinjuku Marui Department Store
fieldData.description:
Futaba Fruits Parlor, located on the 5th floor of Shinjuku Marui Department Store, is a spacious cafe primarily focused on fruit desserts. It's an omni restaurant with vegan options. The vegan options are marked with a "Happy Vegan" icon.

‍

For the parfait, you'll need to veganise it by swapping the ice cream to a vegan soy ice cream. They also have some vegan savoury options like curry rice.
fieldData.name: Futaba Fruits Parlor

fieldData.name-in-original-language: グリーン イタリアン トルチャ
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒160-0022 Tokyo, Shinjuku City, Shinjuku, 3 Chome−14−1 伊勢丹新宿本館 7F
fieldData.meta-description: A macrobiotic Italian high-end restaurant with vegan options
fieldData.description:
Located in a Shinjuku Isetan department store, Green Italian TORCIA is an upscale and classy Italian restaurant opened by the Chaya restaurant chain.

‍

The vegan options are marked clearly in the menu with some interesting options like '3 kinds of vegan roe soy carbonara' and the pomodoro sauce hamburg steak. The prices are on the higher side.

‍

As part of the Chaya chain, Green Italian TORCIA carries their great range of vegan desserts as well. Expect to find vegan mont blanc cake, strawberry cake and more. The seasonal cherry blossom cream cake I tried there was superb with layers of sakura chestnut puree, mochi and red bean paste.

gallery.alt: Vegan sea urchin and chicken pasta. Photo by @greenitalian_torcia

fieldData.name: Green Italian TORCIA

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ファラフェルブラザーズ
fieldData.meta-description: All vegan falafel shop that's budget-friendly and reliable. Has multiple locations in Tokyo
fieldData.description:
Falafel Brothers is a fully vegan chain in Tokyo with locations in Shibuya, Roppongi and Otemachi. Great option if you are looking for a hearty falafel pockets and other comfort food without breaking the bank.

‍

Their falafel bowls and sandwiches are customisable. You can choose from 5 different ‘styles’, for example, an Israeli style with hummus and tahini sauce, or the European variation with beets, sauerkraut, and tahini sauce.

‍

Beyond falafel, they serve a variety of international dishes like gyoza, pizza and desserts like ice cream cookie served in a mini skillet. The portion is generous at reasonable prices.
