fieldData.name: Falafel Brothers

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ザ リトル ベーカリー トーキョー
fieldData.address-text: 6 Chome-13-6 Jingumae, Shibuya City, Tokyo 150-0001, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Highly popular bakery with vegan donuts, cinnamon rolls & bread
fieldData.description:
A collaboration with Good Town Donuts, The Little Bakery Tokyo offers a range of vegan treats located just off ‘Cat Street’ in Harajuku.

‍

When available, you can find a good selection of fluffy vegan donuts (like matcha or passionfruit flavours), cinnamon rolls, baguettes, and other breads. They also serve oat milk lattes. However, the selection changes daily so there could be days with limited vegan options.

‍

There are some dine-in seatings available, but because of the popularity of the cafe, expect to get the baked good as takeaway.
fieldData.name: The Little BAKERY Tokyo

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ジカセイ メンショウ
fieldData.address-text: Shibuya PARCO B1F, 15−1 Udagawacho, Shibuya City, Tokyo
fieldData.meta-description: An omni ramen place in Shibuya Parco with multiple vegan options
fieldData.description:
Located in the PARCO food court (same level as Izakaya Masaka), Jikasei Mensho is a small, modern ramen shop that serves meat but offers several clearly marked vegan options, including miso ramen (spicy and non-spicy) and tantan ramen (with or without soup).

‍

The tantan ramen is a popular pick with a rich and creamy broth that's slightly spicy. Ordering is easy via a screen system (English options available), and service is quick.
fieldData.name: Jikasei Mensho

fieldData.address-text: 5 Chome-1-8 Jingumae, Shibuya City, Tokyo 150-0001, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Elegant vegan eatery in Omotesando serving aesthetic seasonal Japanese sets
fieldData.description:
Tucked away near Omotesando, Brown Rice is an upscale, fully vegan restaurant that offers a serene courtyard setting for enjoying their traditional Japanese lunch sets.

‍

Brown Rice focuses mainly on healthy, beautifully presented Japanese cuisine using macrobiotic principles. The menu features a small selection of delicious seasonal set meals that change regularly. If it's your first time here, try the lunch set with bamboo basket with steamed vegetables. Staff are attentive and helpful, and an English menu is available.

‍

It’s a great spot for a slow, aesthetically pleasing meal, but keep in mind it's quite pricey and the menu is rather small.
fieldData.name: Brown Rice Omotesando

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0001 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Jingumae, 5 Chome−11−13 茶庵表参道 1階
fieldData.meta-description: Cute vegan Japanese cafe with Japanese desserts and a resident cat
fieldData.description:
Tucked away in an alleyway in the busy Harajuku, Cafe Chairo is a cozy, fully vegan Japanese cafe offers unique Japanese desserts with Instagrammable interior and traditional floor seating.

‍

They specialiee in teas and unique Japanese-inspired sweets like mochi, muffins, and more. I tried the matcha red bean muffin which is as photogenic as it is tasty. They have an English menu and English-speaking staff. It's a small, intimate space, so it might not be ideal for groups or families with young children due to the limited seating and floor arrangement.

‍

Be sure to say hi to the resident cat, Koyane-chan, if you visit. But also keep in mind that there is a fish tank, which is not expected for a vegan cafe.
fieldData.name: Cafe Chairo

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒107-0062 Tokyo, Minato City, Minamiaoyama, 5 Chome−10−2 第２九曜ビル 1F
fieldData.meta-description: Healthy vegan salads, bowls & smoothies with limited seating
fieldData.description:
THE_B is a small but fully vegan spot near Omotesando station, and it's a great stop if you are looking for something healthy for your trip.

‍

The menu primarily features a variety of salads (including a unique nato option), bowls like tasty acai bowls, smoothies, and soups. They also offer house-made vegan cheese, cheesecakes, and cookies.

‍

Keep in mind that seating is very limited – there are only about four seats available, making it mostly suitable for takeaway food.
fieldData.name: THE_B

fieldData.address-text: 565 Old Cleveland Rd, Camp Hill QLD 4152
fieldData.meta-description: Cute, pink, fully vegan bakery in Camp Hill
fieldData.description:
If you want to satisfy your vegan sweet tooth at a super cute bakery, Pippa's Pantry should be your next destination.

‍

The pastries and desserts taste great. You can expect to find a variety of cupcakes, croissants, savoury options and more. My personal favourite is her iced vovo cookie and crookie (cookie croissant).

‍

She's open on Fridays and Saturdays at the time of writing. Other than this Camp Hill location, you can also find her baked goods at QLD vegan markets and various Westfield shopping centre popups.
fieldData.name: Pippa's Pantry

fieldData.meta-description: High quality Asian eatery that will wow vegans and impress any non-vegan you bring along
fieldData.description:
It’s well worth making your way up Northcote to visit Brother Bon. This high-quality pan-Asian restaurant has an impressive menu covering multiple cuisines. Usually, when a restaurant tries to do everything, they end up mastering nothing, but Brother Bon completely defies that rule.

‍

I ordered a spread to sample their range: Meaty pork and Napa cabbage dumplings, lemon chicken, wagyu beef nigiri, and special egg fried rice made with tofu scramble. This meal was an absolute perfection from start to finish with so many highlights: The meaty-ness of the pork dumplings, the crispy chicken pieces with bright lemon sauce, and that nostalgic feeling from having egg fried rice again. These dishes were on par with the best non-vegan versions I grew up eating in Hong Kong.

‍

Drinks and desserts are equally amazing. The pistachio praline cold foam matcha was as amazing as it sounded. I finished the meal by sampling their ube and black sesame gelatos, both creamy and flavourful.

‍

Honestly, this is one of the highest-quality Asian restaurants in Australia, and it will easily wow vegans and impress any non-vegan you bring along.
fieldData.name: Brother Bon

fieldData.meta-description: A St Kilda vegetarian restaurant featuring international flavours with many vegan options
fieldData.description: Sister of Soul is a vegetarian restaurant located in St Kilda, offering menus with mostly vegan options. You can expect to find a mix of international flavours, with items like okonomiyaki, nasi goreng, burgers, and various bowls. They also have a separate breakfast menu with more western dishes. With the relaxing atmosphere and friendly staff, it’s a great destination for anyone visiting St Kilda.
fieldData.name: Sister of Soul

fieldData.meta-description: This Avondale Heights vegan cafe offers classic comfort food and many gluten-free choices
fieldData.description: Particle Cafe is a vegan cafe in Avondale Heights. Everything is vegan with many gluten free options. Expect to find classic cafe comfort food like scrambled tofu toast, BLT sandwich and schnitzel jackfruit burger. They also have a range of salad, smoothie bowls and smoothies for those who’s looking for something healthier.
fieldData.name: Particle Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan-friendly sushi train restaurant with a fun delivery system and an upscale Kaiseki option
fieldData.description: If you’re like me, you probably have hoped for a vegan friendly sushi train restaurant before. Luckily, Midori By Tao's may just be what you’ve been looking for. This vegetarian sushi train restaurant where most of the offerings are vegan, and the items containing egg or dairy are clearly marked. They offer a wide variety of sushi rolls as well as a separate hot food menu with dishes like laksa and ramen, which can be ordered via QR code and delivered by a little electric train. They also offer a more upscale vegan Kaiseki (multi-course Japanese tasting menu) experience upstairs.
fieldData.name: Midori By Tao's

fieldData.address-text: 225 Melville Rd, Pascoe Vale South VIC 3044
fieldData.name: Shop225 Pizzeria

fieldData.meta-description: Fitzroy's popular vegetarian cafe has a large, diverse menu that is mostly vegan
fieldData.description: Vegie Bar is a long-standing and popular vegetarian cafe in Fitzroy. It's known for its large, diverse menu that includes curries, pizzas, burgers, noodles, and salads. The menu is vegan by default with optional dairy for some dishes. Portions are generally generous, and it’s often busy. It's a reliable choice for a casual meal in the Fitzroy area.
fieldData.name: Vegie Bar

fieldData.meta-description: A refined all-vegan dining experience at Collingwood
fieldData.description:
For a unique and elevated vegan dining experience, SHU in Collingwood is an amazing option. While they offer a 10-course vegan tasting menu on weekdays, I visited on the weekend specifically for their unlimited plant-based yum cha, and I was very impressed.

‍

The concept is great: They bring you one of all 10 yum cha dishes first, giving you a chance to sample the wide variety of flavours and textures. The menu ranges from perfectly executed classics like pan-fried dumplings to highly creative twists, like a chewy steamed bun made with chickpeas, and beetroot-filled spring rolls. There are no "filler" dishes here. After you finish the initial dishes, you simply order more of whatever you loved most. You can also add on extras, like bottomless drinks or their delicious vegan cannoli dessert.
fieldData.name: Shu

fieldData.meta-description: A 100% vegan South Yarra cafe focusing on healthy bowls, smoothies, and toasties; ideal for takeaway
fieldData.description: Jumi's Cafe is a 100% vegan cafe, with a focus on healthy options like acai bowls, smoothies, wraps, salads, and loaded toasties. They also offer some vegan pantry staples and deli items. It's a good spot for a takeaway or a casual, quick meal, with limited seating.
fieldData.name: Jumi's Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: This Windsor vegan bar and restaurant serves mock meat-heavy Asian and Western comfort food
fieldData.description:
(Tyranny of Distance is no longer vegan and now serving meat)

Tyranny of Distance in Windsor is a fully vegan bar and restaurant. The menu features mock meat-heavy, southeast-Asian inspired dishes like duck roti rolls, massaman chicken curry, as well as western comfort food like arancini and KFC burger. It has a energetic vibe and a large semi-outdoor area.
fieldData.name: Tyranny of Distance

fieldData.meta-description: A CBD laneway vegan cafe specialising in creative sweet and savoury jaffles for a quick bite
fieldData.description: Union Kiosk is a small, hole-in-the-wall style, all-vegan cafe in a CBD laneway, specialising in a wide variety of jaffles (toasted sandwiches). They offer both savoury and sweet jaffles with creative fillings, alongside coffee and other vegan treats like pastries. I tried the Korean beef kimchi gochujang mayo one and it was flavourful and delicious. It’s a popular spot for a quick and affordable vegan meal or snack in the Melbourne CBD.
fieldData.name: Union Kiosk

fieldData.meta-description: An authentic and affordable Mexican restaurant that doesn't compromise on taste
fieldData.description:
Trippy Taco serves up some comforting, cheap, and flavourful Mexican street food. It’s a vegetarian joint, but almost everything on the menu can be made vegan. Just be sure to specifically ask for it when ordering.

‍

I ordered the tofu asada taco (asking for vegan gets you scrambled tofu and vegan cheese) and the Sabrocito breakfast burrito. The burrito was the winner for me: Perfectly saucy, satisfying, and bursting with flavours. The taco was also packed to the brim with fillings, though I personally felt it could have benefited from a dollop of vegan sour cream or mayo to tie it all together. It's a fantastic, no-frills spot for an affordable vegan meal that doesn't compromise on quality.
fieldData.name: Trippy Taco

fieldData.meta-description: An all-vegan fast-food chain offering plant-based burgers, hot dogs, nuggets, and signature fries
fieldData.description: Lord of the Fries is a fast-food chain that is entirely vegan. They offer the classic veganised fast food including burgers, hot dogs, nuggets, and their signature fries with a huge array of different sauces. Try the 'Biggie' burger which is their version of a Big Mac, and get a cookies and cream milkshake to complete your meal.
fieldData.name: Lord of the Fries

fieldData.meta-description: Collingwood's iconic vegan restaurant known for innovative Mediterranean food and a cool vibe
fieldData.description: Smith & Daughters is a well-known, entirely vegan restaurant in Collingwood, from chef Shannon Martinez. It has a reputation for innovative and flavourful plant-based food, often with a Mediterranean or Spanish influence, that aims to impress both vegans and meat-eaters. The decor has a cool and somewhat a rock 'n' roll vibe, which is great for a more special occasion or an indulgent meal. They also have a related deli, Smith & Deli.
fieldData.name: Smith & Daughters

fieldData.meta-description: This Carlton vegan pub serves plant-based pub classics and craft beers in a relaxed, retro setting
fieldData.description:
If you’re craving a classic Aussie pub experience but want it entirely vegan, look no further than Green Man’s Arms in Carlton. It has all the charm of a traditional Aussie pub, but with a fully vegan menu.

‍

I had to try their eggplant parma. It came in a great portion, featuring perfectly soft eggplant encased in a crispy shell, generously topped with Napoli sauce and vegan cheese. The side salad was a little on the oily side, but overall an amazing dish. I also tried the calamari, which was made from king oyster mushrooms. It was super flavourful, and paired with a creamy tofu aioli.

‍

However, the absolute highlight of this meal was their basque cheesecake. I cannot recommend this dessert highly enough. The texture and flavour were both phenomenal. It had a substantial, creamy cheesecake body with a brulee'd crispy top. Paired with the biscuity base and bright lemon curd, this dessert is the perfect end of a pub feast.
fieldData.name: Green Man's Arms Bar and Restaurant

fieldData.meta-description: A Mediterranean wine bar in the CBD with a vegetarian menu; needs to inquire for vegan options
fieldData.description: Patsy's is a Mediterranean-inspired wine bar and restaurant. The menu is vegetarian but the vegan options are not clearly marked on the menu, so you'd need to check with the staff for details. The focus is on wine, and all the wines are vegan-friendly. The prices are on the higher side.
fieldData.name: Patsy's Melborne

fieldData.meta-description: 100% vegan cafe with a diverse menu in Burleigh Waters
fieldData.description: Doko Demo V is a 100% vegan cafe in Burleigh Waters on the Gold Coast. Its menu is diverse with Southeast-Asian dishes like Pad Thai and Okonomiyaki to Western favourites such as burgers, pizzas, and pasta. Popular dishes include their Taipei 101 burger, fish and chips, and the sizzling Mongolian beef. The food quality is good with big portions.The vibe is relaxed with Bali-inspired bamboo and greenery decor.
fieldData.name: Doko Demo V

fieldData.meta-description: Marrickville spot for veg & vegan Napoli-style sourdough pizza
fieldData.description: Pizza Madre in Marrickville is a popular, easygoing spot specialising in vegetarian, Napoli-style sourdough pizza with a tasty pizza crust. Run by the team behind Two Chaps cafe, they offer an authentic wood-fired pizza experience. The menu changes periodically (often monthly), with almost all pizzas can be made vegan using their house-made, melty vegan mozzarella. All their natural wines are vegan too. It's a small, bustling restaurant. Be aware that outside seating can be noisy due to traffic.
fieldData.name: Pizza Madre

fieldData.meta-description: Fully vegan & gluten-free Mexican dishes & cocktails in Darlinghurst
fieldData.description: Bad Hombres is a popular vegan and gluten-free serving Mexican cuisine. The menu focuses on shareable plates perfect for groups. Standout recommendations often include the flavourful, generously portioned cauliflower dish and the Birria mushroom tacos. Other popular choices include their 'fish' tacos and the unique miso eggplant tacos. For something sweet, go for the creme brulee for dessert. They also offer creative cocktails. While the food is good, some may find the flavour less bright than traditional Mexican fare, and the prices could be on the expensive side.
fieldData.name: Bad Hombres

fieldData.meta-description: Upscale vegan restaurant serving seasonal tasting menus, perfect for special occasions
fieldData.description: Yellow is an upscale, fully vegan restaurant and bar in Potts Point, highly regarded for its exceptional dining experience. It currently offers a seasonal 6-course tasting menu, known for creative and beautifully presented dishes that impress even non-vegans with their rich flavours and textures. Optional wine pairing is available. The atmosphere is sophisticated which makes it perfect for a special occasion. Given its popularity, booking ahead is recommended.
fieldData.name: Yellow

fieldData.address-text: Shop 4/241 Commonwealth St, Surry Hills NSW 2010
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan deli cafe serving classic cafe dishes like omelettes and toasties, has house-made vegan meats
fieldData.description:
Shift Eatery is a fully vegan deli cafe in Surry Hills, particularly known for making its own vegan meats, cheeses, and sauces in-house. The menu covers familiar cafe favourites, offering all-day breakfast options like omelettes and pancakes, alongside a variety of sandwiches, toasties, salads, and bowls.

‍

Try their crispy 'chicken' burger and flavourful vegan omelette. They also serve smoothies, coffee, and display sweet treats in their cabinet. The vibe is friendly and unfussy, typical of a neighbourhood spot, though the cafe itself is small with limited seating. It's a reliable choice for a casual meal, takeaway, or delivery. You can also purchase their house-made deli products and other vegan groceries to take home.
fieldData.name: Shift Eatery

fieldData.meta-description: Popular spot for affordable, classic vegan Chinese with faux meats
fieldData.description: Located a short walk from Redfern station, Tian Ci Vegan serves an impressive range of affordable, vegan Chinese dishes. They create traditional Chinese dishes with vegan meat, making it a go-to for those craving classics like Mongolian 'beef' or sweet and sour 'pork'. Popular recommendations also include the crispy deep-fried mushrooms and the authentic-tasting 'chicken'. While the setting isn't overly fancy, the service is notably friendly and good value. The restaurant has a large space and courtyard seatings, though it's worth noting they may sometimes focus primarily on takeaway which means a bit of a wait for food.
fieldData.name: Tian Ci Vegan

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan version of McDonald's with nostalgic burgers and fries
fieldData.description: Mr. Charlie's serves up an entirely vegan menu designed to replicate the classic McDonald's experience. If you're missing Macca's flavours, this is your spot. Expect familiar favourites like burgers that closely mimic the taste and sauciness of the originals, alongside crispy fries and vegan nuggets. The flavours are pretty close to the non-vegan counterpart, making it pretty nostalgia. The vegan "Big Mac" is a popular choice here. Just be prepared for prices that are higher than typical fast food. Also note that side sauces come in small portions and cost extra.
fieldData.name: Mr Charlie's

fieldData.address-text: Shop 13/166-174 Military Rd, Neutral Bay NSW 2089
fieldData.name: Green Sprouts Vegetarian

fieldData.meta-description: Fully vegan Mexican street food & cocktails in Newtown. Also provides good value set menu
fieldData.description:
Vandal offers a fully vegan take on Southern California-inspired street food from its cool, industrial-style space in Newtown. It's particularly popular for its creative tacos – standouts often include the popcorn prawn taco and the flavourful chorizo smash taco. Other recommended bites are the unique cheeseburger spring rolls and the mushroom quesadilla.

‍

Vandal is also known for their good value, check out their Taco Tuesday ($4 tacos) or the $38 set menu which provides a broad taste of their offerings. They also serve cocktails. The venue gets quite busy, especially on weekends, so booking ahead is recommended. Be aware there's a Sunday surcharge and service might slow down during peak times.
fieldData.name: Vandal Taqueria

fieldData.meta-description: Popular vegan spot for Asian yum cha, noodles, mains & desserts.
fieldData.description: Green Gourmet Vegan is a long-standing, fully vegan favourite in St Leonards, offering a wide array of Asian cuisine. This popular spot features everything from yum cha and noodle dishes to stir-fries and an impressive selection of vegan cakes and desserts. Recommendations include their 'prawn' dumplings and carrot cake during yum cha, alongside flavourful mains like Sichuan cauliflower and laksa. The food is overall well-made, but some may find the yum cha variety limited. Previously, they did pay-by-weight lunch buffet but have stopped doing that recently.
fieldData.name: Green Gourmet

fieldData.meta-description: Authentic & creative vegan Thai food with chic interior in Enmore
fieldData.description:
Little Turtle is a popular all-vegan Thai eatery in Enmore, loved for its health-conscious cooking and chic industrial-chic atmosphere. Rather than using faux meats, the kitchen focuses on using tofu and vegetables to deliver authentic Thai flavours in beautifully presented dishes.

‍

Standouts often include the Pad See Ew and green curry fried rice, though some diners note the curries can lean slightly sweeter. Little Turtle has multiple dining areas, including a charming outdoor terrace decorated with fairy lights. It's also a BYO restaurant. Expect friendly, efficient service, but be mindful that parking nearby can be challenging as it's located on a main road.
fieldData.name: Little Turtle

fieldData.meta-description: Fully vegan Marrickville bakery & cafe known for creative and delicious pastries
fieldData.description:
Miss Sina is a popular, fully vegan bakery and restaurant that has been delighting Marrickville locals and visitors since September 2022.Tucked away in a quiet spot, it's known for its incredibly creative menu and warm, friendly service.

‍

They offer an all-day brunch menu featuring innovative dishes like miso butter cabbage and corn agnolotti, alongside sandwiches and breakfast platters. However, the baked goods are true highlights, with German-inspired pastries, cakes, fluffy donuts, famous cinnamon scrolls, and savoury options like vegan sausage rolls often stealing the show. It's a busy spot, especially for baked goods like crookies and kunefe which can sell out, so arriving early or booking for meals is recommended. Keep an eye on their social media for specials.
fieldData.name: Miss Sina

fieldData.meta-description: Hearty vegan pies, mash, gravy & homemade sweet treats near Bondi Beach
fieldData.description:
Funky Pies is a vegan gem, walking distance from the famous Bondi Beach, which makes it a perfect spot for vegans travelling there. They specialises in chunky, handmade pies – all vegan, with gluten-free options available for some popular choices like the Funky Chunky and Moroccan Tangine. They serve your pie traditionally with mash, gravy, and peas, or opt for a side salad.

‍

Beyond pies, you may also find some cakes, cupcakes, and banana bread on-site and serve organic fairtrade coffee (with Bonsoy), juices, and vegan shakes. It’s a great spot to refuel after hitting the beach or the Coogee-Bondi walk. They also have a small selection of vegan groceries to take home.
fieldData.name: Funky Pies

fieldData.meta-description: Creperie with a dedicated vegan menu for sweet & savoury options in South Brisbane
fieldData.description: Miss Claude offers both sweet and savoury crepes in their separate vegan menu. Sweet crepes include classics like strawberry jam, raspberry coulis, or simple lemon & sugar, with vegan coconut ice cream available. For a savoury option, try the 'Vegatouille' featuring a hearty vegetable casserole, but you'll have to add extra if you want vegan cheese with it. While the quality is decent, the crepes can feel a bit pricey for the portion size.
fieldData.name: Miss Claude Crepes

fieldData.meta-description: Popular local spot for stunning vegan açai bowls, smoothies & cabinet desserts
fieldData.description: A local favourite for açai bowls and smoothies, Insane Acai Bar crafts beautifully presented bowls brimming with seasonal fresh fruits. The delicious peanut butter jelly bowl is a favourite of mine. Beyond the bowls, you'll find a cabinet filled with vegan-friendly desserts and treats.
fieldData.name: Insane Acai Bar

fieldData.meta-description: Southeast Asian restaurant chain with options like satay stir-fry, Singapore noodles & spring rolls
fieldData.description: Serving Southeast Asian flavours, P'Nut Asian Kitchen is a restaurant chain that provides vegan options. Some of the stir-fries like satay or teriyaki can be made vegan by choosing the vegetable base. You can also consider adding extra tofu in the stir-fry. Other vegan-friendly options include Singapore noodles (pick the vegetable base) and vegetable spring rolls.
fieldData.name: P'Nut Asian Kitchen

fieldData.address-text: Tenancy 2 Ulster Lane, 211 Elizabeth St, Brisbane City QLD 4000
fieldData.meta-description: Poke bowl chain with vegan-friendly tofu & mushroom vegan bowls, but the fish smell could be a lot
fieldData.description:
This poke bowl chain offers a couple of solid vegan options built around either tofu or mushrooms, both packed with a variety of healthy, whole-food ingredients. While primarily focused on fish, they also have tacos that can be made vegan by requesting no mayo and by choosing tofu or mushroom as the protein. Be aware that due to the fish-heavy menu, the smell can be quite strong if you sit inside the restaurant.

‍
fieldData.name: Cheeky Poke

fieldData.meta-description: Colourful smoothie bowl specialis. All bowls are vegan except some use honey
fieldData.description:
Located in West Village shopping centre, Nautical Bowls specialises in colourful smoothie bowls and açai bowls. Almost all the bowls are vegan, but double check as some uses honey as a topping. Apart from their bowls being colourful and refreshing, a feature I love about them is their nut butter machine, which makes freshly ground nut butter for the bowls.

‍
fieldData.name: Nautical Bowls

fieldData.meta-description: Relaxing Vietnamese cafe near Toowong Village offering vegan banh mi & acai bowl options
fieldData.description: This relaxing Vietnamese cafe near Toowong Village offers a few clearly marked vegan options. While the options are rather limited, the vegan duck banh mi I tried is fresh and tasty. The other vegan option is their house-made granola açai bowls.
fieldData.name: Coffee Stories

fieldData.meta-description: Teneriffe coffee shop that carries a unique vegan cold brew soft serve ice cream
fieldData.description: Primarily a coffee shop in Teneriffe, The Woolshed isn't overtly vegan-focused on its food menu. However, it's worth knowing they stock a vegan-friendly cold brew soft serve ice cream, which is a surprising find.
fieldData.name: The Woolshed

fieldData.meta-description: Northside Thai restaurant featuring a dedicated menu of vegan classics
fieldData.description:
A good vegan option for Brisbane's Northside near North Lakes, Vegan Thai-riffic isn't a fully vegan restaurant as you may expect, but a separate vegan menu within an omni Thai restaurant.

‍

Expect classic Thai dishes like massaman curry, pad see ew, tom yum, and satay skewers. Overall, the flavours are enjoyable, with the pad see ew being particularly good, though the curry is too sweet for me.
fieldData.name: Vegan Thai-riffic

fieldData.address-text: Archie Am Pm Opposite the Dentist and Pathology, Shop 23/735 Beams Rd, Carseldine QLD 4034
fieldData.description: Fully vegan restaurant owned by chef/cookbook author Zacchary Bird and Vegood in Brisbane. Coffee & global inspired drinks on tap, vegan eats and treats. NOTE: Open as an event space without main hours - check socials for pop up dates. Open Tue 9:00am-10:00am.
fieldData.name: Archie AM PM

fieldData.meta-description: Japanese chain restaurant with clearly marked plant-based ramen & donburi
fieldData.description:
Motto Motto has two main vegan offerings - the teriyaki tofu rice bowl and the miso ramen (the tofu curry rice has dairy and is not vegan).

‍

I had the teriyaki tofu donburi $16, and it was pretty delicious, though I was surprised of its small size. It comes with four pieces of tofu that have a great smooth texture, served over rice with seaweed, edamame, pickles and more.

‍

At the time of writing, they are doing a buy one get one free for the vegan miso ramen on every Monday.

‍

For sides, the vegetable and chive gyoza is vegan-friendly, and I also love their peach or lychee iced tea.
fieldData.name: Motto Motto

fieldData.meta-description: A convenient healthy cafe chain for vibrant, vegan-friendly smoothie bowls
fieldData.description:
Coco Bliss hits the mark if you're looking for a healthy smoothie bowl fix in Brisbane. I really enjoy the decadent Ferrero smoothie bowl which is vegan-friendly and has rich choc fudge sauce and hazelnut crunch. All their smoothie and protein bowls are vegan-friendly, but do double-checking that your chosen granola topping is honey-free.

‍

While they offer some hot savoury items like vegan cheese toasties and falafel bowls, they don't stand out as much as the smoothie bowls. For example, the falafel bowl is a bit on the bland side in terms of flavours. Be sure to check carefully when ordering savoury options, as Coco Bliss also serves meat. You'll find several branches across the city, including handy locations within Chermside and Carindale Westfield shopping centres.
fieldData.name: Coco Bliss

fieldData.meta-description: Popular CBD alleyway cafe with marked vegan options. Good food despite higher price.
fieldData.description:
Felix for Goodness is a popular cafe tucked away in Brisbane CBD's Burnett Lane, known for its relaxed, urban vibe. It gets quite busy during lunch, and the tables are fairly close together.

‍

The menu changes regularly and features clearly marked vegan (VG) and vegan-possible (VGO) options – just keep in mind that substitutions may not be available for VGO dishes. While some may find it on the expensive side, the food is tasty. I've tried the surprisingly delicious vegan tuna bruschetta, which uses chickpeas with seaweed as the 'tuna', alongside fried tofu, roasted tomatoes, and standout pickled cucumber. Other options include cafe classics like granola or falafel bowls. Service is typically swift and friendly, though you have to order at the counter.
fieldData.name: Felix For Goodness

fieldData.address-text: shop2B/131 Elizabeth St, Brisbane City QLD 4000
fieldData.meta-description: Japanese takeaway spot with vegan-friendly sorbet, drinks, warabimochi & onigiri options
fieldData.description:
This Japanese takeaway shop offers a curated selection of vegan-friendly snacks and desserts. At the time of visiting, vegan sorbet options included strawberry, and lemon & yuzu, which can be wrapped in mochi skin for a unique 'daifuku' ice cream.

‍

Non-dairy milk is available (extra charge) for drinks like matcha and hojicha, but note that the strawberry range is not vegan as the powder they use has dairy.

‍

Also look out for warabimochi (soft mochi coated in soybean or matcha powder, though pricey) and three vegan onigiri: takana (pickled mustard green), wakame seaweed, and umeboshi (salted plum).
fieldData.name: Shiro Gelato & Snack Brisbane

fieldData.meta-description: A Brisbane CBD spot with great vegan-friendly doughnut options including custard and 'new-tella'
fieldData.description:
Tucked in the Post Office Square food court in Brisbane CBD, Happy Dough offers quite a good variety of vegan-friendly doughnuts.

‍

Their base cinnamon doughnut is both vegan and gluten-free. Other than that, you'll find a good range of vegan-friendly glazed doughnut options, with tempting flavours like vegan caramel, custard, and 'new-tella'.
fieldData.name: Happy Dough

fieldData.meta-description: Gelato chain with some decent vegan flavours
fieldData.description: Gelato chain with vegan flavours that include: mango, raspberry, 96% sugar free chocolate and more. The vegan flavours are marked clearly with a green "Vegan Friendly" sign. The cones are vegan-friendly as well.
fieldData.name: Gelatissimo

fieldData.address-text: Shop TR-06, 111 Boundary Street, West Village Retail, West End QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: Cafe specialising in Hungarian kurtosh chimney cakes. Freshly-made and vegan-options are available
fieldData.description:
This cafe specialises in Kürtősh, a Hungarian pastry (chimney cake) that's soft and bread-y inside, and crispy and caramelised outside. All the options with nut toppings (pistachio, hazelnut) are vegan. My two go-to's are the cinnamon kurtosh and the filled biscoff kurtosh (note: the Nutella one is not vegan). They may also have some other vegan treats like choc chip cookies, depending on the day.

‍

Keep in mind if you visit, because the kurtosh is freshly made and not all staff knows how to do it, sometimes they are not available; I've had a few misses in weekday afternoons.

‍
fieldData.name: Kurtosh

fieldData.meta-description: Milton pizzeria famous for their metre-long pizzas & great vegan options
fieldData.description:
This Milton pizzeria caters to vegans as well as meat eaters. They have dedicated and extensive sections of vegan options on their menu.

‍

Pizzas here are rectangular-shaped, and are available in 25cm, 50cm, or impressive metre-long sizes. The vegan pizzas come with vegan cheese without extra charge. Try the Mediterranean (sun-dried tomatoes, capers, olives) or the Funghi (mixed mushrooms, truffle oil, optional vegan bacon). The vegan carbonara is creamy and generously portioned, but the flavour is mild with a lack of vegan bacon in the pasta. If you are looking for something sweet after, go for their vegan sundae with gelato options including chocolate and hazelnut.
fieldData.name: Arrivederci Pizzeria

fieldData.meta-description: Famous gelato chain where all sorbets (and sometimes specials) are vegan
fieldData.description:
A popular gelato chain across Australia, Messina is known for their good quality gelato options. In Brisbane, you'll find Messina in South Brisbane and on James Street in Fortitude Valley.

‍

Their extensive sorbet options are all vegan, as well as the cones. My favourites are the sweet creamy pandan & coconut, or the tropical salted coconut & mango sorbet. Sometimes they have sorbet specials as well (check their socials for details). If you're visiting after dinner, be prepared for a bit of wait as the queue is often very long.

‍
fieldData.name: Gelato Messina

fieldData.meta-description: Popular West End gelateria with tasty and clearly marked vegan sorbet flavours
fieldData.description:
Located in West End's West Village, this popular gelateria often draws long queues after dinner.

‍

All sorbet options are clearly marked as vegan, including the surprisingly creamy and rich cookie sorbet packed with Oreo bites. About 30-40% of the offerings are vegan-friendly. Staff is happy to offer samples to help you choose. The cones are vegan-friendly too.
fieldData.name: Anita Gelato

fieldData.meta-description: Takeaway salad shop offering fresh, hearty salads. Most options are vegan-friendly
fieldData.description:
Specialising in fresh, hearty takeaway salads, Botanica has several Brisbane locations. While the salads are not marked, the staff are knowledgeable and can guide you in choosing the vegan ones. Often most salads on offer are vegan.

‍

The salads are delicious and nourishing. I particular like the potato & pea, freekeh & eggplant, or the Cypriot grain salad. The portion is also pretty generous. Keep an eye out for their occasional vegan chocolate brownie too.
fieldData.name: Botanica Real Food

fieldData.address-text: Shop 1/70 Kedron Brook Rd, Wilston QLD 4051
fieldData.description: Serves meat, vegan options available. Pizzeria that has a separate vegan menu with vegan antipasti, sides, 7 vegan pizzas, 4 vegan pastas and mains. Catering available. Relocated from 26 Gray St and previously called Pizzantica. Open Wed-Thu 5:00pm-9:00pm, Fri 12:00pm-2:30pm, Fri-Sat 4:30pm-9:30pm, Sun 4:30pm-9:00pm. Closed Mon.
fieldData.name: Antica

fieldData.address-text: shop 3/171 George St, Brisbane City QLD 4000
fieldData.meta-description: Upscale Chinese restaurant in Brisbane with a vegan banquet
fieldData.description: Donna Chang is an upscale Chinese restaurant housed in an impressive old bank building in Brisbane, with high ceilings and elegant decor. For vegans, the main menu have a decent amount of vegan dishes to pick from, including options like dan dan noodles and dumplings. They also have a vegan banquet (about $130 per person) if you want to try a bit of everything.
fieldData.name: Donna Chang

fieldData.meta-description: Upscale restaurant with vegan degustation menu that changes monthly
fieldData.description: Rogue Bistro, located in Newstead, is a modern, upscale dining spot with a moody, all-black interior. For vegans, the main offering is a dedicated multi-course vegan degustation menu, which changes monthly to reflect seasonal produce. Past vegan dishes include koji-roasted sweet potato gratin, Warrigal greens gnocchi ripieni, bruleed basque cheesecake. The price for this vegan degustation is on the higher side at about $120 per person.
fieldData.name: Rogue Bistro

fieldData.address-text: ANZAC Square, shop 1/241 Adelaide St, Brisbane City QLD 4000
fieldData.meta-description: All-vegan CBD spot with a hot food counter offering curries, lasagna & more
fieldData.description:
A convenient spot for vegans in Brisbane's CBD, this all-vegan spot offers a satisfying hot food counter experience.

‍

When you enter, go to the back of the store to select from a rotating array of curries, daal, pakora, vegan lasagne, and more – the Thai green curry and stroganoff are my favourites when available. Beyond the rice-and-dish combos, you can also find dosa, burgers, and salads. While they also have vegan cakes and desserts, their texture can lean towards 'jelly-like' rather than creamy.
fieldData.name: Vege Rama

fieldData.description: Pop-up-turned restaurant serving plant based Mexican street food. Makes its own corn and flour tortillas. Instagram: @elplantamexican Open Tue-Thu 5:30pm-8:30pm, Fri-Sat 5:30pm-9:00pm.
fieldData.name: El Planta

fieldData.meta-description: Hearty, affordable vegan Indian option in Brisbane CBD
fieldData.description:
Conveniently located in the city, Govinda's offers hearty vegetarian and vegan dishes. The staff is knowledgeable and can point out which dishes are vegan and which ones are not.

‍

Portions here are generous. You can choose from various 'feasts', ranging from a simple rice and curry combo of the 'small feast', to a large plate with kofta, chutney, and salad when you order the 'large feast'. You can also request some free poppadums. While the taste won't wow you, Govinda's is still a reliable choice for a satisfying and filling meal.
fieldData.name: Govinda's Brisbane CBD

fieldData.meta-description: Gold Coast vegan cafe serving inventive brunch classics & tasty desserts
fieldData.description:
This vegan cafe located at South Port, Gold Coast, serves up some satisfying and beautiful dishes. All their dishes are so colourful and beautifully presented (taste great as well), including the coconut pancakes that comes with a date caramel sauce and coconut ice cream, and the healthier smoothie bowl which is just so beautifully put together.

‍

But one thing that stood out the most to me is their house-made rice paper bacon which is smoky, chewy, and so flavourful. It’s used for dishes like the BBQ Cheezeburger and the Happy Hashies.

‍

Other than these dishes, their cabinet is filled with made-in-house baked goods and meals that I’ll have to go back and try. Also, they make stunning latte art, and the owners and staff are all super friendly.
fieldData.name: Blendlove

fieldData.meta-description: Modern Indian eatery in Paddington with delicious and clearly marked vegan options
fieldData.description: Paddington's Old Monk brings modern Indian cuisine with quite a lot of options for vegans, which are clearly marked 'VG'. Start with the incredibly flavourful katori chaat (request the vegan version) – a crispy fried potato basket filled with spiced chickpeas, vegan yoghurt, and chutney. For mains, share a few curries. The vegan butter chicken is a highlight for me, pairing perfectly with tandoori roti or saffron rice. However, there aren't any options for vegan dessert at the time of visit.
fieldData.name: Old Monk Modern Indian

fieldData.meta-description: Italian restaurant chain with vegan pizza and pasta options, but vegan options cost extra
fieldData.description:
An Italian restaurant chain with locations across Brisbane (including the CBD, Garden City, and Carindale), Vapiano offers clearly marked vegan options, though expect to pay extra for substitutions like vegan cheese or vegan cream.

‍

The Margherita pizza has a thin, crispy crust but for me it's a bit dry and the vegan cheese is not melted. The Fusilli crema di funghi has a generous amount of mushrooms, but the vegan cream version may lack the expected creaminess. A decent option if nearby, but manage expectations for the price point.
fieldData.name: Vapiano

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan bubble tea shop with experimental Hong Kong-inspired flavours
fieldData.description:
Mother Pearl is a vegan bubble tea chain that's reinventing your typical boba experience with creative flavour combinations, though some drinks may be a bit too ‘experimental’ for some.

‍

All the bubble tea here are vegan, including crowd-pleasers like the Yuen Yeung 3.0, which is a Hong Kong style milk tea + coffee, or the taro mo-latte, a classic oat milk bubble tea with added sweet taro paste. However, not every bubble tea hits the mark for me: For instance, the matcha jasmine is loaded with grass jelly, taro paste, red bean, and matcha pearls, which ends up more like a dessert you have to eat than a drink, and it’s surprisingly low on sweetness. And if you are new to bubble tea, you probably want to steer clear of their QI wellness section, as those bubble teas incorporate Chinese medicine ingredients that may take some getting used to.

‍

Other than bubble tea, you can find some vegan snacks and meals here like wraps drizzled with Hong Kong fermented tofu sauce, peking duck empanadas, and earl grey mochi cookies. Just keep in mind to read the menu carefully as not all items are vegan - like the kimchi cheese empanadas which contains dairy.
fieldData.name: Mother Pearl

fieldData.address-text: Shop 4, Ground Floor, PCCW Tower, Taikoo Place, 979 King's Rd, Quarry Bay, Hong Kong
fieldData.meta-description: This vegan bakery has some hard-to-find items like egg tart and pineapple bun
fieldData.description:
(MAYA's Taikoo Place location is closed; The MAYA x The Cakery at IFC is stll open)

‍

MAYA Bakery & Bar is a chic vegan bakery that offers a delightful mix of hard-to-find Hong Kong-style baked goods. With its main location in the PCCW Tower at Taikoo Place (a great companion stop with Years) and a smaller kiosk at IFC in Central, it caters to vegans who agnate to try the traditional Hong Kong bakery items.

‍

Here you’ll find vegan baked goods like Hong Kong-style egg tarts, pineapple buns, chocolate-dipped croissants and more. The selection is impressive, though the quality can be a bit hit-or-miss depending on the item.

‍

Out of everything I tried, the egg tart and lava tart were standouts. They capture the familiar the texture of the non-vegan counterparts quite well, even though the lava tart would be better if served warm. On the flip side, the texture of bread, like the pineapple bun and croissant, tends to be on the dry side and lacks softness.

‍

Beyond the baked goods, MAYA also offers salad bowls, wraps, and even pizza for those looking for a heartier meal (the selection is bigger in their main branch in Taikoo). For drinks, you’ll find a variety of coffee, smoothies, and tea lattes.
fieldData.name: MAYA Bakery & Bar

fieldData.address-text: Hong Kong, North Point, Electric Rd, 308號, Luen Wo Apartments, 地下C4號舖
fieldData.meta-description: A hole-in-the-wall takeaway place with vegan Hong Kong street food
fieldData.description:
Chuen So Fai is located in North Point on Hong Kong Island. It is a great destination if you want to try some veganised quintessential Hong Kong street food. It’s a takeaway only place offering no-frills, budget-friendly bites on the go.

‍

I tried a mix of siu maai (燒賣) and curry fish balls (魚蛋), with each set of 5 pieces priced at just $8-10. The snacks came with a distinctive mushroom sauce topping, reminiscent of XO sauce, which added a flavourful kick. They don’t seem to have an English menu, so either use Google translate or show them the Chinese characters in this guide to order the same as mine.

‍

Beyond the Hong Kong street food, you can also find options like rice noodle rolls (腸粉), dumplings (粉果), and fried bean sauce mixed noodles (炸醬拌麵). They even offer bento boxes if you're looking for something more filling - but be sure to ask about the ingredients to make sure it doesn’t contain egg or dairy. For drinks, try a classic soy milk or their hand-crushed iced lemon tea.
fieldData.name: Chuen So Fai

fieldData.address-text: Hong Kong, Tong Mi, Tai Nan St, 198號Ground Floor
fieldData.meta-description: A vegan eatery that emphases a quiet and zen atmosphere
fieldData.description:
Tucked away in Sham Shui Po, Yudei offers a serene, zen atmosphere that’s perfect for a quiet solo meal or a calm outing with friends. If you’re looking to host a lively group to catch up, this might not be the spot for you, as discourage any loud chatting.

‍

This restaurant uses a self-service setup - Simply order at the counter and wait for your buzzer before collecting your meal.

‍

Yudei’s menu features a creative fusion of Japanese and other global flavours, sometimes with special collaborations with chef Tina Barrat, who brings in innovative vegan and raw meal sets.

‍

I sampled a few dishes during my visit, including a rich Japanese curry rice packed with a variety of veggies, and a beautifully presented baked potato and pumpkin dish drizzled with homemade onion sour cream. To finish, check whether they have the amazing basque cheesecake as dessert-of-the-day as it has a wonderfully firm yet creamy texture.

‍
fieldData.name: Yudei

fieldData.meta-description: Retro-inspired gelateria serving clearly marked vegan gelato
fieldData.description:
This gelato shop in Central surprises me with their high quality interesting flavours and high quality gelato. They clearly marked “AF” (Animal Free) for the vegan options, which are made with cashew milk. The vegan flavours span from classic choices like “intense chocolate” to inventive ones such as wasabi lime and Szechuan chilli mango.

‍

I was particularly blown away by the pistachio crunch gelato - it’s so good that I went there twice just to have it again. It’s one of the best gelatos I’ve had with its full, rich pistachio flavour and satisfying crunchy pieces.

‍

The space of Snack Baby is a retro vibe, with both indoors and outdoor seatings, though it gets super busy at night.
fieldData.name: Snack Baby

fieldData.meta-description: A popular veggetarian takeaway chain offers everything from bean curd rolls to cheung fun
fieldData.description:
Tin Tin Vegetarian is a popular takeaway chain that’s perfect for a quick bite or an emergency snack.

‍

The menu is filled with classic Hong Kong vegetarian food, like  bean curd rolls, radish cake, sticky rice rolls, and various wheat gluten pieces. If you're in the mood for something more filling, you can also opt for stir-fry noodles or their daily rice set.

‍

My personal favourite here is the steam rice noodle rolls, also known as cheung fun (腸粉). This traditional Hong Kong street snack has a delicious blend of sweet and salty flavours from soy sauce, a sweet red sauce, sesame peanut sauce, and topped with roasted sesame. For those who like a kick, drizzle some extra chilli sauce on top.

‍
fieldData.name: Tin Tin Vegetarian

fieldData.address-text: Hong Kong, Sai Ying Pun, Second St, 118號懿山地舖
fieldData.meta-description: This vegan gem veganises classic Hong Kong dishes like egg waffle and French toast
fieldData.description:
LN Coffee is a fully vegan gem in San Ying Pun that has veganised some traditional Hong Kong dishes that you can’t find anywhere else. The wooden decor and relaxed vibe make it a welcoming spot whether you’re dropping in for a meal or a quick afternoon coffee break.

‍

The menu is impressively diverse with some dishes that I haven’t seen anywhere else in the world. My number one recommendation is the Hong Kong style French toast. It’s perfectly executed without using the conventional egg batter. The cinnamon apple version in particular has won me over with its spot on taste and texture compared to the non-vegan version. Another highlight is the vegan egg bubble waffle which is another Hong Kong street food staple.

‍

If you are looking for something savoury, they also have burgers, pasta and some hearty lunch sets, though they aren’t as impressive as the two desserts I’ve mentioned.

‍

They also have a shop area that’s stocked with vegan snacks, sauces, and cup noodles.
fieldData.name: LN Coffee

fieldData.address-text: 7樓, V.i.p. Commercial Centre, 120號 Canton Rd, Tsim Sha Tsui, Hong Kong
fieldData.meta-description: An authentic yum cha experience for vegans in Tsim Sha Tsui
fieldData.description:
For those seeking an authentic vegan yum cha experience, Veggie Kingdom is a must-try. Located on the 7th floor of the VIP Commercial Center, which is right across from Harbour City in Tsim Sha Tsui, this hidden gem is as authentic and high quality as it gets in terms of traditional yum cha.

‍

All the beloved staples are here: siu mai, rice noodle rolls, spring rolls, and dumplings, each crafted to showcase vibrant flavours and textures. Out of all the dim sum I’ve tried, I was particularly blown away by the shredded turnip puff, mushroom siu mai, and golden vegetable dumplings.

‍

Due to its popularity, it’s wise to book a table in advance or arrive early to secure a spot. Also, keep in mind that there might be a dine-in time limit, so plan your meal accordingly.
fieldData.name: Veggie Kingdom

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan-friendly chocolate specialty shop located in Brisbane CBD
fieldData.description:
Noosa Chocolate Factory is a chocolate specialty shop located in Brisbane CBD. They offer a variety of chocolates, including some delicious vegan options. Vegan products are conveniently marked with a "vegan friendly" symbol on the packaging.

‍

The shop has many choices such as fruits wrapped in chocolate, Turkish delight chocolate, chocolate with desiccated coconut, coffee chocolate and more. They also serve chocolate drinks. I prefer the hot chocolate drink as they are even more rich and delicious compared to the iced ones.

‍

Prices are on the higher side. For example, a vegan milk chocolate costs about $10, including the surcharge for non-dairy milk.

gallery.alt: 56% cacao semi dark hot oat chocolate

fieldData.name: Noosa Chocolate Factory

fieldData.meta-description: Hip burger joint with vegan option burgers and yoghurt
fieldData.description:
YOMG Burgers is a great spot for vegan-friendly eats if you’re craving a combo of burger with froyo. Though it’s an omni restaurant, they’ve got some solid vegan options, and I went there specifically to try their Miss Fu vegan burger and vegan froyo flavours.

‍

The Miss Fu burger was the only vegan burger option they have. You can choose between a plantein patty or a vegetable fritter - I prefer the fritter, which is a bit more substantial with a great texture compared to the plantein one which is a bit too thin for the burger. The burger also comes with a vibrant red beetroot bun, crispy fried potato, vegan cheese, tofu mayo, and more.

‍

For their frozen yoghurt, they had three vegan flavours on the day of visit: salted pistachio, chocolate fudge, and açai. All of them are great but pistachio is my favourite. Unlike the yoghurt, the toppings  aren't marked whether they are vegan, but the staff was super helpful in checking which ones were suitable. Go for the classic combo of  Biscoff sauce, Oreos, fruits, and nuts for a satisfying bowl of froyo.

‍

While the burger and froyo were excellent, it’s worth noting that their vegan options beyond these are somewhat limited. They do offer sweet potato fries and 'super blend' smoothies, but oddly, their "just fries" aren’t vegan because they contain dairy.

gallery.alt: Miss Fu Burger with Veg Fritter

fieldData.name: YOMG

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan fast-food chain delivering solid vegan comfort food in the Valley
fieldData.description:
I recently stopped by Lord of the Fries in Fortitude Valley after quite some time, and I’m glad to say their vegan fast food is still hitting the mark. The portions are generous, the flavours are good, and it’s clear they’re sticking to what they do best - delivering solid vegan comfort food.

‍

I tried the Biggie, their take on a vegan Big Mac. With two thick burger patties and all the classic burger ingredients, it’s a satisfying and fulfilling meal on its own. The sweet potato fries (freshly made and also in a generous portion) and cookies & cream milkshake (a bit coconut-y in flavour but overall creamy and tasty) are both great choices to add to your vegan comfort food meal.
fieldData.name: Lord of the Fries Fortitude Valley

fieldData.meta-description: Netherworld combines vegan-friendly food with nostalgic gaming fun
fieldData.description:
If you’re into vegan eats and retro gaming, then Netherworld in Fortitude Valley is worth checking out. It’s a vegan-friendly omni restaurant where all dishes are vegan by default (unless you opt for non-vegan swaps, which you really don’t need to do).

‍

The vibe here is super fun, with arcade machines, pinball machines, retro consoles, and board games found throughout the whole bar and restaurant, making it a great place to hang out with friends or embrace some nostalgic solo gaming.

‍

I got to try a few vegan dishes here. The Mimic Mac and Cheese has a creamy base with some flavourful and garlicky breadcrumbs on top. While the pasta is tasty, I find myself wishing for a bit more cheesiness and saltiness as the flavours come mostly from the breadcrumbs. The Phoenix Burger is a solid choice with a crispy chicken-style patty and slaw, pickles, cheese, and a mild chipotle mayo that taste great altogether. For dessert, the Peanut Butter Oreo Pie is not my favourite unfortunately. While the flavours are decent, it is a bit too sweet even for a sweet-tooth like me, and the jelly-like texture of the filling might not appeal to everyone.
fieldData.name: Netherworld

fieldData.meta-description: A Japanese cafe with limited vegan option but a beautiful outdoor garden
fieldData.description:
For food, this Japanese cafe has two vegan options - eggplant onigiri and seaweed onigiri. I tried the eggplant one which was well made and delicious.

‍

I'm impressed by the drinks. They have a great selection of Japanese tea lattes which are delicious. I got the genmaicha strawberry latte, which was delicious with the strong roasted flavours of genmaicha and a fragrant strawberry syrup.

‍

If you visit on the weekend, I'd recommend sitting outside enjoying the view of the Japanese garden. But keep in mind that it's not open on weekdays.

‍

Also, because this place is quite popular, visiting by yourself could mean having to sit at the high bar seat, and not at a table, which may not be the most comfortable as the bar seats are super close to each other. Just something to keep in mind for solo visitors.

‍
fieldData.name: Mountain River Patisserie

fieldData.meta-description: A bar located at the Brisbane Ovolo hotel with vegan-option pitas
fieldData.description:
Bar Kazba is located at the Fortitude Valley Ovolo Hotel. Two of their pita meals are vegan - falafel and cauliflower shawarma. The pita also comes with fries and a green chilli dipping sauce.I tried both are really liked them. They are filled with a generous amount of filling including tabouli, pickled onion and tahini sauce. The pita pockets are soft and fresh. Everything just works together and the result is delicious.

‍

For dessert, I tried their pistachio baklava ice cream sandwich, which is tasty with a nutty pistachio ice cream and thin, flaky baklava pieces. It would be even more perfect if the baklava pieces are thicker to balance out the jam filling.

‍

Even though the items I've tried were delicious, keep in mind that the vegan options are NOT marked on the menu, so please double checked to make sure what you order is vegan.

gallery.alt: Falafel and Cauliflower shawarma Kazba pitas
Pistachio baklava Ice cream sandwich, sumac jam

fieldData.name: Kazba Cocktail Bar

fieldData.meta-description: An Indian restaurant in West End with a good selection of vegan options
fieldData.description:
This Indian restaurant in West End has a good selection of clearly marked vegan dishes.

‍

In the lunch menu, the options with VGO can be made vegan. And for dinner, they have a separate vegan menu with quite a lot of options. The vegan butter chicken rice bowl that I tried came with rice, pickled onion and pappadum. Overall it’s quite tasty with a creamy tomato-y butter chicken sauce. It has a generous amount of soy chunks. The rice is also well cooked.

‍
fieldData.name: Indian Room West End

fieldData.address-text: Shop 1/124 Merivale St, South Brisbane QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: A takeaway-only vegan bakery in South Brisbane serving high quality baked goods
fieldData.description: This vegan bakery and patisserie is located near the Southbank train station. Although it only has a takeaway counter and no seats during my visit, I'm impressed with the quality of the snickerdoodle cookie croissant I tried. It tastes amazing with all the wondering layers of a good croissant. Other than croissant, you can expect to find danishes, cookies, and some savoury options.
fieldData.name: Sweet & Green Patisserie

fieldData.meta-description: A serene vegan cafe in Salisbury serving light meals and unique lattes
fieldData.description:
Jing Si Books & Cafe is a nice hidden gem in Brisbane. Located in the quiet streets in Salisbury, this all-vegan cafe offers a calming atmosphere that's great for a relaxing meal.

‍

The menu is on the simpler, lighter side. I tried the Jing Si rice bowl set, which includes a comforting miso soup and a colourful rice bowl topped with a vegan egg made from tofu and pumpkin, spongy tofu, avocado, vegan meat floss, fresh salad and more. They also have a great selection of teas and lattes, including unique ones like genmaicha and black rice latte.

gallery.alt: Jing Si rice bowl with vegan egg

fieldData.name: Jing Si Books & Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: Authentic Vietnamese restaurant with a dedicated vegan menu and flavourful dishes
fieldData.description:
This Vietnamese fusion restaurant has a dedicated vegan menu. With prior experience of running a vegetarian grocery shop (Health T) and another vegan-friendly eatery in West End (Fat Carrot), they know how to cook a flavourful and satisfying vegan meal.

‍

This restaurant has a dedicated vegan menu with classic Vietnamese dishes like pho and rice paper rolls. All the dishes I tried here are well-made and flavourful.
fieldData.name: SEN Legend

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ヴィーガンビストロじゃんがら
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0001 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Jingumae, 1 Chome−13−21 シャンゼール原宿1号館 ２号館 ２Ｆ
fieldData.meta-description: A bustling vegan restaurant in Harajuku offering authentic vegan ramen and Japanese dishes
fieldData.description:
Located in the heart of Harajuku, Vegan Bistro Jangara is a must-visit for ramen lovers. Opened by the ramen chain 'Kyushu Jangara', this vegan restaurant knows a thing or two about crafting a delicious bowl of ramen.

‍

The ramen here is authentic and delicious, with rich, umami broth and classic toppings. The kobonshan ramen is a must-try if it’s your first time visiting. This style of ramen originates from Kumamoto in Kyūshū. This vegan version wow’ed me when I first tried it. It has an incredibly rich umami broth, with some amazingly meaty grilled ‘meat’ as toppings.

‍

Beyond ramen, the menu features other vegan Japanese dishes like sizzling grilled soy meat plates, gyoza and karaage. The karaage's texture leans a bit spongy for my taste, but the tartare sauce that comes with it is tasty.

‍

With its central Harajuku location and popularity among tourists, this restaurant is almost always full, especially around lunch and dinner times. I arrived at around 8pm on a weekday and still had to wait 20 minutes. When you arrive, simply wait by the lift area until the staff calls you in one by one. You can scan the QR code on the wall to see the menu before heading in the restaurant.
fieldData.name: Vegan Bistro Jangara

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ユニバーサル ベイクスアンドカフェ
fieldData.address-text: 5 Chome-9-15 Daita, Setagaya City, Tokyo 155-0033, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: A cozy vegan bakery offering diverse baked goods, from croissants to curry buns
fieldData.description:
Universal Bakes & Cafe is a cute, fully vegan bakery offering an enticing array of baked goods that will make you want to try one of everything. You’ll find vegan croissants, sweet red bean paste-filled buns, apple crumble toast, and more. One of their most popular items is the French toast topped with a scoop of vegan ice cream, served in a cast iron skillet for 990 yen.

‍

I got the delicious curry bun, which has a crispy outer layer, soft bread and rich curry fillings.

‍

While the bakery has limited seatings, the outdoor area allows you to enjoy your treats while facing a serene neighbourhood street. Just be aware that to dine in, you'll need to order a drink along with your baked item.
fieldData.name: Universal Bakes and Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: A highly popular vegan ramen chain offering delicious ramen at reasonable prices
fieldData.description:
T's Tantan is probably the most famous and popular vegan restaurant in Tokyo, and it’s for a good reason. Every time I visited, the ramen is reliably delicious at a reasonable price.

‍

The Tokyo Station branch can be a bit tricky to find, follow the signs for the Keiyō line train (the red coloured JE line) until you reach the escalators marked "Keiyō line (direction for Maihama)," and T’s Tantan will be on the right of that. This popular spot has a constant queue, so if you can, go to the less busy branches at Ueno or Ikebukuro Stations, or their flagship restaurant in Jiyugaoka.

‍

For first-timers, go for the golden tantan noodles. The rich, creamy broth packs flavours. With toppings of soy mince, sesame, peanut butter and veggies, this ramen is satisfying and delicious at just 1,100 yen. They also offer other bowls like black sesame tantan ramen and yuzu ramen. For something extra, add three gyoza for 320 yen.

‍

In addition to the dine-in menu, T's Tantan has some takeaway options that make a perfect meal to take on the Shinkansen bullet train. Options include a soy meat bento box or a 10-piece gyoza bento for 1,000 yen each.

‍

menu.alt: Follow this red JE Keiyō line train until you reach the escalators

fieldData.name: T's Tantan

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒152-0035 Tokyo, Meguro City, Jiyugaoka, 2 Chome, ９−６ B1F
fieldData.meta-description: The flagship restaurant of the popular T's Tantan, offering a wider selection of top-quality dishes
fieldData.description:
T's Restaurant is located in Jiyugaoka, just a 10-minute train ride from Shibuya Station. This neighbourhood has a charming European atmosphere and is home to the flagship restaurant of the highly popular T's Tantan chain. Unlike the crowded Tokyo Station T’s Tantan, T's Restaurant is a much quieter and classier option, offering delicious dishes that’s not available at T's Tantan, yet still with reasonable prices.

‍

Almost everything I’ve tried here is top-notch. A must-try dish from their menu is the paella doria - a creamy, cheesy baked rice topped with an incredibly flavourful and perfectly textured fried chicken. You can even add 2 extra pieces of the fried chicken for just 220 yen more.

‍

If you're craving the famous tantan ramen, you can enjoy it here without the crowds and headache of locating the branch inside the maze-like Tokyo Station. One dish I wouldn’t recommend here is the pizza, as it's pretty average with a dry, cracker-like texture.

‍

For something sweet, try their parfaits or creme brûlée. They also sell their own brand of vegan products in the shop area, such as tantan ramen cup noodles, ready-to-eat curries, sauces, and dashi (broth) powders.

‍

gallery.alt: The fried chicken on top is perfect

fieldData.name: T's Restaurant

fieldData.name-in-original-language: たいやき ひいらぎ
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0013 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Ebisu, 1 Chome−4−1 恵比寿アーバンハウス 107
fieldData.meta-description: One of the few places you can try a vegan version of this fish-shaped Japanese street food
fieldData.description: This vegan-friendly spot in Ebisu specialises in egg-free taiyaki (a beloved Japanese street food dessert that’s shaped like a fish). Their regular taiyaki (200 yen) is a delicious vegan treat, featuring a thin, wafer-like shell filled with sweet red bean paste and chewy mochi bites. Keep in mind the ice cream taiyaki is not vegan.
fieldData.name: Taiyaki Hiiragi

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒160-0022 Tokyo, Shinjuku City, Shinjuku, 2 Chome−1−5, Parkside Square, 1階
fieldData.meta-description: A vegan dessert shop near Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden with a great selection of sweets
fieldData.description:
Marbre Vegan is a charming vegan dessert shop in Shinjuku. Located near Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden, this is the perfect pitstop after exploring the famous garden.

‍

This small cafe offers a delightful array of vegan desserts, all delicious and expertly crafted. The menu features classics such as strawberry cake, tiramisu, and apple tart, but they also have seasonal specials like the sakura cake I tried. Gluten-free options are marked on the menu. Other than the sweet options, they also have a rotating savoury option, like the katsu cutlet sandwich during my visit.
fieldData.name: Marbre Vegan

fieldData.address-text: 1 Chome-13-1 Tsukiji, Chuo City, Tokyo 104-0045, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: A modern vegan twist on traditional Japanese coffee shops, offering veganised classic dishes
fieldData.description:
If you're familiar with the classic Japanese "kissaten" coffee shop chains, then you probably have heard of Komeda Coffee.

‍

This Ginza branch is their all-vegan venture called Komeda Is. With an interior featuring wood, plants, and plenty of natural lighting, it offers a modern and green twist on the traditional kissaten ambiance.

‍

The food menu here is just as impressive, veganising a wide range of classic Japanese coffee shop dishes. You’ll find delicious options like katsu cutlet sandwich, avocado teriyaki burger, tofu fritters, and more. The katsu sandwich is a classic 'kissaten' dish, and this vegan version features vegan cutlet with a crispy outside and a firm meaty texture, and a tangy, slightly spicy sauce.

‍

The drink selection will also impress, featuring hard-to-find treats like Vienna coffee which comes with vegan whipped cream. And at the time of writing, you get a piece of soft toast for free until 11am with any drink order.

gallery.alt: Vienna coffee with vegan whipped cream
Sweet red bean paste on toast

fieldData.name: Komeda Is

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0042 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Udagawacho, 15−1 渋谷PARCO B1
fieldData.meta-description: A Shibuya vegan izakaya restaurant that offers one of the best plant-based karaage
fieldData.description:
Izakaya Masaka, located in the PARCO shopping centre in the heart of Shibuya, is a popular all-vegan restaurant serving up a small menu of traditional Japanese dishes.

‍

The star of the show is undoubtedly the karaage - one of the most realistic and insanely delicious vegan meat I’ve tasted. The meaty texture and rich flavours make this a must-try item. Choose from one of the many sauces to top the karaage like teriyaki mayo or sichuan spicy sauce. The gyoza is another delicious, authentic choice with its crispy base and classic gyoza filling.

‍

Because of its central location and relatively small space, expect a bit of a wait during peak lunch and dinner hours, especially on weekends.
fieldData.name: Izakaya Masaka

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒160-0022 Tokyo, Shinjuku City, Shinjuku, 3 Chome−38−1 ルミネエスト新宿 8F
fieldData.meta-description: A popular ramen chain that offers vegan options with rich broth and plant-based gyoza
fieldData.description:
Ippudo is a famous ramen chain across Japan, and this location in Shinjuku Lumine EST offers two delicious vegan ramen options - a tonkotsu ramen and a soy sauce ramen.

‍

I ordered the special silk-smooth veggie tonkotsu MIRATon, which is a delicious vegan-take on tonkotsu ramen. While the toppings like the vegan meat don’t stand out, the rich and creamy broth steals the show. This location also serves up tasty and reasonably-priced vegan gyoza with a juicy koya tofu and mushroom filling. The gyoza is pan-fried with a crispy base.

‍

Not all Ippudo locations provide these vegan options. Other than this Shinjuku shop, I’ve seen the branch in Kyoto near Karasuma Station that has vegan ramen.
fieldData.name: Ippudo

fieldData.name-in-original-language: フルーツ アンド シーズン
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒150-0021 Tokyo, Shibuya City, Ebisunishi, 1 Chome−10−1, Clean Palace, 1F
fieldData.meta-description: A trendy vegan cafe offering photogenic fruit sandwiches with fluffy vegan whipped cream
fieldData.description:
If you are in Tokyo, you have to try the viral cream sandwich. And Fruits and Season is one of my favourites to try that.

‍

This chic cafe specialises in vegan whipped cream fruit sandwiches. It offers a great selection of sandwiches made with high quality fruits, including seasonal varieties. The sandwiches has fluffy whipped cream in between soft sandwich bread. With the colourful fruits, these sandwiches are as photogenic as they are delicious. I had the mixed fruit sandwich which includes kiwi, strawberry, banana and mandarin. You can also find fruit tarts, fruit jellies, and açai bowls in this cafe.

‍

Dine-in customers are required to order a drink in addition to their food items. During busy hours, there is also a 60-minute time limit for dining in.

‍

Fruits & Season has a sister cafe called So Tarte that specialises in seasonal fruit tarts, with branches in Omotesando and Yoyogi-Uehara.

gallery.alt: Vegan mixed fruit sandwich with oat latte

fieldData.name: Fruits and Season

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒104-0061 Tokyo, Chuo City, Ginza, 2 Chome−4−6 ベルビア館 1階
fieldData.meta-description: A creative all-vegan cafe in Tokyo offering unique dishes like vegan omurice and nuggets
fieldData.description:
If you are looking for some creative vegan dishes, 2foods would be a great stop to put on your list. This all-vegan cafe has two locations: Ginza and Shibuya, both of which are inside the Loft shop. The decor is modern with a colourful industrial vibe.

‍

The menu features creative vegan takes of dishes that may be hard to find elsewhere, including omurice (rice topped with egg), and vegan nuggets. I tried the omurice with demi-glace sauce, which is a creative dish with creamy vegan egg on top of rice with a tangy sauce. Although it resembles the appearance of omelette rice, the egg part is pretty mild in taste without much of an eggy flavour.

‍

For those with a sweet tooth, go for their doughnuts or chocolate croissants. Many of the menu items are available for purchase in their shop section including the vegan “Ever Egg”.
fieldData.name: 2foods

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒600-8133 Kyoto, Shimogyo Ward, Inaricho, 448 鴨川ビル 1F
fieldData.meta-description: This riverside cafe offers classic Japanese dishes made with local organic ingredients
fieldData.description:
This all-vegan cafe gives you a beautiful view of the Kamo River while you dine. If you come early, you may even be able to secure one of the window seats.

‍

The menu offers classic Japanese cafe dishes like lunch plates, curry rice and buddha bowl. I tried the Veg Out plate which comes with a selection of small dishes made with organic veggies and grains from local farmers. Flavours could be on the milder side for some people. The preparation of ingredients is relatively simple which showcases the natural flavours of the local veggies. They also have a selection of desserts including the pecan tart I tried, but it was  a bit too dry and crumbly for my liking.

‍

Even though some of the dishes may not wow you, Veg Out still offers a unique dining experience with a beautiful river view.
fieldData.name: Veg Out

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ヴィーガンラーメン ウズ キョウト
fieldData.meta-description: Experience a unique, sensory-rich dining experience with rich and delicious vegan ramen and sushi
fieldData.description:
Vegan Ramen UZU offers a truly unique and immersive dining experience in Kyoto. When you enter, you’ll be greeted with soothing music, and the staff will put a drop of essential oil on your wrist before you enter the restaurant to enhance your dining experience.

‍

The place is intimate with only about 14 seats at one big table, with a striking digital wall art installation by teamLab.

‍

The food here is amazing. They offer 5 types of ramen.  The ‘Green MISO’ ramen has a complex blend of flavours and textures. The inclusion of green tea gives the broth its colour and unique flavours. The rich, umami broth base is made over 12 hours with ingredients like kelp and shiitake mushrooms, resulting in a super rich and memorable broth. The perfectly-cooked noodles are made with flours from Hokkaido and Miyazaki. Even though this bowl was a bit too spicy for me, I couldn’t help but finish the whole thing.

‍

While they are famous for their ramens, I’m also wow’ed by their sushi. Each piece gives you an intricate blend of flavours, featuring ingredients like lotus root, perilla leaves, wasabi hummus and more. It’s topped with edible flowers that you can break and sprinkle over the top.

‍

Booking online in advance is highly recommended as it’s a highly popular restaurant. You will be charged a 4,000 yen holding fee when you book, and the amount will be refunded to you after your visit. And on the day of visit, they can charge the same credit card as the one you used for the booking, which makes the dining experience quite seamless.
fieldData.name: Vegan Ramen UZU

fieldData.name-in-original-language: ディスイズネイチャー
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒600-8002 Kyoto, Shimogyo Ward, Otabicho, 35 京都高島屋 S.C. [T8 1F
fieldData.meta-description: Try the viral flower bouquets made from sweet bean paste and vegan gelato
fieldData.description:
This viral flower bouquet ice cream shop in Kyoto makes one of the prettiest and photogenic vegan desserts. The flower bouquet is actually made from sweet bean paste, similar to the main ingredient of traditional Japanese sweets - wagashi. They meticulously pipe the colourful bean paste into shapes of flowers and leaves. They’d even call you over before they put on the finishing touches so that you can see the process up close.

‍

The bottom part of the bouquet is where you will find the gelato. All the gelato flavours are plant based and doesn’t contain animal-derived dairy products according to the menu. During my visit, they had interesting flavours like cactus and salted truffle & cacao, alongside some classic flavours like matcha and strawberry.
fieldData.name: (THISIS) NATURE

fieldData.name-in-original-language: 豆乳ラーメン専門店豆禅
fieldData.address-text: 13-4 Shimogamo Higashitakagicho, Sakyo Ward, Kyoto, 606-0865, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: Ramen Towzen features customisable ramen and creative plant-based versions of traditional dishes
fieldData.description:
This vegan ramen restaurant is a hidden gem in Kyoto for vegan foodies. Walk through a garden path before entering this homey restaurant with tatami floor and traditional floor seatings. Remember to take off your shoes before entering.

‍

Towzen offers a concise menu of classic Japanese dishes made vegan, including ramen, sushi and soy meat rice bowl. For ramen, they provide quite a few customisation options, including the flavour, spice level, size, etc.

‍

I opted for their Towzen set which comes with ramen, one piece of eggplant ‘eel’ sushi, salad and soy pudding. The tantan ramen has a thick and creamy broth with soy mince topping, the sushi uses eggplant to recreate the appearance and texture of eel, and the soy milk pudding is an unexpected surprise with spot-on flavour and texture.

‍

One thing to keep in mind is that this restaurant has a strict ‘no photos’ policy for the interior. So make sure you take photos only of the food.

‍

This restaurant is also located about 15-minute walk from the famous Shimogamo Shrine, which makes it a great option to visit after your meal here.
fieldData.name: Ramen Towzen

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒604-8061 Kyoto, Nakagyo Ward, Shikibucho, 261 ヒューマンフォーラム本社ビル 2F
fieldData.meta-description: A charming all-vegan eatery near Nishiki Market serving beautiful & delicious 'gozen' meals
fieldData.description:
Mumokuteki Cafe is one of my favourites in Kyoto. Located in a central location close to Nishiki Market and the Teramachi-Dori shopping street, this charming, all-vegan cafe offers set meals that are as beautiful as they are delicious.

‍

On the ground level when you first enter, you’ll find their shop selling clothing and household goods. Look for the stairs that go up to the second level where the cafe is located.

‍

On the menu, you’ll find their ‘gozen’ meals which include a main with a variety of side dishes, soup and rice. The main dishes include a selection of tofu hamburger steak, miso cutlet and soy karaage. I tried the 3-kind gozen meal, which comes with all 3 types, alongside 6-7 small dishes, soup and rice. Highly recommend it as it is delicious with a great variety of flavours and textures.

‍

Other savoury options include a 'gozen’ meal with a bamboo basket steamed vegetable, vegetable curry rice, ramen and omurice made with yuba (tofu skin).

‍

You’ll also find a great variety of desserts here including tiramisu parfait, cheesecake and soft serve ice cream shakes. The tiramisu, although not traditional, is tasty with its soft, espresso-soaked sponge cake with 2 layers of mousse.

gallery.alt: Two kind curry rice with vegetable
