fieldData.name: Mumokuteki Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: A small, atmospheric vegan restaurant offering delicious Japanese and Korean dishes
fieldData.description:
A small, atmospheric restaurant in a traditional Japanese house, Itadakizen Kyoto is an all-vegan restaurant North of downtown Kyoto.

‍

Their small menu is a fusion between Japanese dishes like soy milk broth enmen noodles, and Korean dishes like bibimbap and kimbap. I’ve chosen to go for the Korean cuisine with bibimbap and kimbap. The bibimbap is smaller than expected, but it has a generous amount of topping and authentically served in a hot stone bowl. Overall the dishes are well-made and delicious, but a bit pricey considering the smaller portion.

‍

As Itadakizen is a relatively small restaurant and food is prepared fresh, the wait time for food could be long if the place is busy. I’d also recommend making a booking on their website especially if you are going for dinner.
fieldData.name: Itadakizen Kyoto

fieldData.name-in-original-language: アインソフ ジャーニー
fieldData.meta-description: A famous vegan chain restaurant from Tokyo that's popular among tourists
fieldData.description:
Located in the central shopping district of Kawaramachi, Ain Soph Journey Kyoto is a reliable choice for a tasty vegan meal. Ain Soph is a vegan restaurant chain from Tokyo, and this is the only branch located outside of Tokyo.

‍

Housed in a renovated two-level Japanese house, the restaurant offers a cozy space with a traditional Japanese flair. This restaurant is very popular especially among tourists, so expect some wait time if you are going on weekends or during dinner times.

‍

Compared to my last visit a few years ago, they have simplified the menu and sadly some of my favourites are not available anymore, like the fluffy matcha red bean pancake. That being said, the current menu is still great with choices like burgers, curry rice and other plates. They still offer the original ‘heavenly pancake’ which comes with two pieces of fluffy pancakes, whipped cream, ice cream and fruits.
fieldData.name: Ain Soph Journey Kyoto

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒550-0014 Osaka, Nishi Ward, Kitahorie, 1 Chome−14−20 ２F
fieldData.meta-description: A vegan ramen restaurant in downtown Osaka that offers 3 types of ramen bowls
fieldData.description:
Vegan Ramen by Playpen Friends is a trendy vegan ramen restaurant in the heart of Osaka. They offer 3 types of ramen broth: miso, shoyu (soy sauce) and tomato.

‍

While the portion of the toppings and ramen is generous, for me, the flavours are on the simpler side, which gives me a sense that this restaurant is tailoring the offerings to cater to the expectations of tourists looking for a vegan take on traditional ramen. Despite that, it’s still a decent choice given its central location and friendly service.
fieldData.name: Vegan Ramen By Playpen Friends

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒530-0001 Osaka, B1F Osaka Ekimae 4th Building, 1-11-4,Umeda, Kita-ku, Osaka-city
fieldData.meta-description: A rather disappointing vegan restaurant with subpar overpriced food
fieldData.description:
My experience dining at this vegan place was interesting and weird. They operate as ‘Second Room Cafe’ during the day which serves meat, but transition to a fully vegan menu at night and operate under a different name. Diners get their own private room, with the one I was in having floor seating, pipes running through one side, and a children's toy set in the corner. The vibe was strange and the room wasn't the cleanest.

‍

On the menu you’ll find veganised versions of famous Japanese dishes like okonomiyaki, takoyaki, karaage and more. One positive aspect is that they lists the ingredients for each dish which makes it clear that it’s vegan. I tried the takoyaki and karaage. Unfortunately, the food quality was subpar compared to other options in Osaka.

‍

The takoyaki was mostly batter with hardly any other ingredients inside, and was a bit undercooked, making it too soft and starchy, and lacking in the crispy outer layer that a traditional takoyaki has. The karaage was just deep-fried soy protein chunks that were too oily and under-seasoned for my taste.

‍

Although it's commendable that they are offering a vegan menu, the execution of the dishes fell short, giving the impression that they may have been trying to cater to tourists traveling to Osaka who may not know the authentic quality of those dishes.
fieldData.name: Vegan & Gluten Free Osaka

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒550-0013 Osaka, Nishi Ward, Shinmachi, 1 Chome−9−9 Alivio 新町 １F
fieldData.meta-description: Popular and high quality vegan eatery conveniently located in the Shinsaibashi area
fieldData.description:
Paprika Shokudo is a busy vegan cafe with a focus on organic ingredients. The ambiance is cozy with wooden accents, and if weather allows, choose one of the outdoor terrace seats facing a quiet local street.

‍

Although the menu is a bit on the expensive side, the quality of the food justifies the price. Try the popular vegan oyster which is made with tofu and mushrooms, or the soy meat karaage that has an excellent texture. For dinner, they offer set meals that include a main dish (like the oyster or karaage) with salad, miso soup, and rice, ranging from 2,000 to 2,500 yen. I tried the karaage plate which has a generous amount of karaage pieces with great texture.

‍

Other than the vegan plates, they also serve rice bowls, pasta, and pizza. Leave room for dessert, as they offer vegan cheesecake, brownies, and ice cream.
fieldData.name: Paprika Shokudo

fieldData.name-in-original-language: オプティマス カフェ
fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒541-0041 Osaka, Chuo Ward, Kitahama, 2 Chome−1−14 KITA2 BLD.
fieldData.meta-description: A river-view vegan cafe serving comfort food like breakfast plates and soy milk ramen
fieldData.description:
Optimus Cafe is a bustling vegan eatery in Osaka. If you're lucky enough to secure a riverside seat, you'll have a delightful view of the river and the Osaka City Central Public Hall across.

‍

For breakfast, go for the ‘Have a good day plate featuring toast with a tofu and hummus spread, house-made vegan sausage, a side salad, and pickles. Their lunch menu offers hearty options like soy milk ramen, curry rice, and buddha bowls. The food leans towards the simple side, but the flavours are good.

‍

You’ll also find vegan treats in their cabinet including matcha brownie, gluten-free cookies and carrot cake.
fieldData.name: Optimus Cafe

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒542-0083 Osaka, Chuo Ward, Higashishinsaibashi, 1 Chome−13−9 第５天偉ビル 二階 vegan glutenfree takoyaki
fieldData.meta-description: A small vegan takoyaki (octopus balls) restaurant located near Dotonbori
fieldData.description:
OKO Takoyaki, the sister shop of OKO Okonomiyaki, offers an all-vegan menu of takoyaki (a classic Japanese street food of octopus balls) and kushikatsu (deep fried skewers). This small upstairs restaurant has an eclectic interior featuring colourful walls covered with customer messages.

‍

They offer takoyaki plates that costs 1,000 yen with five variations of different sauces like classic takoyaki sauce and spicy sauce. While the takoyaki is a bit too starchy without chewy bites in the middle or the crispy shell, it's still a fun and affordable vegan option in the area.
fieldData.name: OKO Takoyaki

fieldData.name-in-original-language: 遊べるお好み焼き屋 OKO
fieldData.address-text: 1 Chome-15-24 Higashishinsaibashi, Chuo Ward, Osaka, 542-0083, Japan
fieldData.meta-description: An eclectic okonomiyaki specialty restaurant that offers vegan option okonomiyaki
fieldData.description:
Just 10 minutes from the famous Dotonbori area, OKO Okonomiyaki is a unique, vibrant vegan-friendly restaurant in Osaka run solely by one energetic lady. This place is super popular during dinner time (6-9 pm) so be prepared for a long wait time. If it’s too busy, consider their sister shop, OKO Takoyaki, which is just a block away serving all-vegan takoyaki.

‍

The interior of OKO Okonomiyaki is an eclectic mix of colours with customer messages covering the walls. You first order on the ground floor, and then you find a seat upstairs. Keep an ear out for your order number, as you'll need to head downstairs to collect your food. Remember to clean up and return the tray downstairs after you finish your meal. There's no staff extra staff other than the owner, and because of that, the restaurant may not be the cleanest.

‍

Specify the vegan version of okonomiyaki, yakisoba and gyoza when you order as they also serve meat here. The okonomiyaki is made with okara (soy pulp) instead of egg to bind the ingredients. You can find vegan mayonnaise at the service counter on each floor. While it’s overall enjoyable, the taste and flavour may not blow you away. With the location being close to Dotonbori, this restaurant is still a good option for vegans exploring the area.
fieldData.name: OKO Okonomiyaki

fieldData.name-in-original-language: お茶とお花とモンブラン
fieldData.meta-description: A beautiful cafe that's in between Osaka and Kyoto, serving even more beautiful vegan parfaits
fieldData.description:
Located in the Ibaraki suburb between Osaka and Kyoto, Ocha Ohana Montblanc is a gorgeous all-vegan dessert cafe that you can't miss. Despite being a bit off the beaten path, it only takes around 30 minutes to reach from either of the major cities.

‍

The food here is prepared to perfection with painstaking attention to details. The seasonal vegan parfaits are easily the stars of the show here. Meticulously constructed with countless layers of high-quality, vegan ingredients, these parfaits are works of art on a plate. The flavour rotates regularly, so be sure to check their social media for the current offering. This one I tried is a strawberry and sakura parfait. There are a total of 16 elements with contrasting flavours and textures like an edible sakura-flavoured leaf, matcha mochi and sakura chestnut montblanc.

‍

Other than parfait, you’ll also find other seasonal desserts and savoury dishes like pasta and salad. I tried the tomato soup lotus root pasta dish which comes with a muffin and a vinegar soda.

‍

The cafe is just as beautiful as the food. As soon as you step into the second-floor dining area, you're greeted by a breathtaking view of the entire ceiling covered in a kaleidoscope of dried flowers.

‍

A few tips for your visit: the cafe only accepts cash, so come prepared. They have limited operating hours for dine-in, only opening two days a week at the time of writing. And due to the tiny size with just three tables upstairs, I’d highly recommend making a reservation for your visit. The online booking system requires a Japanese phone number. Given that you don’t have one, I'd recommend messaging them on Instagram to book.
fieldData.name: Ocha Ohana Montblanc

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒530-8558 Osaka, Kita Ward, Umeda, 3 Chome−1−3 ルクア イーレ 2F
fieldData.meta-description: A busy cafe near Osaka and Umeda station that specialises in matcha and hojicha
fieldData.description:
Famous for their matcha offerings, Iyemon Cafe near Osaka station has some vegan desserts. The vegan options are marked with a red “Vegan” box with a leaf. Options include matcha anmitsu, hojicha tiramisu and matcha affogato. For drinks, sample their soy matcha latte. However, there are no savoury vegan options.

‍

I've tried their vegan anmitsu, which includes a scoop of matcha ice cream instead of soft serve ice cream in the non-vegan version. It comes with agar agar jelly, fruits, mochi and sweet red bean paste. Overall it's tasty with rich matcha flavour.
fieldData.name: Iyemon Cafe

fieldData.address-text: Japan, 〒530-0016 Osaka, Kita Ward, Nakazaki, 1 Chome−10−14 あじゅ
fieldData.meta-description: Aju is a small vegan izakaya in Osaka serving classic Japanese dishes like yakitori and okonomiyaki
fieldData.description:
Aju is a small vegan izakaya serving classic Japanese dishes. It's a one-person operation, with the owner handling everything from cooking to serving. Be prepared for a wait if there are other customers. There’s even a card saying that he can’t handle more than 4 customers at a time.

‍

The menu features veganised versions of izakaya staples like okonomiyaki and yakitori. The okonomiyaki has the classic look and flavour, topped with mayonnaise and seaweed, with mock meat inside. The yakitori plate uses soy protein, konjac, and other vegan ingredients to mimic the look and texture of different grilled chicken skewers. These are great options to sample the owner's plant-based take on classic Japanese dishes.
fieldData.name: Aju

fieldData.address-text: Unit 8/115 Wickham St, Fortitude Valley QLD 4006
fieldData.meta-description: A long-standing vegetarian restaurant in Brisbane located near the Valley
fieldData.description: Tea Master is a vegetarian restaurant near the valley that is one of the OG of Brisbane's veg scene. The Asian style dishes are mostly vegan and clearly marked. You'll find bento boxes, stir fries, noodles, hot pots and more. You'll also find a wide range of drinks including vegan bubble tea, but keep in mind that they use a one-use plastic cup for bubble tea.
fieldData.name: Tea Master Vegetarian Cafe Restaurant

fieldData.meta-description: Japanese snack cafe offering vegan sorbet, onigiri, warabimochi and more
fieldData.description:
Shiro Gelato and Snacks is a Japanese snack cafe offering vegan sorbets, onigiri rice balls, warabimochi, and various drinks like matcha and hojicha lattes. Vegan options are clearly marked with VG. (but the strawberry range is not vegan as the strawberry powder they use to mix with the milk has dairy.)

‍

The sorbet flavours change regularly; I tried the lemon & yuzu flavour during my visit. I recommend the Shiro Lover style, where the sorbet is wrapped in mochi skin and topped with a few pieces of warabimochi. The sorbet was tasty, and the warabimochi was soft and fresh.
fieldData.name: Shiro Gelato & Snacks Southport

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan bakery in Southport that also offers great gluten-free options
fieldData.description:
Sacre Coeur Patisserie is a fully vegan bakery that also offers excellent gluten-free options. All the baked goods are made in-house. Options include pistachio croissants, hazelnut pain au chocolat, and fruit tarts. Savoury options are also available like bolognese pie and cheesy sausage roll.

‍

I tried the pistachio croissant, which was delicious, though slightly undercooked in the middle. There are some relaxing outdoor seating and the staff is friendly.

‍
fieldData.name: Sacre Coeur Patisserie

fieldData.meta-description: An all vegan bakery with a dazzling selection of baked goods
fieldData.description:
This bakery in Southport is all vegan with a dazzling range of baked goods. They offer bakery classics like filled doughnuts, croissants, cream jam buns, as well as some more creative options like croffin (croissant muffin). You’ll also find savoury options here like cheesy garlic scroll, pizza bread and a selection of hot pies.

‍

It’s hard to pick a favourite out of everything I tried here, but my favourites were the choc honeycomb croffin and the cinnamon scroll with biscoff icing.

‍

Although the food was great, I wouldn’t really recommend the drinks. Both the iced chocolate and the dirty chai I tried were pretty weak unfortunately.

‍
fieldData.name: Made With Love Bakery

fieldData.meta-description: Delicious vegan bubble tea shop with milk and cream made with five types of nuts
fieldData.description:
Nuttea makes delicious bubble tea with thick cream made with 5 types of nuts - Walnut, hazelnut, cashew, almond and macadamia. It’s hard to find a vegan cream that’s this thick, creamy with a nutty flavour. I would highly recommend getting a drink with the thick cream, like the earl grey with chocolate nut cream or the matcha nut mylk tea.

‍

They have two locations in Melbourne - One in Melbourne Central, and one in Fitzroy located inside Vincent's Marketplace, which is a vegan grocery store.
fieldData.name: Nuttea Melbourne Central

fieldData.meta-description: Great pizzas and even more amazing vegan wings
fieldData.description:
This vegan wood-fire pizzeria in Melbourne makes great pizzas, and even more amazing vegan wings.

‍

The pizzas are fresh, and the base is fragrant and chewy. Tried the pepperoni pizza, cheeseburger pizza (with crumbled burger patty, cheese, pickles, sesame seeds, etc) and the G.O.A.T pizza (a special with vegan goat cheese, caramelised onion, tomato, pine nuts, etc). All three pizzas I've tried here are consistently great.

‍

But the stand out dish for me is their Not Wings vegan chicken wings. The texture is one of the best I’ve had. Perfectly meaty and delicious. And the wings are coated with a sweet sticky sauce. Don't miss this if you are a fan of vegan meat alternatives.
fieldData.name: Red Sparrow Pizza & Rooftop Bar

fieldData.meta-description: Fully vegan Italian restaurant at the heart of Melbourne CBD
fieldData.description:
Located on Hardware Lane right in the CBD, Funghi e Tartufo is a 100% vegan traditional Italian restaurant. While the location is atmospheric, it does feel a bit touristy, and unfortunately, my experience here was a bit disappointing.

‍

While the food quality and the service were ok, my main issue was their portion and value for money. The portions were quite small considering the premium prices, and the food didn't feel particularly special. The dish I liked the most was the creamy mushroom pappardelle, which featured perfectly cooked pasta in a creamy sauce and came in a decent portion size.

‍

However, the Pesce Spada alla Siciliana (a breadcrumb-crusted grilled swordfish with a zucchini and fennel salad) was a letdown. For $36, you receive just three small pieces of "swordfish" that seemed like the pre-packaged vegan seafood you can buy at a vegan grocery store, just crumbed and fried. The small portion continued to their dessert as well. I ordered the pistachio gelato, which was $20 for three small, plain scoops drizzled with pistachio liquor. The gelato tasted decent, but it was visually underwhelming with no toppings and simply too expensive for what it was.
fieldData.name: Funghi e Tartufo

fieldData.meta-description: Doughnut chain with some vegan options like custard doughnut and jam doughnut
fieldData.description: This doughnut chain has some tasty vegan options, including vegan custard, jam, cream & jam and original glazed. With multiple locations in Melbourne, this is a convenient option if you want to have something sweet during the day.
fieldData.name: Daniel's Donuts

fieldData.meta-description: Gelateria in Melbourne that has some vegan flavours
fieldData.description: This gelato specialty shop has several locations in Melbourne. Their dairy-free options are vegan, featuring flavors such as dark chocolate and passionfruit. The texture and flavours are good, making it a great option as dessert after dinner.
fieldData.name: Piccolina Gelateria

fieldData.meta-description: A modern vegan deli specialising in sandwiches and pastries
fieldData.description:
Smith & Deli in Melbourne offers a modern and sophisticated vegan deli experience, specialising in sandwiches and baked goods.

‍

You’ll find a selection of toasties and sandwiches here like the reubenstein toastie which has pastrami and sauerkraut, or the foghorn legless which is a sourdough sandwich with schnitzel and bacon.

‍

For me, the highlight here is the selection of pastries. You’ll find a cabinet full of delectable options, like the berry yoghurt danish and the chocolate stick that I tried, both of which are fantastic.

‍

They also have a grocery section selling pantry staples and frozen ready-to-eat meals.
fieldData.name: Smith & Deli

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan-friendly Japanese restaurant in Collingwood serving teishoku, ramen and gyoza.
fieldData.description:
Decorated with colourful traditional Japanese signs, Wabi Sabi Salon is a vegan-option restaurant located in Collingwood. They have 3 vegan teishoku sets and I chose the ‘pumpkin stuffed mushroom tempura’. Teishoku, meaning ‘set meal’ in Japanese, usually comes with a main dish, several side dishes, soup and rice.

‍

The price for the teishoku sets are pretty high at around $32, but the quality and variety of food make it worthwhile. Each component, from the main dish to the small sides, is delicious and offers a great range of textures and flavours. The crispy mushroom tempura, in particular, stood out as my favourite. I also added a mini curry to the set, though it didn’t quite justify the additional $6.

‍

Beyond teishoku, Wabi Sabi Salon also offers vegan tantan ramen, gyoza, and tofu curry rice.
fieldData.name: Wabi Sabi Salon

fieldData.meta-description: A Japanese takeaway spot in Brisbane CBD serving classics like curry rice, donburi and sushi
fieldData.description:
A Japanese takeaway spot on Adelaide Street. The food is pretty tasty with good prices. The vegan options are marked clearly with a VG on the menu. You can expect to find options like veg tempura curry rice and teriyaki tofu donburi. They also have some vegan sushi in the fridge section like inari and tempura nigiri. They also run promotion on selected days of the week, for example, the curry rice is $9.9 on Wednesdays at the time of writing this.

‍

It gets quite busy during lunch time as it's located in the Brisbane City. They have limited seats inside, so I'd recommend getting the takeaway and eat at one of the food courts or parks nearby.

Veg tempura sushi and tempura nigiri

fieldData.name: Niko Niko

fieldData.meta-description: Delicious vegan comfort food with a playful twist in West End's live music venue, The Bearded Lady
fieldData.description:
The Vegan Mary has become my new go-to for a tasty burger in the West End area. They began their journey as a food truck early in 2023, and has now found a permanent home in West End, serving as the kitchen for The Bearded Lady.

‍

Specialising in 100% vegan comfort food, The Vegan Mary has a menu of classic burgers and snacks. All the burgers I've tried here are delicious with great attention to detail. My top pick is the No Cluck'n Around burger, which uses crispy fried oyster mushrooms alongside other classic burger fillings. For snacks and bites, I particularly enjoy the buffalo cauliflower wings which has a deliciously tangy and spicy sauce.

‍

It's a good idea to check The Bearded Lady's page before heading over, as they often host live bands which might require a ticket for entry.
fieldData.name: The Vegan Mary

fieldData.address-text: 471 S Pine Rd, Everton Park QLD 4053
fieldData.meta-description: An all-vegan, anime-themed ramen restaurant in Everton Park
fieldData.description:
This colourful, anime themed ramen bar in Everton Park is a vegan gem in Brisbane. Everything here is vegan. The menu features highly customisable ramen and stir-fry. You can pick the sauce, noodle type and toppings you prefer. Try the tan tan ramen broth for ramen and the surprisingly flavourful garlic mushroom sauce for stir-fry.

‍

Be sure to leave some space for the amazing desserts. I've tried all 4 and they are all superb. The ice cream they use is soy based and super creamy. And the purple yam doughnuts are a must-try.

‍

Other than the delicious food, another stand out feature here is the big portion, especially the stir fry.

gallery.alt: Yellow noodles in the tan tan ramen

fieldData.name: Neon Ramen

fieldData.address-text: Opera Quays, Shop 10/3 Macquarie St, Sydney NSW 2000
fieldData.meta-description: Famous Belgium chocolatier with some disappointing vegan options
fieldData.description:
Right next to the Opera house is the Guylian Belgium Chocolate Cafe. They've also got two other branches at the Rocks and in Sydney CBD. The first thing that caught my eye was their vegan cakes, as it's always great to find vegan dessert options at well-known spots.

‍

At the time of visit, they have four vegan desserts, including the vegan red velvet cake that I tried. Despite the beautiful presentation, the taste is disappointing. The cream lacked flavour, and the texture of the red velvet biscuit is more like a soggy sponge cake. For $16.5, I was expecting more.

‍

I also tried their dark hot chocolate, which the staff confirmed it can be made vegan. But it's also weaker than I expected from a chocolatier cafe.
fieldData.name: Guylian Belgium Chocolate Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: Busy vegan Vietnamese restaurant near Newtown train station that serves delicious Asian comfort food
fieldData.description:
Just a short walk from Newtown train station is Golden Lotus, a Vietnamese vegan eatery that seems to be full all the time. And after going there, I can let you know that it’s popular for a reason!


The clay pot fried fish is one of my favourite dishes in Sydney. Incredibly rich and packed with deep flavours, and the vegan fish texture is also great. Other delicious dishes I’ve tried here include the rich and creamy laksa, and the yellow noodle soup with rich broth and generous toppings.


As I mentioned, this place gets pretty busy. If you don’t want to wait long, visit on a weekday, or have early dinner here.

gallery.alt: Vegan fried fish in clay pot

fieldData.name: Golden Lotus Newtown

fieldData.meta-description: An all-vegan Vietnamese restaurant in Newtown with decent food and warm service
fieldData.description:
Vina Vegan is a vegan Vietnamese eatery in Newtown. As soon as you walk in, you are welcomed by the friendly and warm staff, and its welcoming environment.

‍

The menu is full of classic Vietnamese dishes. I enjoyed the vermicelli salad with spring rolls and vegan chicken. It comes loaded with toppings and tastes fresh. The salted vegan fish fried rice is another dish I'd recommend with its strong flavours.

‍

However, not everything was a hit for me. The crispy yellow noodles were too oily for me. And the vegan chicken that comes with the dish was more tough than crispy. Also, the Vina pancake "Banh xeo" had a unexpectedly sour taste, which I wasn't a big fan of. Still, with the friendly service and some tasty dishes, I'd say Vina Vegan is worth a visit.

gallery.alt: Vermicelli salad with spring rolls and vegan chicken
Spring rolls in the vermicelli salad
Crispy vegan prawn in sweet & sour sauce sizzling plate
Crispy yellow noodles with veggies, vegan ham & crispy vegan duck in mushroom sauce.

fieldData.name: Vina Vegan

fieldData.meta-description: Located in Newtown, Calle Rey is a vegan Mexican restaurant with a Japanese twist.
fieldData.description:
(Calle Rey has added meat to the menu in March 2025. Their menu now features about 50% vegan dishes and 50% non-vegan dishes. This review was written prior to the change)

‍

Who knew a vegan Mexican restaurant with a Japanese twist existed? Calle Rey in Newtown is a unique vegan restaurant with delicious food.

‍

The watermelon tuna tartare was an unexpected favourite of mine; it's fascinating how the slow-cooked watermelon mimics the texture of tuna. The dish comes with avo and cucumber, which you can eat all together on a corn chip.

‍

I’ve tried 3 types of taco during my visit: The smoked chicken, Fable carnitas, and the California roll taco. Each one has its own unique flavour profile, but if I had to pick my favourite, it would be the Japanese-Mexican fusion of the California roll taco. The contrasting texture of cream cheese and crispy prawn in a taco is unexpected and delicious.

‍

If you happen to visit on a Taco Tuesday, you can get their taco for just $5 each which is amazing value considering the quality.
fieldData.name: Calle Rey

fieldData.meta-description: All-vegan supermarket in Glebe with a great selection of products
fieldData.description:
(This review was written for their previous Glebe shop.) In Glebe, you'll find the Vegan Grocery Store - An all-vegan supermarket with a great range of products. It's located right opposite two other vegan favourites – Soul Burger and Oh My Days. From tasty cheeses and meat substitutes to vegan leather handbags and pet foods, they have got it all.

‍

Honestly, it's hard to walk around without wanting to buy everything. Be sure to go to their special section to pick up a few discounted goodies. And if you can’t make it in person or want to shop from home, they have an online store that delivers Australia-wide.

gallery.alt: Vegan leather handbags from Matt & Nat
Pick up a few discounted goodies from the special section
They also carry some vegan desserts in the shop

fieldData.name: Vegan Grocery Store

fieldData.meta-description: A sweet, cozy Japanese cafe located in Newtown, serving delicious classics like curry and sushi.
fieldData.description:
Nestled in the heart of Newtown, Comeco is a delightful vegan Japanese cafe. You’ll feel welcomed by its warm service and ambiance when you arrive.


They've got a relatively small menu featuring some classic Japanese dishes like curry rice and tempura. The food I’ve tried here is overall tasty with great attention to details.


Their tempura and onigiri plate is a great choice for anyone who wants a bit of everything. The Japanese curry rice is tasty with rich curry, but the katsu is a bit too thin and not as ‘meaty’ as I’ve hoped. But I’d still recommend the katsu curry rice instead of the one without as it’s only $1 difference.


If you're up for a snack, their vegan chicken karaage with a karashi mustard sauce is great. If you are craving desserts, try their sweet potato doughnuts. I’ve tested the yuzu custard and kinako sugar flavours, and both of them are delicious with a fluffy and chewy doughnut. For drinks, the sesame and hojicha lattes are classic Japanese choices that’s hard to find elsewhere.

Karaage add-on for onigiri tempura plate
Side salad in onigiri & tempura plate

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan burger joint in Sydney with a few locations, serving classic burgers, fries and more.
fieldData.description:
Soul Burger is a vegan burger joint in Sydney with a few branches, including the one in Glebe which I visited twice. You’ll also find their sister brands in the shops: Plantas (Mexican cuisine) and Zayna's Lebanese.


Soul Burger has a good range of vegan burgers, sides, and milkshakes. My favourites are the meaty lamb brisket burger, and the comfort food goodness of the Southern fried chicken burger. Their meatballs in the subs are also superb.


But not everything hit the mark for me. The burrito from their sister brand, Plantas, could do with a lot more seasoning. The satay burger was decent but didn't deliver on the rich peanut taste I was hoping for. Still, with daily specials like a $10 meatball sub on weekends, Soul Burger is worth a try when you’re in Sydney.

gallery.alt: Plantas burrito with grilled PB chicken

menu.alt: Menu with their sister brands Plantas and Zayna's Lebanese

fieldData.name: Soul Burger

fieldData.meta-description: Great vegan spot in Darlinghurst, offering Thai-inspired cuisine
fieldData.description:
Located within walking distance from the city, Kindness Vegan in Darlinghurst is a good option for vegan food.


They have a menu of classic Thai dishes. Overall the food is good, but not amazing. The standout dish for me is the massaman curry, which is flavourful. The delicious seaweed tofu mimics the texture of fried fish with the seaweed wrapped around the beancurd roll, and it’s a nice addition to the curry. Be sure to ask for a mild curry if you are not great with spicy food. The pad si iew, a fried rice noodle dish with sweet soy sauce, is well made and satisfying. But the gravy noodles with flat rice noodles don’t quite hit the mark for me because the sauce is not strong enough to be called gravy.


For dessert, I tried the grilled banana with sticky rice, which was a special during my visit. It was delicious with the crispy caramel banana paired with soft, chewy sticky rice.

gallery.alt: Grilled caramelised banana with coconut sticky rice
Thai lemon tea and Thai milk tea

fieldData.name: Kindness Vegan

fieldData.meta-description: A hidden gem for pastry lovers, Oh My Days offers a range of delectable baked goods
fieldData.description:
Now, if you're a fan of pastries and all things baked, Oh My Days is a must-visit. I absolutely love this place, especially their deliciously flaky croissants.


The pandan coconut croissant is so delicious that I bought a second one to take back with me. The flaky pastry coupled with the sweet pandan coconut filling makes it one of my favourites this trip. The melted cheese croissant toastie with bacon is also amazing, featuring the melty mozzarella from Rebel and Rascal, a local vegan cheese brand with a shop in Newtown.


They have both indoor and outdoor seating, and you'll also find the Cruelty Free Shop and Soul Burger nearby - perfect for a bit of shopping after your meal.

Flake pastry of Oh My Days
Their special: Thai milk tea croffin
Inside the Thai milk tea croffin
Ham and cheese croissant has amazing texture

fieldData.name: Oh My Days

fieldData.meta-description: An all-vegan bakery in Surry Hills with delicious pastries, doughnuts and desserts
fieldData.description:
This is one of my favourite spots from this Sydney trip. This hidden gem of a bakery in Surry Hills offers a fantastic range of all-vegan pastries and desserts.


Everything I tried was fantastic. Their truffle potato danish and almond choc croissant are my favourites, each offering an amazing flaky croissant texture with delicious fillings/toppings. The cheeseburger jaffle is another delicious item with melty cheese and classic burger fillings. And the hot chocolate doughnut has a tasty cakey texture. Honestly, it's hard to go wrong here when anything you choose.


Keep in mind that they only have a limited seatings outside the bakery.
fieldData.name: Miss Sina + Nutie

fieldData.meta-description: Vibrant vegan eatery in Surry Hills, serving delectable plant-based cuisine
fieldData.description:
Yulli's is another all-vegan spot that deserves a visit, or two as in my case. I love the food here, with the savoury options standing out more than the desserts.


Don’t miss their Korean fried broccolini. It is light, crispy and coated with a strong, sticky sweet chilli sauce that packs a punch. The zucchini flowers is also well made with a tasty beetroot filling and a mustard dressing. The creamy cauliflower pappardelle and baked zucchini are also great options.


Their dessert menu, though not as impressive to me as their savoury dishes, is still great. The chocolate lava cake is well made with a beautiful presentation. But the kanafe dessert is not my favourite as the filo pastry lacks crispiness, and the combination of mozzarella in a dessert is a bit off to me.

gallery.alt: Beetroot cream inside the zucchini flowers
Baked zucchini in filo pastry with tom yum sauce and black olive mousse

fieldData.name: Yulli's Surry Hills

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan-friendly eatery in Sydney CBD serving tasty Taiwanese cuisine
fieldData.description:
Located in the heart of Sydney CBD, Mother Chu's is a decent Taiwanese restaurant option for vegans.


Their golden mushrooms and soy sheets roulades in black pepper sauce is a standout, offering a delicious and unexpected combination of beancurd rolls with a taro filling. The steam BBQ buns also make for a nice side - soft bun with just the right amount of filling. However, the sizzling plate with soya bean roll is a bit disappointed with the small portion of the dish.


Keep in mind that some dishes have honey, like the ‘glazed honey gluten with walnuts’ I had. Specify ‘no honey’ when you order those dishes. Also be prepared for a bit of a wait during dinner time as this place can get quite busy.

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan cheese heaven in Newtown with a selection of dairy-free cheeses and more
fieldData.description:
This all-vegan cheese shop in Newtown carrying several brands, including their own - Rebel & Rascal. If you're a cheese lover, this place is perfect for you!


If you are lucky, you may get some delicious samples from one of the friendly owners and staff. I’ve tried a few and the ricotta and marinated fetta are amazing. The marinated fetta is especially versatile - it can be mixed in pasta or simply enjoyed on crackers. Not to mention the price of their cheeses are also reasonable. Plus, they carry all-vegan pastries from Oh My Days.

fieldData.name: La Petite Fauxmagerie

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan patisserie in Newtown with delightful macarons and cozy seating
fieldData.description:
Le Gourmand is a bit of a mixed bag, but worth visiting for their incredible vegan macarons when you are in Newtown. This entirely vegan patisserie offers some indoor seating, making it a nice spot to unwind on a lazy afternoon.


The vegan macarons are a treat - crispy shells, soft filling, and a great selection of flavours. The peanut butter and iced vovo flavours are my favourites. However, I also had the pistachio crème brûlée here and it left much to be desired with its weird texture.
fieldData.name: Le Gourmand

fieldData.meta-description: Vibrant Greek-inspired vegan spot in Newtown with a diverse menu of wraps and desserts
fieldData.description:
If you're up for some Greek-inspired vegan food, then check out I Should Be Souvlaki in Newtown. This all-vegan spot had some decent dishes, but I have to say it didn't live up to the hype for me. That being said, the food is still good overall.


The menu offers a good range of options, from their signature wraps to cheesecakes. The signature souvlaki wrap (I chose chicken and ultimate lamb protein) is tasty, but I find it less flavourful than expected. The salted and pepper calamari is okay, although it’s a bit too soft and not crispy enough for me. Both the southern fried chicken tenders and the popcorn cauliflower are decent but not amazing.


But the real highlight of the meal is the lemon blueberry cheesecake - the lemony flavour is spot on, and the texture of the baked cheesecake is amazing.
fieldData.name: I Should Be Souvlaki

fieldData.meta-description: Indulge in incredible Italianflavours and a bustling atmosphere in Gigi at Newtown
fieldData.description:
If you're a fan of Italian cuisine, the you need to visit Gigi's Pizzeria in Newtown! The dishes I had here were amazing. But keep in mind that they can be quite busy, so go early especially on the weekend because they don’t take bookings.


The Salsiccia e Broccoli pizza I tried is amazing. The soft, chewy base, topped with beyond sausage, sautéed broccoli, and crumbled mozzarella, was exceptional. The Calzone Speciale, filled with ricotta, mushrooms, and smoked slices, was also impressive with its tasty, cheesy filling.


And if you still have room for dessert, try the classic tiramisu. It’s well made with great texture, though I personally would have preferred it a bit sweeter.

gallery.alt: Patate pizza with roasted potatoes, truffle pate, garlic, rosemary and more
Atlantico pizza with smoked salmon, capers, onion and more

fieldData.name: Gigi Pizzeria

fieldData.meta-description: Omni Japanese restaurant in Newtown with great vegan options like ramen, gyoza and more
fieldData.description:
Although Neko Neko is not a vegan restaurant, its vegan offering is pretty impressive. “Neko” means cat in Japanese, and that’s why you’ll find a lot of cat-themed decor here, perfect for cat lovers like myself.


Their ramen is entirely vegan, and there are quite a few other vegan dishes on the menu as well.


I tried the vegan tan tan ramen, which has chewy ramen noodles with a decent broth. It would be even better if the mince tasted less like TVP. The vegan superfood agedashi tofu & eggplant teishoku meal set is a delightful assortment of tofu, eggplant, pickles, veggies, and rice. However, the eggplant, agedashi tofu bowl is rather oily.


Their vegan gyoza is a must-try. It’s soft, flavourful, and crispy. And don't miss their housemade soy matcha latte. It's rich, delicious, and comes in a cute little bottle.

gallery.alt: Plate of 7 small dishes and rice in teishoku set

fieldData.name: Neko Neko Newtown

fieldData.address-text: 2468 Gold Coast Hwy, Mermaid Beach QLD 4218
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan Asian restaurant on the Gold Coast that has been open for over 20 years
fieldData.description:
Tian Ran is a vegan restaurant on the Gold Coast that offers classic Asian dishes. The standout dish is the crispy teriyaki chicken, which has a crispy batter and a delicious sweet sauce. But some dishes are a bit too dry, such as the satay sticks and the salt & pepper tofu.

‍

The service is friendly and overall it's a good choice if you are looking for food on the Gold Coast

gallery.alt: Sago with Coconut Milk and Palm Sugar

fieldData.name: Tian Ran

fieldData.meta-description: A classy restaurant on the Gold Coast that offers a fully vegan and gluten-free menu
fieldData.description:
(Greenhouse Canteen on the Gold Coast is permanently closed since Sep 2023)

Greenhouse Canteen is a vegan, gluten-free restaurant located on the Gold Coast. Overall the food and service are good, but not particularly memorable.

‍

The standout dish is the Korean rice cake which has a flavourful Korean sweet chilli jam and the rice cakes are deliciously crispy. But the truffle mac and cheese is a bit of a let down with an underwhelming truffle taste and overcooked macaroni. The pumpkin Alfredo gnocchi is good but not as tasty as the one served at the now-closed South Brisbane branch.

‍

With the classy vibes of the decor, Greenhouse Canteen is a nice vegan option on the Gold Coast.
fieldData.name: Greenhouse Canteen + Bar Gold Coast

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan cafe in West End, Brisbane with delicious vegan food, cozy atmosphere and friendly service
fieldData.description:
(Cinnamon & Co. is permanently closed since Oct 2023)

‍

Cinnamon & Co is a great vegan restaurant cafe located in West End, Brisbane. I've tried a few dishes here and the quality is consistently high. They change the menu from time to time. Recently, I've tried the the bang bang bowl which is a rice bowl with sweet chilli sauce on top of crispy tofu and veggies. The tarragona and ianri are also my previous favourites that have rotated out of the menu at the time of writing. For drinks, try the house-brewed chai if you are a chai lover.

‍

The environment at Cinnamon & Co is also cozy and welcoming. They have a basement level where they sometimes host a vintage clothing shop or activities like trivia or board game night. The service is also warm and friendly, which makes for a great dining experience.

Pot of house brewed chai on oat milk
Texture of the mushroom meatballs in Tarragona

fieldData.name: Cinnamon & Co.

fieldData.address-text: Shop 8, Fountain Court, 141 Sutton St, Redcliffe QLD 4020
fieldData.meta-description: Thai Redcliffe is a small but authentic restaurant with some great vegan dishes
fieldData.description:
If you're looking for a hidden gem in Redcliffe with great vegan options, Thai Redcliffe is what you're looking for. This Thai restaurant has a surprisingly big vegan menu, including classic dishes like curry, pad Thai, and spring rolls.

‍

During my 2 visits, the food has been consistently great. Some of the standout dishes include the Vegan Thai Redcliffe curry (creamy and flavourful, could be too spicy for some) and pineapple fried rice with BBQ pork. For the choice of mock meat, I'd recommend going with the crispy chicken.

‍

One thing to keep in mind is that the restaurant is quite small, with only about five tables. If you're planning to visit, it's a good idea to book ahead, especially since there aren't many vegan options in the area.

gallery.alt: Pineapple fried rice with BBQ pork
Vegan Thai Redcliffe curry with crispy fish

fieldData.name: Thai Redcliffe

fieldData.address-text: Little Stanley St Shop 6C, South Brisbane QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: Ma Pa Me is a great vegan-friendly restaurant in Southbank, Brisbane with delicious Southeast Asian
fieldData.description:
Ma Pa Me is a great vegan-option restaurant located in Southbank, Brisbane that serves delicious Southeast Asian cuisine. The restaurant has a separate vegan menu that offers some great options.

‍

One of my favourites here include the pumpkin white curry and the vegan 'ma' gado gado, both of which are rich and flavourful. For the gado gado, I'd recommend asking them to make it with more sauce if possible. It is perfect by itself or with a bowl of rice. Another stand out dish is the jackfruit rendang which has a strong, umami flavour.

‍

Some of the dishes I've tried here are nice but too oily, including the nasi goreng and pad Thai.

gallery.alt: Jackfruit Rendang, Gado Gado and Pumpkin White Curry
Thai green curry with roasted pumpkin

fieldData.name: Ma Pa Me

fieldData.address-text: 4/3282 Mount Lindesay Hwy, Browns Plains QLD 4118
fieldData.meta-description: Good value Asian-fusion restaurant located on the South side
fieldData.description:
Permanently closed since November 2023

‍

Overall I enjoyed the meal here. Everything is tasty and well made, and the service is friendly as well. The food is also good value with decent portion.

‍

One thing to keep in mind is that almost every item on the menu is fried/deep-fried. Although the dishes are made well (crispy & crunchy without too oily), it’s possible to feel a bit heavy afterwards with all the fried food.

‍

But if you like fried food with an Asian flair, you’ll love this restaurant!

‍

They have only 3-4 tables in the restaurant so definitely call ahead to book if you are planning to go!

gallery.alt: Satay Bean Curd on noodles with fried enoki mushroom

fieldData.meta-description: A high end veg restaurant serving Middle Eastern dishes with hints of Mediterranean
fieldData.description:
Overall I enjoyed the food at Za Za Ta. The standout dishes were the black lentil mushroom manti (it’s a dumpling dish made with Fable meat. Deep flavours with contrasting textures) and triple cooked potato (so surprisingly crispy and flavourful, and the garlicky vegan butter the potatoes are served on is amazing).

‍

Other dishes are nice, but one dish that was a bit of a let down was the green wheat tabbouli, which didn’t pack the flavour punch like some of the other dishes. For that price, I was expecting more than just a small raw salad.

‍

The prices of Za Za Ta are on the higher end with pretty small portions. But it still can be a good choice for special occasions if you don’t mind spending more.

fieldData.meta-description: A classy restaurant in Woolloongabba with an innovative vegan menu
fieldData.description:
Detour in Woolloongabba provides a fantastic dining experience. Although the prices are on the higher side, the menu showcases creativity and flavours that are hard to find elsewhere in Brisbane.

‍

The 'Herbivore' part of the menu is all vegan with 7 choices at the time of visit, including charcoal roasted broccoli, beetroot tartare, fossilized carrots and roasted sweet potato green curry. They also had an impressive vegan dessert that night which was a nitro meringue with raspberry and basil.

Roasted sweet potato with green curry

fieldData.name: Detour

fieldData.meta-description: Vegan restaurant in the Clayfield area that serves authentic Thai cuisine
fieldData.description:
U Tong Thai is a hidden gem in Brisbane that specialises in vegan Thai food. The dishes are in general well portioned and delicious. All savoury options I've had here are great. Some stand-out dishes include the whole coconut curry, pad see ew, pineapple fried rice and the side of coconut rice.

‍

Free parking is available at the front of the restaurants.

Banana fritter and lychee with ice cream

fieldData.name: U Tong Thai

fieldData.meta-description: Beautiful, rustic cafe in Hamilton serving classic cafe food and some authentic Asian dishes
fieldData.description:
Pancha has changed from vegan to serving meat since Aug 2023. This review is written prior to the change.

‍

Pancha is a beautiful rustic cafe in Hamilton. They put emphasis on using local produce from their family farm and from other local farmers. All the food is here vegan but they have dairy milk for coffee.

‍

The food quality is great here with rich flavours and textures. You will find some Asian dishes like pad thai and massaman curry, both of which are delicious and authentic. If you are looking for Western flavour, their mushroom arancini is amazing. Just keep in mind that they like to put rose petals on everything.

Owner Sam holding the acai berry smoothie

fieldData.name: Pancha Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: A bulk food store chain in Australia for zero waste, sustainable shopping
fieldData.description:
This health food, bulk food store has branches in Queensland, Victoria, New South Wales and ACT. They have a good selection of vegan products and they are marked with a green vegan label.

Here you can find products like snacks, granola, nut butter, cleaning products, body care products and more. They have paper bags and glass jars if you don't have your own containers.
fieldData.name: Naked Foods Bulk Food Store

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan cafe in Spring Hill serving delicious Asian-inspired comfort food
fieldData.description:
Vega Cafe is an all vegan cafe located in Spring Hill. I've visited many times and they make some of the most delicious vegan dishes I've had in Brisbane. And the owners and staff are always friendly and welcoming.

‍

It's hard to choose a favourite here as the quality is consistently high. The murtabah is a must-try with its creamy curry chicken filling in crispy roti pocket. And the vegan omelette is my favourite in the breakfast menu with its creamy, egg-like texture. They also open for dinner for a few days a week; The yellow curry in the dinner menu is one of the most flavourful and rich curries I've had in a while.

‍

They also carry a good selection of cabinet desserts including macarons, croissants and doughnuts.

gallery.alt: Iced mocha with added whipped cream
Hello sunshine smoothie and Cebu peach iced tea

fieldData.name: Vega Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: A vegetarian cafe in Stafford Heights with plenty of vegan options and relaxing vibes
fieldData.description:
Located in a quiet neighbourhood in Stafford Heights, Enoki Coffee is a relaxing cafe with plenty of vegan options. At the time of visit, all items on their menu except one are either vegan or can be veganised.

‍

Choices include arancini, avo toast, halloumi bagel and more. The dishes I tried, summer sorbet tacos, panko fried mushies and coconut tofu noodle bowl, were all well made and tasty.

‍

Staff is also friendly and helpful. They also sell art from local artists in the shop.
fieldData.name: Enoki Coffee & Co

fieldData.meta-description: A funky bar + restaurant in West End with vegan options
fieldData.description:
This bar & restaurant in West End has funky atmosphere and colourful eclectic furniture. Their menu has some clearly-marked vegan options including pizzas, burger and nachos.

I've tried two of their vegan pizzas: Brother from another mother and Tim Curry III. The base is more of a thin cracker type base. They are generous with the topping. However, the taste is rather mild.

Overall good choice for vegan dinner because of the unique vibes and friendly staff.
fieldData.name: The Burrow

fieldData.meta-description: Restaurant in Paddington, Brisbane serving all vegan comfort dishes
fieldData.description:
An all-vegan restaurant in Paddington, Brisbane. The atmosphere here is relaxing, and staff is helpful and friendly.

The food is general good with choices like burgers, mac & cheese, pancakes, etc. However, their signature CFC, which is a fried chicken dish with mashed potatoes, fries, slaw and gravy, was disappointing with small chicken pieces and huge portion of potatoes.

gallery.alt: Chicken pieces have good meaty texture

fieldData.name: Yavanna

fieldData.address-text: 7/60 Santa Cruz Blvd, Clear Island Waters QLD 4226
fieldData.meta-description: This vegan-option cafe serves Coco Fluff ice cream, acai bowls and other desserts
fieldData.description:
While the menu is not vegan, Goji Granola Bar & Cafe makes some delicious desserts including their Coco Fluff ice cream, acai bowls and granola.

The staff is helpful and friendly. With the cafe located in a quiet location, it's a good choice to relax if you are in the area.
fieldData.name: Goji Granola Bar & Cafe

fieldData.meta-description: A beautiful cake shop specialising in raw desserts located in Maleny, Queensland
fieldData.description:
Maple & Sage is a vegan bakery specialising in raw desserts in Maleny. It's one of the most aesthetically pleasing dessert shops I've seen. From the cakes to all the decorations, everything looks stunning!

Here you can find a selection of raw desserts, salads and smoothies. The doughnut I've tried tastes great. Other than food, their shop section carries eco-friendly household and personal care products.

A must-visit if you are near Maleny and Sunshine Coast!

gallery.alt: A closer look at the passionfruit cream doughnut
Dessert cabinet with doughnuts, cake slices and more

fieldData.name: Maple & Sage (Permanently Closed)

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan burger shop shared with a smoothie, juice bar
fieldData.description:
Moofree Burger is a vegan burger chain in the Brisbane area. This shop in North Lakes is shared with Charlie's Raw Squeeze - A smoothie and juice bar.

‍

They have a wide selection of burgers, chips, desserts and drinks. In general the food is well-made and tasty. However, sometimes the food is not executed perfectly, like overly salty chips.

‍

They run discount on various items throughout the week, like $10 burgers on Monday and buy-1-get-1 free smoothie on Tuesday.

gallery.alt: The mint acai smoothie is delicious
The gravy chips tastes good but way too salty

fieldData.name: Moofree Burger & Charlie's Raw Squeeze

fieldData.meta-description: Green Edge offers an impressive selection of vegan groceries, but food has some room for improvement
fieldData.description:
Green Edge is a vegan restaurant and grocery store located in Windsor, known for being one of the originals in the Brisbane's vegan scene. The place is reachable by bus or train, and they offer free parking as well.

‍

One of the standout features of the Green Edge is its shop section, which is fully stocked with vegan groceries, makeup, house supplies, shoes, and recipe books. The selection is impressive, but prices can be on the higher side.

‍

For the cafe section, Green Edge offers pizzas, burgers, pasta and other vegan comfort food. I'm especially impressed with their pizzas with melty cheese and a generous amount of toppings. However, some dishes I've tried were a bit disappointing, like the cauliflower buffalo wings which could be crispier on the outside with the inside less mushy. They also have a fully vegan deli section, dessert cabinet and ice cream parlour inside the shop where you can get something extra after your meal.

gallery.alt: Korean BBQ pork & seafood marinara pizzas
Korean BBQ pork bowl and southern crispy chicken pancakes
Bacon and egg muffin is nice, but quite small for the price

menu.alt: Sausage rolls and pies behind the cashier

fieldData.name: The Green Edge

fieldData.address-text: Shop G03/21 Buchanan St, West End QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: A modern vegan cafe in West End with an emphasis on local produce and seasonal menu
fieldData.description:
Located on a quiet street in West End, Grown is a modern vegan cafe with an emphasis on fresh local produce and seasonal menu.

‍

Food is well presented and delicious. I love the creative details of the dishes. For example, the avo toast comes with a cheese made of cashew and sesame. Or the way they create a crispy, creme brûlée-like crust of the French toast by torching it with sugar.

‍

For brunch, they offer a more cafe style menu. While in the evening, they offer a more fine-dining style.

gallery.alt: Housemade hashbrown with tomato, kimchi, avocado and more

menu.alt: They have cabinet dessert which change often

fieldData.name: Grown

fieldData.meta-description: This Japanese restaurant in South Brisbane has a separate vegan menu with quite a few options
fieldData.description:
This Japanese restaurant in the South Brisbane/West End area has a separate vegan menu with quite a few options, including the classics like sushi, ramen and bento boxes.

The food here is good in general with some better dishes than others. I love the vegan tempura as it's hard to find one without egg in the tempura batter. The karaage cauliflower is also tasty. However, some of the other dishes like the tempura sushi roll is a bit of a miss.

gallery.alt: Vegetable croquette curry rice, burdock chips and ginger tofu bento box
Tempura platter, vegetable croquette curry rice, teriyaki tofu and yakisoba

fieldData.name: Okuman Karaage & Ramen Bar

fieldData.address-text: Shop 4/156 Boundary St, West End QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: An Italian Restaurant serving classic Italian dishes like pizza, pasta, burgers and more
fieldData.description:
This Italian eatery in West End, Brisbane offer some classic dishes including pizza, pasta and tiramisu. The food is delicious in general. I especially love the pizzas and the tiramisu. The portion of the pasta dishes, however, could be a little bit small for the price.

‍

Also keep in mind that they charge for table water. Ask for tap water if you don't want to pay for water.
fieldData.name: Nonna's Nightmare

fieldData.meta-description: A trendy vegan restaurant in South Brisbane serving all vegan and gluten free dishes
fieldData.description:
This vegan and gluten-free restaurant in South Brisbane offers delicious food and great vibes. Some of the dishes are creative like the mushroom cheeseburger using tempura mushroom as the 'buns'.

The dishes are in general very well made and pack full of flavours. I especially love the Korean rice cake, chickpea fettuccine and the mushroom cheeseburger. I also love the chai latte and hot chocolate here. However, I have tried 3 of the 4 desserts and I would not recommend any of them.

General good vibes in the restaurant. I love the booth seatings, but usually they won't be available unless you book in advance. Some of the other seatings could be a bit cramped as they are very close together.

At the time of writing, they offer AU$5 tacos on Tuesday. They are full of toppings and are very delicious.

gallery.alt: The Korean rice cake is amazing

fieldData.name: Greenhouse Canteen + Bar South Brisbane

fieldData.meta-description: A ramen place in Paddington with a few vegan options
fieldData.description:
This ramen place in Paddington has 2 vegan ramen. The miso one is vegan by default, and the veg one is vegan after removing the egg. They also have a vegan tofu bao and a few vegan sides.

The broths of both ramen are rich and tasty. I especially love the flavourful mushroom in the ramen. The ramen consistency could be too soft for some people.

At the time of writing, they are doing a AU$10 special for ramen on Monday and Tuesday 4:30-5:30.
fieldData.name: Hai Hai

fieldData.meta-description: A cafe in West End, Brisbane with a focus on wraps. Vegan options available.
fieldData.description:
Wrapture is a cafe in West End, Brisbane specialising on wraps. They have 4 wraps that can be veganised: Falafel, sultan, satay tofu and zen tofu. They also usually have a selection of vegan sweets and desserts next to the counter.

Keep in mind that you'd need to specify a vegan wrap when you order as the default pita wrap is not vegan. The vegan wrap is AU$1 extra.

The wraps are freshly made and delicious. And the filling is generous.

gallery.alt: Falafel wrap and satay tofu wrap

fieldData.name: Wrapture

fieldData.meta-description: A Japanese ramen restaurant with a separate vegan menu
fieldData.description:
Located on Melbourne Street in South Brisbane, Taro's Ramen has a small vegan menu with some classic Japanese dishes, including ramen, gyoza and curry rice.

‍

The 3 different ramen choices: vegan classic, vegan red and vegan fire, are the same with different spicy levels. They taste good with a flavourful broth and chewy noodles. The toppings could be a bit more generous, as you only get 2 small pieces of tofu and veggies for the price.

‍

The cold tomato noodles are another good choice. It's flavourful and refreshing. However, I wouldn't recommend the curry rice as it lacks toppings and not worth the price.

gallery.alt: Marinated tofu in vegan classic ramen

fieldData.name: Taro's Ramen

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan restaurant in West End, Brisbane serving a variety of Asian dishes
fieldData.description:
This vegan Asian restaurant in West End, Brisbane has a big menu. You will find dishes including Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese and more.

‍

Honey chicken, fried rice and rosemary chicken are my go-to's. Food quality is nice but nothing too memorable. Overall value is good with generous portion.

gallery.alt: Spring rolls, fried rice and salt & pepper tofu

fieldData.name: Vegan Restaurant West End

fieldData.meta-description: Nurcha is a one-stop shop for vegans on the Sunshine Coast with a cafe and a grocery shop
fieldData.description:
Nurcha is a great place to visit for vegans. You can find delicious food, groceries, crystals, decor, and so much more here.

The selection for their grocery and homeware is pretty impressive. From vegan snacks to big home fixtures, you will spend some time going through all the items. The prices are also reasonable once you joined the free membership.

The Nurcha cafe also has a wide range of choices, from healthy acai bowls to freshly made pizzas. The food I've tried are well made and delicious. There is also plenty of seating, both indoor and outdoor, where you can sit and relax for an afternoon.
fieldData.name: Nurcha Kawana

fieldData.meta-description: Plant-based cafe at Buderim, Sunshine Coast that serves some delicious cafe classics
fieldData.description:
Cafe Vie closed down in February 2024.

‍

Cafe Vie is one of the must-visit cafes on the Sunshine Coast. The menu includes some inventive cafe classics like vegan poached egg on muffin with beef, and vanilla cream red velvet pancake. The food quality is impeccable.

‍

They also make sure you feel welcomed. Owners and staff here are warm and friendly.

‍

They also have a good selection of cabinet baked goods including some tasty cookies and cakes. And be sure to stop by their shop section and get some goodies to take home.

‍

One other good thing is that the owners also run an animal sanctuary called Mini Tails, and the proceeds from the cafe goes to helping the animals.
fieldData.name: Cafe Vie (Permanently Closed)

fieldData.address-text: Shop 4/321 Montague Rd, West End QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: An Asian restaurant in West End, Brisbane with an extensive vegan menu
fieldData.description: This Asian restaurant in West End, Brisbane has a few clearly marked vegan options, like vegan honey chicken, smoked 'duck' banh mi and more.
fieldData.name: Mr Hong Modern Asian Restaurant

fieldData.meta-description: Authentic vegan yum-cha and traditional Cantonese cuisine
fieldData.description:
It’s rare to find an authentic yum cha place nowadays, let alone an all-vegan one. Easy House ticks all the boxes: vegan, authentic and delicious.

‍

They do yum cha at lunch and dinner times. The dishes I've tried are exceptional with authentic taste. The flavours are true to what you will get in Hong Kong. Other than the yum cha, they also do other classic dishes that are commonly found in Hong Kong.

‍

The staff in this family-owned restaurant is very friendly and helpful.

‍

Highly recommend Easy House if you want to try good quality vegan yum cha.
fieldData.name: Easy House Vegetarian Restaurant

fieldData.address-text: Shop 1617, Ground Level, Pacific Fair Shopping Centre, 2-30 Hooker Blvd, Broadbeach QLD 4218
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan Thai restaurant in Pacific Fair shopping centre
fieldData.description:
Siam Purity is a vegan Thai restaurant in the Pacific Fair shopping centre. You will find traditional dishes here like pad Thai, tom yum soup, curry rice and more. The menu is pretty extensive.

‍

The food is well-made with reasonable prices. The crispy honey soy and green curry fried rice are both delicious.

‍

One interesting things for this place is that the food is delivered by a friendly robot!

gallery.alt: Vegan honey crispy soy and peanut sauce stir fry

fieldData.name: Siam Purity

fieldData.address-text: 1C/2375 Gold Coast Hwy, Mermaid Beach QLD 4218
fieldData.meta-description: A small cafe in Mermaid Beach which has a fashion boutique in the same location
fieldData.description:
Lovechild is a vegan restaurant + bar in the Mermaid Beach area.

They serve some classic fast food like burgers and fried chicken. The quality is quite good, I especially enjoy the fried chicken tender for its texture. However, some may find that the price is a bit high for the portion you get.

One side of the shop is dedicated to their fashion and accessories - Lovechild Boutique + Beauty.
fieldData.name: Lovechild Kitchen + Bar

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan Taiwanese restaurant in Southport, Gold Coast
fieldData.description:
Kuan Yin has recently undergone an ownership change, shifting its menu towards Thai-style dishes while retaining some Taiwanese dishes from the previous owner.

‍

On their all-vegan menu, you’ll find Asian classics like fried rice, curries, hot pots and more.

‍

The bento box I tried came with two small dishes (tofu and stir-fried veggies on the day I visited), a salad, pickles, rice, and fruit, in addition to an entree of your choice. I chose the snow fish, which tasted great with good texture, but could benefit from a bit more sauce to complement the rice.
fieldData.name: Kuan Yin Tea House

fieldData.meta-description: A vegan bakery in Helensvale with a wide selection of classic baked goods
fieldData.description:
Flour of Life bakery in Helensvale is a dream come true for vegans. You will find many of your childhood favourites veganised here, like cream doughnut, lamington and custard tart.

Other than sweets, they also have a good selection of savoury pies, tarts, sandwiches and more. You probably need to visit multiple times to try more of their stuff.

Keep in mind that they don't have seatings at the store.
fieldData.name: Flour of Life Bakery

fieldData.meta-description: A vegetarian cafe in Broadbeach with many vegan options
fieldData.description:
Beautiful cafe in the Broadbeach area. It's a vegetarian cafe with many dishes that are vegan or veganisable.

Food is tasty and beautifully presented. Other than the a la carte menu, they do all-you-can-eat buffet daily with dishes like curry, desserts and more.
fieldData.name: Cardamom Pod Broadbeach

fieldData.meta-description: Comfort food cafe in Paradise Point serving burgers and bowls
fieldData.description:
This vegan cafe in Paradise Point makes some delicious vegan comfort food. Burgers, all-day breakfast, pancakes and more. The dishes I've tried are all well-made and tasty. I especially love the chicken burger.

The environment is relaxing and the staff is friendly.
fieldData.name: Plant Based Eatz

fieldData.meta-description: Veg cafe in Southport with vegan food that's as stunning as they are delicious
fieldData.description:
Cardamom Pod Brickworks is a modern cafe is located in Brickworks Ferry Rd, Southport. Even though the food I've tried there is well-made and delicious, it's important to note that they have introduced dairy cheese to their otherwise vegan menu in 2024.

‍

You will find some familiar dishes that are elevated. All the dishes are as beautiful as they are delicious. I really appreciate the presentation and effort they put in the dishes. In the times I've visited, the food quality is very consistently high. For first-timers, try their beautiful acai bowls or blinged avo benny. If you visit on the weekend, the Indian street food waffle is a great choice.

‍

They are usually quite busy especially on weekends so be prepared to wait a little bit for a table.

gallery.alt: Green smoothie (front) and iced matcha with boba (back)

fieldData.name: Cardamom Pod Brickworks

fieldData.address-text: Shop 7/50 Woodland Dr, Reedy Creek QLD 4227
fieldData.meta-description: A 100% vegan Japanese restaurant in Reedy Creek with authentic delicious food and friendly service
fieldData.description:
Izakaya Midori has a mission: to provide 100% vegan Japanese cuisine that is good for the environment, animals and your health. They envision a future where karaage doesn't need to come from chicken.

‍

The menu is filled with Japanese classics like sushi, ramen, katsu rice bowl, etc. The dishes are as beautiful as they are delicious.

‍

Other than the amazing food, the service here is warm and friendly. They try their best to make sure your experience is as perfect as possible.

gallery.alt: Katsu don and chiki avo nigiri

fieldData.name: Izakaya Midori

fieldData.address-text: Shop 2B/220 Melbourne St, South Brisbane QLD 4101
fieldData.meta-description: A bubble tea house in West End Brisbane that makes vegan soft serve
fieldData.description: This tea shop in West End has quite a few vegan dessert options. The best one being their vegan soft serve ice cream. Flavour rotates regularly, and they include cherry blossom, chai, taro and more. You can add additional toppings like pearls, Oreo and fruits. They also have vegan bubble tea and sometimes other vegan desserts. The prices are reasonable with generous portion.
fieldData.name: Botanical Lab

fieldData.meta-description: Brisbane branch of an International vegan chain with a focus on Asian dishes
fieldData.description:
Loving Hut is an international vegan restaurant chain. The Brisbane one is located in Mount Gravatt. They have a decent sized menu, with a focus on Asian dishes. You can find some classic Asian food like laksa, BBQ pork bun and Singapore noodles here. They also have some western choices like pasta and cakes.

‍

The decor can be a bit dated, but the friendly service and good food are enough for a recommendation. They also have a shop section selling vegan products, like frozen vegan meat.
fieldData.name: Loving Hut Brisbane

fieldData.meta-description: A Taiwanese fusion restaurant in West End, Brisbane
fieldData.description:
Vegeme is an Asian fusion restaurant in West End, Brisbane. The owners are Taiwanese and the menu features some Taiwanese classic dishes, with some dishes from other Asian countries including Japanese inari and Korean bibimbap.

‍

Most of the dishes are vegan and are clearly marked. Food is good value with generous portions. There are a few dishes that I love here, including the bean sauce on noodles (be sure to add an extra scoop), beancurd wallet with veggies (served in a sizzling plate), and the sweet & sour pom pom mushroom rice.

‍

For small dish, go for the suji (Taiwanese fried chicken) or the salt and pepper konjac ring. And I love the sweet red bean soup as dessert.

‍

The service is always warm and welcoming. With its central location in West End, I'd highly recommend Vegeme if you are craving some Asian comfort food.

gallery.alt: Sweet and sour pom pom mushroom rice
Beancurd wallet with veggies served on a sizzling plate

fieldData.name: Vegeme

fieldData.meta-description: An Instagrammable cafe in Bowen Hills serving comforting cafe food and desserts
fieldData.description:
Plant Vibes is a beautiful vegan cafe in Bowen Hills. You'll be welcomed by the friendly staff and cozy decor when you arrive. The menu features classic cafe dishes like toasties and pancakes. They update their menu every few months.

‍

On weekends, they often have special cabinet dessert items like injected croissants or coffee in doughnut.

gallery.alt: Creamy ginger cap and long black

fieldData.name: Plant Vibes

fieldData.meta-description: A cute cafe in Fortitude Valley serving unique vegan dishes like macarons and croffle
fieldData.description:
When you first walk in Little Digs, you will be greeted with the funky colourful decor.

‍

Not only do they serve some delicious classic cafe food, they offer some innovative dishes that are hard to find elsewhere. One good example is their croffle, which is a croissant pressed into a waffle. The result is a flaky, buttery waffle that is super delicious. Other dishes like vegan macarons and Shibuya toast are also special and creative.

‍

Their other, more classic choices, like burgers and burritos are also well-made and beautifully presented. The portions are generous here. If you are in Brisbane, I'd highly recommend visiting Little Digs.
fieldData.name: Little Digs

fieldData.meta-description: Dicki's is a plant-based cafe in New Farm, Brisbane
fieldData.description:
Dicki’s is a 100% vegan cafe located in New Farm. The vibe is relaxing and the food is consistently high quality.

‍

On the menu, you'll find comfort food options like the kimchi schnitzel burger, 'build-your-own-bao' plate and the breakfast burrito. I especially love their breakfast burrito which is loaded with scrambled tofu, vegan sausage, hash brown and more. They also have a specials menu which includes seasonal fluffy waffle and other dishes like mushroom arancini and satay duck wrap when I visited.

gallery.alt: Sticky duck build your own baos, breakfast burrito and iced mocha with ice cream

fieldData.name: Dicki's New Farm

fieldData.address-text: 473 S Pine Rd, Everton Park QLD 4053
fieldData.meta-description: Vegan bakery in Everton Park selling sweet and savoury goods like cupcakes, brownies and pies
fieldData.description:
Veganyumm is an all-vegan bakery in Everton Park with amazing baked goods. You will find a wide selection of sweet and savoury baked goods. One of their famous creations is the colourful galaxy brownie - blue, yellow, pink icing on top of a chocolate brownie. It's super rich and delicious. If you don't feel like a brownie, they also have tons of other options including the amazing cupcakes.

They also have drinks: Shakes (the Snickers one is great) and coffee.

For those who don't feel like sweet that day, they also have delicious savoury options like sausage roll, shepherd pie and more.
fieldData.name: Veganyumm
